231.text: This matches the term's established religious-zeal sense elsewhere in Paul (Rom 12:8; 2Cor 8:7); no divergence.

232.text: Innocence is the terminal state that grief, earnestness, indignation, fear, longing, zeal, and punishment-readiness together, sharing the same party, produce and prove.

390.text: Knew is not the verse's operation word itself but the ground cited within the master's directed answering-operation toward the servant.

391.text: Knew grounds the master's charge, tightly linking to wicked (M58) and slothful (M67) as the basis of the accusation against the same servant, delivered via answering (M41).

587.text: Unlike argos (bare state of non-work) or atakteō (disorderly neglect of duty), okneros roots idleness specifically in fear/timidity -- a shrinking-back disposition opposed to boldness (tolmeros), giving it a distinct psychological color within the cluster.

600.text: G3636 shares with G0812 the sense of dereliction toward an entrusted obligation, but oknēros is attested as an adjective describing persons or things (servant, or a task being 'no trouble'), whereas atakteō is a verb naming an act/state of the subject ('we were not idle'). This grammatical difference means atakteō frames dereliction as something one does or fails to do, while oknēros frames it as a quality one has or lacks -- a real cross-strong distinction in how the shared characteristic is grammatically instantiated.

602.text: Across its three occurrences G3636 shows a semantic range not shared by G0812 at all: in Phil.3.1 it shifts from a moral character-flaw sense (timid/lazy person, as in Matt.25.26 and Rom.12.11) to a neutral sense of 'burdensome/tedious' describing an act (writing), a range extension into describing tasks/things rather than persons that G0812 (always verbal, always describing the subject's own disorderly conduct) never exhibits.

608.text: G4710 is exclusively nominal across all twelve of its occurrences (N-ASF, N-GSF, N-DSF forms), meaning the subgroup's noun-member consistently names diligence/zeal/haste as a possessable, giveable, or measurable quality (something one 'shows', 'has produced in you', 'puts into a heart', or is measured 'by') -- structurally opposite to G4709's pure manner-of-action adverbial function. This is the clearest grammatical-role divergence between the two subgroup members: G4710 names the THING, G4709 describes the HOW.

609.text: G4710's occurrence list shows a wider register-range than G4709's: it covers pure physical haste with no moral overtone (Mark 6:25, Herodias's daughter rushing to the king with a grim request; Luke 1:39, Mary's journey), alongside heavily moralized/evidentiary senses in the Pauline corpus (2Cor 7:11-12, 8:7-8; used as proof of sincerity of repentance or love) and paired-virtue senses (Rom 12:8, 12:11; Heb 6:11; 2Pet 1:5, chained with faith/virtue/knowledge). G4709's three occurrences, by contrast, are uniformly positive/earnest in register (pleading, searching, doing one's best) with no neutral-or-negative-context instance comparable to Mark 6:25's use for a request tied to John the Baptist's beheading -- showing G4710 tolerates a broader range of surrounding moral valence than G4709 does within this subgroup.

716.text: Neither member strong's occurrences show the characteristic revealing a perception, belief, or judgement the person holds -- G0812 (2Thess.3.7) is Paul's self-report of past conduct as example, and G3636's occurrences (Matt.25.26, Rom.12.11, Phil.3.1) describe a disposition or quality censured, exhorted against, or disclaimed rather than a conclusion the idle/slothful person reaches. Record none.

717.text: The evidence does not show the characteristic clearly preceding or following a judgement/belief in any occurrence -- in Matt.25.26 the master's judgement ('you knew...') follows the naming of the servant as slothful, suggesting the characteristic is named then judged, but this is a single data point and the other occurrences (2Thess.3.7, Rom.12.11, Phil.3.1) show no judgement-sequence at all. Further analysis with adjacent context would be needed to resolve a consistent pattern.

718.text: No orientation toward a future fullness is shown by either member strong; both name a failure or absence (idleness, sloth) rather than a movement toward maturity or completion. Record none.

719.text: The subgroup's evidence does not establish what 'immediate response' the characteristic produces in the person exhibiting it or others around them -- 2Thess.3.7 and Matt.25.26/Rom.12.11/Phil.3.1 name the disposition/act itself but the verses supplied do not narrate a response following it. Adjacent verses (e.g. the servant's punishment narrative in Matt.25.27-30, or the community's reception of Paul's example in 2Thess.3.8-10) would be needed to establish whether an immediate response is consistent or varied.

720.text: Sustained effect cannot be distinguished from immediate response within this subgroup's own evidence; the occurrences state the characteristic (idleness/sloth) as a fact or charge without narrating either an immediate or ongoing consequence. Adjacent context (e.g. Matt.25.28-30's judgement outcome for the slothful servant) would be needed to compare immediate versus sustained effect.

722.text: Matt.25.26 presents the servant's slothfulness as a settled, judged character trait at the point of reckoning, offering no indication of reversibility within the verse itself; whether this is meant as irreversible (final judgement) requires the wider parable context.

723.text: The mechanism does differ across contexts: G0812 in 2Thess.3.7 operates through self-disciplined labor/example (a corporate, social-order mechanism rooted in military 'breaking rank' imagery), while G3636 operates through inner fear-driven hesitation (a psychological mechanism, per LSJ's 'shrinking, timid... especially from fear' sense) that manifests as failure to act on an entrusted task (Matt.25.26) or is negated as an exhortation to fervency (Rom.12.11).

724.text: The characteristic's role reads as belonging to the fallen condition rather than created design: both G0812 (Paul disclaiming idleness as a moral failure to avoid) and G3636 (censured in the wicked servant, warned against in Rom.12.11) are consistently treated as departures from an expected standard of diligent service, never as part of humanity's original constitution.

726.text: In Matt.25.26 slothfulness is presented as a settled character trait named at judgement ('you wicked and slothful servant'), with no accompanying emotion-language, though the LSJ root sense implies fear/timidity as the felt cause of the disposition. In Rom.12.11 it is addressed as a disposition to be avoided ('do not be slothful in zeal'), again without explicit emotion-language but implicitly contrasted with fervency of spirit.

727.text: The felt quality is consistent as a settled disposition/character trait across both members and all occurrences (self-descriptive discipline in G0812; censured or warned-against character trait in G3636), varying only in whether it is disclaimed (2Thess.3.7), condemned (Matt.25.26), or exhorted against (Rom.12.11) -- the underlying quality itself (a lasting orientation, not a momentary lapse) does not vary.

728.text: The mode of operation varies by grammatical/contextual level: G0812 operates verbally as an act/state of the subject describing a completed pattern of past conduct (military-order-derived, corporate/social dimension); G3636 operates adjectivally, applied to persons as a character-quality (Matt.25.26, Rom.12.11) or, distinctly, to a task/act as its resulting quality ('no trouble', Phil.3.1) -- a further contextual variation not shared by G0812.

729.text: G3636 operates through a communicative/speech-based mode in Matt.25.26, where the master directly addresses the servant with an accusatory epithet ('You wicked and slothful servant!') as part of a judgement speech. Rom.12.11 operates through a direct imperative address ('Do not be slothful'). G0812 in 2Thess.3.7 is not itself a commanded/addressed speech-act but a self-reported past pattern offered as example.

732.text: The person in whom slothfulness is present but not overcome (Matt.25.26's servant) is shown as fear-driven at root (per LSJ's root sense) yet is directly charged by the master with knowing his obligation and failing to act on it -- an inner-being state of culpable, self-aware neglect rather than ignorance.

733.text: The characteristic operates within an existing relational bond of entrusted obligation in both instances with clear direction: G0812 within the bond between Paul's team and the Thessalonian believers they served (2Thess.3.7); G3636 within the bond between a master and his servant to whom talents were entrusted (Matt.25.26). Both show the characteristic assessed specifically in light of a prior relational commitment, not across relational distance.

734.text: The characteristic operates within covenantal/entrusted contexts specifically: G0812 within the apostolic-community relationship of mutual obligation, G3636 within the master-servant relationship of entrusted stewardship (Matt.25.26) and the believer's obligation of service to the Lord (Rom.12.11) -- in each case a relationship carrying an expected standard, not crossing into contexts lacking such an entrusted bond.

735.text: The relational scope includes those bound by an entrusted obligation to another party -- an apostle to a congregation (G0812), a servant to a master (G3636/Matt.25.26), a believer to the Lord (G3636/Rom.12.11). It excludes relationships with no standing obligation or commission; the characteristic is not shown applied to strangers or to those without an entrusted role.

739.text: As a negative/absence characteristic (dereliction), it does not itself instantiate an aspect of divine likeness; rather its absence highlights the aspect of the divine likeness it violates -- namely faithful, diligent stewardship reflecting God's own faithfulness. Record: no positive aspect instantiated; it names the failure of an aspect (faithful service) rather than the aspect itself.

740.text: As a term for failure/dereliction, this characteristic is an exclusively creaturely deficiency -- it has no corresponding reality in God, who is never described as idle, slothful, or negligent of obligation in Scripture; it names a lack that only a creature bound by entrusted duty can exhibit.

741.text: Where the characteristic is present (the slothful servant, Matt.25.26), it indicates a marring of the divine image's call to faithful stewardship -- the servant fails to reflect the diligent, productive character expected of one entrusted with the master's goods. Where it is absent (Paul's team, 2Thess.3.7, disclaiming idleness), the divine image's stewardship aspect is upheld as a positive example.

742.text: The pattern shows the characteristic engaging primarily at the level of will/behavior (the acting/laboring person, G0812) and disposition/inner orientation rooted in fear or reluctance (G3636's oknos root) -- it engages the soul-level orientation toward action but shows no explicit body link (no somatic/physical vocabulary) and no explicit spirit-level engagement in these occurrences; the depth is behavioral-dispositional rather than body-mediated.

743.text: No body link exists in this subgroup's evidence -- neither G0812 nor G3636 employ physical/bodily vocabulary; the characteristic is expressed through labor/conduct (G0812) or character-attribution/disposition (G3636) without reference to bodily mediation. Record none.

744.text: No movement across constitutional levels or from an external spirit source is shown; the characteristic in both members is presented as a settled quality or pattern of the person's own conduct/disposition (G0812's self-reported past labor pattern; G3636's servant/persons characterized by fear-rooted reluctance), not as something imposed or transmitted from outside. Record none of the sort described.

745.text: This subgroup's evidence does not show God extending the characteristic itself (dereliction is never something God gives); rather God's relation to it is as the one who assesses/judges its absence or presence (Matt.25.26's master figure) or as the object of the diligent service that should replace it (Rom.12.11's 'serve the Lord'). No direct extension pattern applies.

746.text: God's disposition toward dereliction of duty, as shown in Matt.25.26, is one of direct confrontation and censure ('you wicked and slothful servant') -- indicating God does not tolerate neglected stewardship but holds the entrusted person accountable to the standard expected.

750.text: The servant who receives an entrusted task from his master but fails to act on it (Matt.25.26) is in an inner-being state of fear-rooted timidity and self-aware neglect -- he 'knew' the master's expectation yet did not take it up, indicating a culpable rather than ignorant failure to receive and act on what was entrusted.

751.text: The subgroup's evidence shows no explicit adversarial-spirit activity behind dereliction of duty; both occurrences attribute the failure to the human person's own disposition (fear-rooted timidity, or simple non-labor) rather than to external spiritual instigation. No pattern of adversarial site is evidenced.

753.text: The origin is consistently the human person's own will/disposition across all occurrences -- G0812 originates in Paul's team's own chosen self-discipline (negated: they chose not to be idle); G3636 originates in the servant's own fear-rooted character (Matt.25.26) or is warned against as a self-originating temptation for believers (Rom.12.11). The origin does not change with context; it remains internal to the person in every case.

754.text: The pattern shows engagement with the will/volitional faculty (choosing to labor or not, G0812) and the affective/dispositional faculty rooted in fear (G3636's oknos root), but no engagement with the cognitive/perceptual faculties beyond the accusatory 'you knew' in Matt.25.26 -- indicating the characteristic's nature is primarily volitional-dispositional rather than perceptual or intellectual.

756.text: G3636 names a disposition/quality (an adjective describing a settled character trait, 'slothful') applied to a person (Matt.25.26, Rom.12.11) or, distinctly, to a task's resulting quality (Phil.3.1, 'no trouble').

757.text: Both are simple in structure, not compound -- neither term combines multiple distinct constituent elements; each names a single unified failure/quality (disorder/dereliction for G0812; fear-rooted reluctance/sluggishness for G3636).

759.text: The characteristic excludes/resists diligent, orderly labor and confident, bold engagement with an entrusted task -- it is defined precisely against faithful stewardship and zealous service.

760.text: The characteristic ends where mere passivity without relational obligation begins (it is not simple rest or inactivity in a neutral sense) -- it is distinctly a failure measured against an entrusted duty or standard of conduct, not idleness in a morally neutral context; it also is not fear itself but the behavioral outworking of fear-rooted reluctance (G3636's root) or of chosen disorder (G0812's root).

761.text: G3636 co-occurs with 'wicked' (ponēros, M58) in Matt.25.26 as a paired accusation, and with 'fervent in spirit'/'serve the Lord' (M69/M78, zeal-related) in Rom.12.11 as its positive contrast within the same verse. G0812 co-occurs with no other M-code in 2Thess.3.7 (sole M-code in that verse).

762.text: The co-occurrence pattern shows this characteristic sits at a junction point in the inner-being landscape between moral character-judgement (paired with 'wicked') and the positive pole of zealous service (paired with fervency/service) -- it functions as the negative hinge that either compounds with wickedness in condemnation or is directly negated to make room for zealous devotion.

763.text: In Matt.25.26 the naming of slothfulness precedes and grounds the master's judgement-speech ('you knew...'); in Rom.12.11 the prohibition of slothfulness precedes the positive commands to be fervent in spirit and serve the Lord. In both, the characteristic (or its negation) functions as a preceding condition for what follows.

764.text: The sequence shown is developmental/hortatory rather than strictly causal: the naming or negation of the characteristic sets the stage for a subsequent moral or relational outcome (judgement in Matt.25.26; positive exhortation in Rom.12.11), functioning as a precondition to be cleared or corrected rather than a mechanical cause producing a fixed effect.

765.text: This characteristic produces condemnation/judgement in Matt.25.26 (the master's rebuke and subsequent punishment follows directly from the naming of the servant as slothful) by the mechanism of exposing an unmet entrusted obligation. It does not itself produce a further positive characteristic; its removal (negation) is instead what allows fervency and service to be enacted (Rom.12.11).

766.text: This characteristic is produced by fear/timidity at root (G3636's oknos derivation, 'shrinking, timid... especially from fear') or by a chosen disorderly departure from expected conduct (G0812's atakteō root, breaking rank) -- fear and willful disorder are its respective producing sources across the two members.

767.text: Neither member strong is shown to be a constituent element of another characteristic, nor to contain another as its own constituent, within this subgroup's evidence; each stands as a distinct, non-compound characteristic (per M0.2.2).

768.text: Within the subgroup, G0812 and G3636 most closely resemble each other, both naming dereliction of an entrusted obligation; they are distinguished precisely as already established in char_reading: G0812 is a verbal act naming chosen disorderly conduct (military-order root), while G3636 is an adjectival disposition/quality rooted in fear-driven shrinking-back, and can also describe a task's burdensome quality (Phil.3.1) rather than only a person's character.

769.text: The precise boundary: G0812 names the act/pattern of behaving in a disorderly, non-laboring way (a verb of conduct); G3636 names the underlying disposition or resultant quality (an adjective of character or of a task) that may motivate or accompany such conduct but is not itself the conduct -- the overlap is in outcome (neglected duty) while the boundary is act versus quality/disposition.

770.text: The distinction between G0812 and G3636 is one of kind (act versus disposition/quality) rather than degree, direction, or constitutional level -- both operate at the same behavioral/relational level toward an entrusted obligation, but differ in what kind of inner-being reality (verbal act vs. adjectival state) each names.

772.text: Both patterns occur. In 2Cor 7:11-12 and 8:7-8, earnestness FOLLOWS a prior belief/experience (godly grief, or Paul's estimation of the Corinthians) and becomes evidence for a further judgement about character. In Luke 7:4 earnestness accompanies a plea that itself is grounded in a preceding judgement ('he is worthy'). No verse shows earnestness itself producing a subsequent belief with no antecedent -- it functions consistently as accompanying or evidencing judgement rather than generating one from nothing.

780.text: In 2Cor 7:11, earnestness is one of a cluster of vividly named emotional responses (fear, longing, indignation) produced by godly grief -- here it functions as a felt, almost visceral moral urgency accompanying repentance, closer to transient intensified emotion than a fixed disposition, though it is offered as evidence of settled character change.

815.text: The characteristic co-occurs frequently with: fervency of spirit and service (Rom 12:11); faith, speech, knowledge, and love (2Cor 8:7); grief, fear, longing, indignation (2Cor 7:11); love proven genuine (2Cor 8:8); virtue and knowledge in a growth-chain (2Pet 1:5); hope (Heb 6:11); and care/heart (2Cor 8:16). It clusters especially with love, faith, and hope as an accompanying, evidencing quality.

817.text: In 2Cor 7:11 earnestness heads a sequence of responses produced by godly grief (grief precedes and produces earnestness, which is followed by further responses like indignation and fear); in 2Pet 1:5 effort/diligence precedes and initiates the addition of virtue to faith, beginning a developmental chain. The characteristic thus can both follow an antecedent cause (grief) and precede a subsequent development (virtue-chain).

818.text: Both causal and developmental relationships are shown: godly grief causally produces earnestness (2Cor 7:11), and earnestness/effort developmentally initiates a sequential chain of virtue-building (2Pet 1:5) -- the sequence is not merely correlational but shows genuine cause-then-effect and effort-then-growth structuring.

820.text: Yes, this characteristic is produced by godly grief, as shown explicitly in 2Cor 7:11 ('see what earnestness this godly grief has produced in you').

821.text: The characteristic functions as a constituent element within larger virtue-lists or evidence-catalogues (2Cor 7:11's list of grief's fruits; 2Cor 8:7's list of Corinthian excellences) rather than being itself composed of other named characteristics as constituents -- it is a component contributing to a whole (proof of genuine repentance/love) rather than a compound built from other cluster members.

1000.text: In Ps.99.3 H3034 is used in its standard Hiphil sense 'let them praise', squarely within the base gloss with no divergent nuance.

1001.text: This is the first pass over this verse. H3034 (praise) co-occurs with M01 (awesome, H3372H) and M13/M61 (Holy, H6918G): praise here is the human response summoned by the fearsome and holy character of God's name — the thanksgiving-praise cluster functions as the vocal/liturgical outworking triggered by the awe/holiness characteristics present.

1109.text: In Ps.138.2 'give thanks' sits squarely within the base Hiphil liturgical gloss with no distinguishing nuance -- straightforward thanksgiving toward God's name.

1110.text: In Dan.9.20 the surface sense shifts from the base gloss 'give thanks/praise' to the Hithpael sense 'confessing' (sin), the penitential branch of the root rather than the celebratory branch predominant elsewhere in this batch (e.g. 1Chr.16.4, 1Chr.29.13). The impact here is that the same verb carries confession-of-guilt force rather than praise, compared against its overwhelmingly praise-directed use in the Chronicles verses of this batch.

1111.text: In 2Chr.30.22, 1Chr.16.4, 1Chr.23.30, 1Chr.25.3, 1Chr.29.13, 2Chr.5.13, 2Chr.7.6, and 2Chr.20.21 the term functions in its standard liturgical thanksgiving sense with no divergence from the base gloss.

1112.text: In Ps.138.2, thanksgiving (H3034) is directed at the divine name and stands alongside steadfast love (M07/M50, H2617A), faithfulness (M13, H0571G), and exaltation (M22, H1431) -- thanksgiving here is the responsive verbal act that answers and publicly announces those other divine attributes; it is the vehicle by which love/faithfulness/exaltation become spoken acknowledgment.

1114.text: In Dan.9.20, confession (H3034, penitential sense) is paired tightly with prayer/plea (M42, H6419/H8467) and sin (M56, H2403B) -- here thanksgiving's confessional branch functions not as praise but as the verbal admission accompanying supplication, distinguishing this occurrence from the praise-cluster co-occurrences seen elsewhere in the batch.

1121.text: In 2Chr.20.21, thanksgiving (H3034) co-occurs with counsel (M63, H3289), singing (M22), holiness (M61, H6944G), and steadfast love (M07/M50) in a martial-liturgical setting -- thanksgiving here precedes and accompanies the army's advance, functioning as a vocalised expression of trust that goes before military action rather than in a temple setting.

1122.text: In Ps.138.2 the psalmist (first person) initiates the thanksgiving-operation directed toward 'your name' (the Lord), a first-person-to-divine-second-person direction.

1124.text: In Dan.9.20 Daniel (first person, 'I') initiates the confessing-operation directed toward the Lord his God, alongside speaking and praying.

1131.text: In 2Chr.20.21 those appointed to sing (party, appointed by Jehoshaphat) initiate the thanksgiving-operation ('Give thanks') directed toward the Lord, going before the army.

1281.text: Building on the prior finding (praise as response to awe/holiness): from praise's own vantage point, the verb itself supplies the missing verbal enactment the awesome/holy name calls for — M01 and M13/M61 name the divine attributes that make the name praiseworthy, while H3034 supplies the community's required liturgical action, closing the loop between attribute and response.

1282.text: H3034 ('let them praise') is the role-T3-tagged operation in this verse; it is initiated by the implied worshipping community ('them') and directed toward God, whose great, awesome, and holy name/person is the object of the praise-act.

1346.text: In Ps.138.2 the Hiphil form sits squarely within the standard 'give thanks' sense (1c1), directed at the divine name alongside love/faithfulness -- no notable divergence from the base gloss.

1347.text: In Dan.9.20 the form is Hithpael, aligning with sense 1d1 'to confess (sin)' rather than the more common Hiphil praise sense -- here the nuance shifts from acclamation to penitential self-admission, paired with prayer and sin-language; this contrasts sharply with the praise-oriented occurrences in Chronicles/Psalms in this same batch.

1355.text: In 2Chr.20.21 the imperative 'Give thanks' matches the base Hiphil sense exactly, here issued as a military marching command -- no lexical divergence, only unusual (martial) setting.

1356.text: Building on the prior finding that thanksgiving answers love/faithfulness/exaltation: from thanksgiving's own vantage, it is the SOLE verbal-response mechanism in the verse that converts three separate divine attributes (steadfast love M07/M50, faithfulness M13, exaltation M22) into one unified act of acknowledgment -- without H3034 these attributes would remain unspoken states; thanksgiving supplies the only verb of address directed at the divine name itself.

1358.text: Building on the prior finding that confession here functions penitentially alongside prayer and sin: from confession's own vantage, it is the operative link binding sin (M56) to prayer/plea (M42) -- confession names what prayer is FOR, converting M42's general 'seeking' into a specific penitential seeking, since without confession the plea would lack its stated object (the sin admitted).

1365.text: Building on the prior finding of thanksgiving preceding the army's advance: from thanksgiving's own vantage, it is the final, climactic verb in a chain that begins with counsel (M63) and singing (M22) -- thanksgiving supplies the actual spoken content ('his steadfast love endures forever') that the counsel decided should be voiced and the singing was to carry, making it the terminus of the other M-codes' preparatory action.

1366.text: H3034 ('give thanks,' HVhu1cs) is the operation-tagged verb of thanksgiving-relevance in this verse, though role-T3 is not itself marked on H3034 here; the clear role-T3 operation is H7812 'bow down' -- initiated by the psalmist (first person) and directed toward God's holy temple, establishing the posture that the following thanksgiving-act (H3034) then verbally performs toward God's name.

1368.text: Role-T3 operation is 'speaking' (H1696G, M42/T3), initiated by Daniel (first person 'I') and directed toward the Lord his God, with confessing (H3034) naming the specific content of that directed speech-operation.

1375.text: Role-T3 operations 'appointed' (H5975H) and 'went' (H3318G) are initiated by the unnamed leader (Jehoshaphat, per context) directed toward the singers/people, who then march before the army; the imperative thanksgiving (H3034) is the content the appointed singers are commanded to voice toward the Lord.

1394.text: In Ps.111.1 the first-person cohortative expresses standard personal vow of thanksgiving 'with my whole heart' -- no divergence from base gloss beyond the wholehearted qualifier attaching to 'heart', not to the verb itself.

1419.text: M08/M16/M22 (praise), M47 (heart), M16 (company/council) appear together; H3034 anchors the whole-hearted (M47) vow of thanksgiving performed within the gathered upright company (M16), each M-code contributing a distinct dimension (manner, location, disposition) to the single act H3034 names.

1676.text: In Ps.99.3 the occurrence sits squarely within the Hiphil 'praise' sense, summoned by God's awesome and holy name; no notable divergence from base gloss.

1679.text: Building on the prior finding (praise as the required verbal enactment triggered by God's awesome/holy name): from praise's own vantage point, H3034 completes the sequence begun by M01 (awesome) and M13/M61 (Holy) by supplying the community's obligatory vocal response, making praise functionally dependent on those preceding attribute-terms.

1682.text: H3034 in Ps.99.3 is itself the home strong but is not tagged role-T3 (Operation) in the role list; it carries the M49 cluster tag only, so no D7.7.1 relation applies from this strong's own tagging.

1730.text: In Ps.138.2 the Hiphil 'give thanks' sits squarely within the base gloss of praising/thanking the divine name; no notable surface divergence from the general stepGloss is present here.

1731.text: In Dan.9.20 the Hithpael form carries the penitential 'confessing (sin)' sense rather than the more common Hiphil praise/thanks sense -- this occurrence's nuance shifts the term toward self-accusatory admission, distinct impact from the doxological uses seen in the Chronicles/Psalms occurrences in this batch, where the same root instead announces praise.

1740.text: Building on the prior chain: thanksgiving's role as sole verbal-response converting love/faithfulness/exaltation into acknowledgment is reinforced by noting the temple/name-word cluster (T2 tags) surrounding it -- thanksgiving is the one act among all attributes present that actually crosses from named divine quality into spoken human response toward the temple/name.

1742.text: Building on the prior finding that confession binds sin (M56) to prayer (M42): from this vantage, confession is also grammatically the middle verb of a three-verb sequence (speaking-praying-confessing), marking it as the term that gives the whole clause its specific penitential character rather than leaving it general devotional speech.

1749.text: Building on the prior finding of thanksgiving as the terminus of a counsel-then-singing chain: this vantage adds that thanksgiving here directly quotes the same fixed formula seen in 2Chr.5.13/7.6 ('his steadfast love endures forever'), showing this specific verbal content recurs across cultic and martial settings alike as the fixed liturgical content thanksgiving always supplies.

1750.text: H3034 ('give thanks') itself is the T2-tagged act (not role-T3 operation) in Ps.138.2; the only role-T3 operation word present is H7812 'bow down', initiated by the psalmist and directed toward the holy temple -- no role-T3 tag attaches to H3034 here, so D7.7.1 targets the bowing rather than the thanking.

1752.text: In Dan.9.20 H3034 ('confessing') carries only M49, not role-T3; the role-T3 operations present (speaking, presenting) are initiated by Daniel and directed before the Lord his God -- H3034 itself is not tagged as the operation word here.

1759.text: In 2Chr.20.21 H3034 ('thanks') carries only M49, not role-T3; role-T3 operations present (appointed, praise, went, army, say) are initiated by the king/people and directed toward the Lord and before the army -- H3034 itself is not tagged as the operation word.

1792.text: In Ps.111.1 'give thanks with whole heart' emphasizes wholehearted disposition but remains within the base sense of the verb; the intensifying phrase is carried by 'heart' not by H3034 itself.

1800.text: No role-T3 tag on H3034 in Ps.44.8; no operation-word relation recorded for this verse.

1809.text: Building on the prior finding that M47 (heart), M16 (company) each supply manner/location dimensions: from H3034's own vantage, it is the single named act that these dimensions modify, confirming H3034 as the grammatical and conceptual head of the verse's worship description.

2042.text: In 1Chr 16:35, yadah co-occurs with M45 (salvation/deliverance - 'save', 'deliver'), M79 (salvation), M61 (holy), M22/M33 (glory), M22 (praise, H8416). Yadah's own contribution is to be the concluding verbal act that the plea for deliverance culminates in: thanksgiving is the response called for once salvation (M45/M79) is granted, distinct from the naming of God's holiness (M61) or the request for glory (M22/M33) which frame what is being thanked for.

2045.text: In 1Chr 16:35 the operation-words 'gather' (H6908) and 'save'/'deliver' (H3467/H5337, non-home) are initiated by God toward the worshiping party; yadah is the worshipers' own reciprocal operation, directed back toward God's holy name, forming a two-directional relation (God delivers -> people give thanks).

2061.text: In 2Chr 29:31 and 2Chr 33:16 'thank offerings'/'thanksgiving' sit squarely within todah's cultic-sacrificial base gloss with no notable shift.

2063.text: In 2Chr 29:31, todah (thank offerings) co-occurs with M22 (glory-related 'said'), M23/M72 (consecrated), M44 (assembly), M09/M34 (willing), M47 (heart), M36 (burnt offerings). Todah's own contribution: it names the specific sacrificial category the consecrated assembly brings, standing alongside but distinct from the burnt offerings (M36) which serve full dedication rather than gratitude.

2066.text: In 2Chr 29:31 the operation-words 'bring'/'brought' (H0935P, role-T3) are initiated by Hezekiah's assembly, directed toward the house of the Lord, carrying todah offerings as the object of the action.

2213.text: 'thanks/thank' in Ps.7.17 and Ps.52.9 sit within the standard Hiphil sense of giving thanks to the Lord for his righteousness/goodness -- no notable divergence from the base gloss.

2220.text: In Ps.7.17, giving thanks (H3034) is explicitly grounded in God's righteousness (M12, H6664G) and paired with singing praise (M22) to God's Most High name (M08) -- thanksgiving here is the vocal acknowledgment specifically of divine righteousness, distinct from the covenant-love grounding seen in 1Chr.16.41.

2223.text: In Ps.52.9, thanking God (H3034) is paired with waiting/hoping (M16/M68, H6960A) for his name and the presence of the godly (M05, H2623) -- thanksgiving here anchors present gratitude while hope (waiting) anchors future expectation, godliness (M05) providing the communal context in which both are exercised.

2269.text: In Ps.106.47 the infinitive construct sits within its standard sense of giving thanks to God's holy name after deliverance/gathering; no divergence from base gloss.

2271.text: In Ps.140.13 the imperfect 'shall give thanks' describes the righteous's future/habitual acknowledgment of God's name; standard sense, no divergence.

2272.text: In Ps.142.7 the infinitive construct 'give thanks to' following deliverance from prison matches the base gloss of thanksgiving for rescue; no divergence.

2293.text: H3034 in Ps.106.47 is tagged only M49, not role-T3; the verse's role-T3 word is H6908 ('gather'), directed by the Lord toward the worshippers from among the nations -- not H3034's own operation tag.

2295.text: H3034 in Ps.140.13 carries only M49; the verse's role-T3 words are H3477G ('upright', qualifying) and H3427 ('dwell'), not H3034 itself.

2296.text: H3034 in Ps.142.7 carries only M49; the verse's role-T3 words (H3318H 'Bring', H3803 'surround', H1580 'deal bountifully') are separate strongs -- 'Bring me out' is God's operation directed toward the psalmist, but not H3034's own tag.

2304.text: H3034 co-occurs with M45 (save), M61 (holy), M22/M33 (glory, praise). First pass: thanksgiving here is the intended outcome of the sought salvation (M45) and is directed toward God's holy (M61) name, with glorying (M22/M33) as its accompanying expression -- thanksgiving is thus the responsive, dependent characteristic following divine deliverance.

2306.text: H3034 co-occurs with M12 (righteous/upright, twice). First pass: thanksgiving is presented as the characteristic act performed BY the righteous/upright (M12), linking this cluster's act of thanks to moral character as its precondition or fitting expression.

2307.text: H3034 co-occurs with M47 (soul/self, 'me') and M12 (righteous). First pass: the psalmist's own selfhood (M47) is the site from which thanksgiving arises upon deliverance, while the righteous (M12) are the community that will gather around him -- thanksgiving here bridges personal rescue and communal righteousness.

2431.text: In Ps.30.4 'give thanks' sits squarely within the Hiphil base gloss of H3034 (give thanks, laud, praise) with no notable contextual divergence.

2432.text: In Ps.97.12 'give thanks' matches the standard Hiphil imperative sense of H3034 without special nuance.

2437.text: In Ps.30.4 H3034 (give thanks) co-occurs with M05 (saints/holy) and M61 (holy name); thanksgiving here is directed specifically at the divine holiness named in the verse, functioning as the worshipper's response to that holiness.

2438.text: In Ps.97.12 H3034 co-occurs with M04 (rejoice) and M12 (righteous) and M61 (holy name); thanksgiving stands as the verbal counterpart to the emotional rejoicing and moral righteousness of the addressees, all converging on God's holy name.

2605.text: Praise (H3034) here co-occurs with M12 (righteous/rules, on H6664G/H4941G): the rising to give thanks at midnight is explicitly motivated by and directed toward God's righteous rules, making the thanksgiving-act a direct response to the other characteristic's content rather than an independent occurrence.

2614.text: The role list tags H6965B (rise) as role-T3 operation, initiated by the speaker ('I') and directed toward the act of praising God at midnight; H3034 (praise) itself carries M49 in this verse, naming the goal of the rising rather than being itself T3-tagged.

2755.text: Here yadah is used in its standard Hiphil sense 'I will praise you,' matching the base gloss with no notable shift.

2756.text: Other M-codes present are M12 (righteous/upright, twice) and M47 (heart); praise here is conditioned by an upright heart and directed toward learning righteous rules, so praise functions as the response-term while M12/M47 supply the moral-inward qualifiers it responds from -- a supportive but distinct relation, not identity.

2757.text: The operation word (role-T3) is H3925H 'learn,' initiated by the psalmist ('I') directed toward God's righteous rules as object; praise (H3034) is likewise the psalmist's own initiated act directed toward 'you' (God), the two operations run in parallel from the same initiating party.

2764.text: In Ps.118.19 'give thanks' functions in its standard Hiphil sense, directed to the Lord upon entering the gates of righteousness; matches base gloss with no notable shift.

2765.text: Other M-code present is M12 (righteousness, H6664G); the gates are described as gates 'of righteousness,' through which the psalmist enters in order to give thanks -- righteousness here characterizes the access-point/setting while thanksgiving is the resulting act performed within it, a sequential rather than identical relation.

2766.text: Operation words (role-T3) are H6605A 'Open' (imperative, addressed presumably to gatekeepers/God, directed toward the gates) and H0935G 'enter' (initiated by the psalmist 'I', directed into the gates); give thanks (H3034) is the psalmist's further self-initiated act performed to the Lord once entry is granted.

2972.text: Across its full occurrence list H8426 clusters into three recurring realizations of one lexeme: (1) the concrete thank-offering sacrifice (Lev.7.12 x2, Lev.7.13, Lev.7.15, Lev.22.29, Ps.50.14, Ps.50.23, Ps.107.22, Ps.116.17, Amos.4.5, Jonah.2.9, 2Chr.29.31 x2, 2Chr.33.16, Jer.17.26, Jer.33.11), (2) the vocal/manner accompaniment of praise, 'with/in thanksgiving' (Ps.69.30, Ps.26.7, Ps.95.2, Ps.100.4, Ps.147.7, Isa.51.3), and (3) the institutional thanksgiving choir/procession/company (Neh.12.27, Neh.12.31, Neh.12.38, Neh.12.40, Ps.42.4). A fourth, rarer sense realizes it as verbal confession (Josh.7.19, Ezra.10.11). This is a single strong showing internally the full sense-range attributed to the subgroup label (hymn, choir, offering) without needing a second member strong to supply any of these senses.

2973.text: Since H8426 is the sole member strong of this subgroup, there is no second lexeme to compare it against directly; the meaningful cross-comparison available is internal -- between H8426's own sacrificial/cultic-object occurrences (e.g. Lev.7.12-15, Lev.22.29, 2Chr.29.31, 2Chr.33.16, Jer.17.26, Jer.33.11, Amos.4.5) versus its choir/procession-as-institution occurrences (Neh.12.27-40, Ps.42.4) versus its purely adverbial/manner occurrences ('with thanksgiving', e.g. Ps.69.30, Ps.95.2, Ps.100.4, Ps.147.7, Ps.26.7). These three groupings do not overlap grammatically: the sacrificial sense is always the head noun or a construct-genitive qualifier of an offering-word (zebach, shelamim), the choir sense functions as a collective-body noun (subject or object of appointment/movement verbs), and the manner sense is marked by a preposition (b-) modifying a separate main verb of praise. No morphological distinction (all occurrences are the same feminine noun stem, singular or plural absolute/construct) drives this three-way split -- it is purely syntactic/contextual, meaning the noun's referent is disambiguated entirely by its syntactic role in each verse rather than by any inflectional change.

3153.text: Todah takes hold rightly under conditions of a willing heart (2Chr.29.31, 'all who were of a willing heart') and right ordering of one's way of life (Ps.50.23, 'to one who orders his way rightly'); it operates rightly when accompanied by genuine acknowledgment rather than mere ritual performance.

3160.text: The human-to-God movement of todah requires an inner posture of humility and right-ordering ('to one who orders his way rightly,' Ps.50.23), willingness ('willing heart,' 2Chr.29.31), and honest acknowledgment (confession, Josh.7.19, Ezra.10.11) rather than mere external ritual performance.

3170.text: 2Chr.29.31 shows that genuine extension of todah is accompanied by consecration ('you have now consecrated yourselves to the Lord') and a willing heart, indicating that inner conditions of dedication and voluntary devotion in the giver (here, the assembly/nation) accompany the sincere bringing of thank-offerings.

3171.text: 2Chr.29.31 shows the assembly had first to consecrate themselves before bringing thank offerings, indicating a person must have first undergone consecration/dedication to the Lord before rightly extending todah.

3182.text: Todah ends where a different sacrificial category begins: it is explicitly distinguished from the burnt offering (2Chr.29.31, 'brought sacrifices and thank offerings...brought burnt offerings') and from the peace offering more generally, being a specific sub-type marked by gratitude/acknowledgment rather than full dedication (burnt offering) or general fellowship (peace offering).

3193.text: Across this pass's occurrences the surface form 'give thanks' overwhelmingly renders the Hiphil stem in liturgical/doxological contexts (e.g. Ps.138.2, Ps.106.1, Ps.111.1, Ps.44.8, Ps.86.12, Ps.28.7, 1Chr.16.35/8/41, Ps.54.6, Ps.75.1x2, Ps.92.1, Ps.106.47, Ps.122.4, Ps.140.13, 1Chr.16.34, Ps.107.1, Ps.118.1/28/29, Ps.30.4, Ps.97.12, Ps.30.12, Ps.9.1, Ps.79.13, Ps.145.10, Ps.118.19, Ps.57.9, Ps.108.3) -- a large, internally consistent block where the verb names a vocal, addressed act of gratitude toward the Lord's name, character, or acts, with no confession-of-sin sense present in any of these.

3200.text: Across this pass's occurrences the core Hiphil imperative/perfect/participle sense 'give thanks/praise' recurs as the dominant pattern in liturgical contexts: Isa.12.1, 2Chr.30.22, 2Chr.7.6, 2Chr.20.21, 2Chr.31.2, Ezra.3.11, Neh.12.24, Ps.109.30, Isa.12.4, Jer.33.11, Ps.7.17, 1Chr.16.4, 1Chr.29.13, Ps.35.18, Ps.118.21, Ps.52.9, Ps.107.8/15/21/31, Ps.100.4, Ps.136.1/2/3/26, Ps.33.2, 2Chr.5.13, 1Chr.16.7, Neh.12.46, Ps.138.4, Ps.138.1, 2Chr.7.3, 1Chr.23.30, 1Chr.25.3, Ps.142.7, Neh.11.17 -- all render the same basic act of vocal, often corporate/musical, thanksgiving directed at the Lord, frequently anchored by the refrain 'his steadfast love endures forever.'

3203.text: Within the confession-branch occurrences themselves, a further distinction is visible by stem/subject: Lev.16.21 (Qal-tq, Aaron confessing the people's sin OVER the scapegoat) and Num.5.7/Lev.26.40/Lev.5.5 (individual or corporate confession as a required legal/cultic act tied to restitution or covenant curse) represent a ritual-legal register, whereas Dan.9.20, Neh.1.6, Ezra.10.1, Neh.9.3, Dan.9.4 represent a personal/intercessory-prayer register (confession embedded within extended penitential prayer, weeping, and prostration) -- both are 'confession' but differ in whether the act is a discrete ritual requirement or an extended devotional/intercessory posture.

3223.text: The characteristic takes hold rightly under conditions of an upright/whole heart (Ps.111.1 'with my whole heart', Ps.119.7 'with an upright heart') and of recognized, perceived benefit or deliverance already received (Ps.118.21 thanks following answered prayer) -- inner uprightness and awareness of grace received are the conditions for it operating rightly.

3231.text: The human-to-God movement requires an inner posture of humility and honesty: in the confession-branch this means not covering or concealing iniquity (Ps.32.5 'I did not cover my iniquity'), and in the praise-branch it requires wholeheartedness and uprightness (Ps.111.1, Ps.119.7) -- both branches require the person to set aside self-protective concealment or half-heartedness.

3243.text: The subgroup's own occurrences show the characteristic modeled or commanded (imperatives to 'give thanks', appointed offices) but do not directly narrate a case of one person receiving the exhortation to thanksgiving/confession FROM another and the inner conditions of their uptake or resistance; resolving this would need adjacent verses (e.g. the narrative surrounding Hezekiah's encouraging speech in 2Chr.30.22 or the congregational response to the Levites' commanded praise) to see how hearers responded internally.

3248.text: The pattern of engagement (mouth, heart, whole body in prostration) versus non-engagement (never engaging in the dead/Sheol, Ps.6.5/Isa.38.18) indicates the characteristic's nature as a fully embodied, life-dependent act requiring the coordinated engagement of inner faculties (heart's conviction) and outer faculties (voice, posture) together -- it is not a purely cognitive or purely emotional faculty-engagement but demands their union in a living person.

3260.text: The characteristic functions as a constituent element of larger worship acts (sacrifice, temple liturgy, prayer) rather than the reverse: e.g. in 2Chr.30.22 thanksgiving is one component within the larger act of a festival service including sacrifice, and in Dan.9.4/Dan.9.20 confession is one component within the larger act of intercessory prayer -- it is a part contributed to a bigger whole, not itself containing those wholes.

3263.text: The distinction from the nearest neighbour (halal/praise) is one of kind and scope rather than degree: yadah is kind-broader (covering both praise and confession of sin, two distinct moral directions) while halal is kind-narrower (exaltation/boasting only) -- not a matter of intensity but of the range of content the act can bear.

3277.text: In Ps.38.12 and 2Sam.4.8 and Prov.29.10 the surface sense diverges from the neutral base gloss 'seek' because it participates in the idiom 'seek my life/his life' -- meaning to seek to kill, not merely to search for or desire. This idiomatic shift carries lethal hostile intent, contrasting against occurrences like 1Kgs.22.8 where the same root (H1875, related seeking root) denotes benign consultation of the Lord.

3280.text: In Prov.29.10 bloodthirsty men (party) initiate the seeking-operation directed toward the life of the upright (the other party), an adversarial pursuit paralleling the Ps.38.12 pattern.

3283.text: In Prov.29.10 M06 (hate) and M34 (blameless) and M12 (upright) co-occur with the seeking; the seeking of the upright's life is the outworking of the bloodthirsty men's hatred (M06), showing seeking here as the operational expression of a prior hateful disposition rather than an independent characteristic.

3376.text: In Zeph.2.3 all three occurrences of baqash sit squarely within the base gloss 'seek' (the Lord, righteousness, humility) with no surface divergence -- straightforward imperative use.

3378.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Zeph.2.3 alongside baqash (the co-occurring M12 righteousness and M05 humility terms are the OBJECTS sought, not separate characteristics of the seeker in this verse's role tagging) -- baqash stands as the operative seeking-act relating to those pursued qualities.

3383.text: In Zeph.2.3, the seeking operation is initiated by 'the humble of the land' (addressed party) and directed toward the Lord, and secondarily toward righteousness and humility as sought qualities.

3399.text: In Ps.10.13 darash surfaces as 'call to account' rather than 'seek/inquire' -- this is a specialized forensic-requiring sense (cf. sense 1a6 'to investigate, enquire', extended toward legal reckoning) distinct from the devotional 'seek' sense used in Ps.10.4 just verses earlier in the same psalm, showing the root's range from religious pursuit to judicial demand within a single context.

3402.text: In Ps.10.4 darash (negated: 'does not seek') occupies the negative pole of the cluster's dual seeking-motif, paired with M08 pride and M58 wickedness in the same verse -- the wicked's pride is what suppresses the seeking-act, making darash's absence diagnostic of the wicked disposition.

3403.text: In Ps.10.13, other M-codes present (M58 wicked, M30 renounce, M47 heart) describe the wicked's rejection of God, while darash's own forensic sense ('call to account') stands as the rhetorical question's target, not modified by those terms directly.

3409.text: In Ps.10.4, the seeking operation (negated) is attributed to 'the wicked' (party) with God as its withheld object -- the wicked initiates no such act toward God.

3410.text: In Ps.10.13, the 'call to account' operation is rhetorically denied by the wicked (party) regarding God's (party) prerogative to require reckoning of him.

3537.text: In Ps.40.14, Ps.70.2, Ps.71.13, and Ps.71.24 'seek' functions in the stock formulaic phrase 'those who seek my life/hurt' -- fully within the base gloss's hostile-pursuit sense, consistent across all four occurrences with no unique nuance.

3543.text: Here the seeking (H1245, 'sought to do me hurt') is reported as already having resulted in the seekers' shame (M07) -- the causal pairing seen in Ps.40/70/71.13 is now narrated as fulfilled, and M12 (righteousness, H6666) is introduced as the psalmist's own vindicating quality contrasted against the failed seekers, adding a new relational thread beyond the shame-pairing.

3698.text: In construct with 'wicked' (wicked's way), derek functions to qualify/characterize the moral course of the wicked person rather than a literal road; standard figurative use.

3748.text: In Ezek.3.18 'require...at your hand' shifts from ordinary 'seek' to a legal/covenantal demand for blood-guilt accountability -- a judicial nuance heavier than plain searching, distinct from the more neutral/hostile-pursuit senses in 1Sam.22.23 and Jer.26.21 where it means 'seek to kill.'

3750.text: No prior context recorded. In Ezek.3.18 baqash (require blood) co-occurs with M58 (wicked) and M56 (iniquity); this seeking-characteristic's own contribution is that it names God's active accountability-demand triggered BY the wicked person's iniquity, linking the watchman's silence to a required reckoning rather than merely describing the wicked state itself.

3753.text: The operation 'require/seek' is initiated by God (speaking in first person, 'I will require') and directed toward the watchman ('at your hand'), a party held accountable for the wicked person's death.

4120.text: In Ezek 33.8 the surface rendering 'require' diverges from the base gloss 'seek/desire' toward the juridical sense of exacting blood-guilt from a negligent watchman -- carrying a forensic-accountability nuance absent from the more relational 'seek' occurrences (Song 5.6, 1Chr 16.10, Ps 105.3), and impacting the verse by casting God as the one who will hold the failed watchman legally liable.

4122.text: In Song 5.6, 1Chr 16.10, Ps 105.3, and Isa 45.19 the surface gloss 'sought/seek/Seek' sits squarely within the base sense of active searching/desiring with no notable divergence.

4125.text: No other M-code characteristic is tagged in Ezek.33.8 alongside H1245's blood-requiring; the wicked/iniquity terms present are role-tagged but not this cluster's home strongs.

4126.text: No other M-code characteristic is tagged in Ps.105.3 alongside H1245's seeking of the Lord.

4130.text: In Ezek.33.8, H1245 (require) is an operation initiated by the Lord (first person 'I will require'), directed toward the negligent watchman/prophet ('at your hand') regarding the wicked person's blood.

4131.text: In 1Chr.16.10 and Ps.105.3, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by worshippers ('those who seek'), directed toward the Lord as its object.

4517.text: In Ps.10.15 'call to account' renders the demand/require sense (1a4-1a6) of darash, applied to God calling the wicked's wickedness to account; this sits within the base gloss's legal-demand nuance, no unusual shift from attested senses.

4518.text: No prior context recorded. Other M-codes present (M24 'break/evildoer', M58 'wicked/wickedness') describe the object being judged; H1875's seeking-to-call-to-account functions as the judicial-inquiry operation directed AT those wicked characteristics, related but from a different cluster's vantage -- this pass notes the directional link without duplicating M24/M58's own findings.

4519.text: In Ps.10.15 the Psalmist (implicitly addressing God as agent) initiates the operation 'call to account' (H1875, role-T3) directed toward 'the wicked and evildoer' (party present, H7563/H7451H) -- an imperative summons for divine reckoning against the wicked party.

5236.text: In 2Chr.7.14 'seek my face' is the classic idiomatic combination (seek + face) meaning seeking God's favor/presence in penitence -- squarely within the base gloss's known idiomatic use, no further divergence.

5241.text: In 2Chr.7.14, seeking (H1245, seek my face) sits within a tightly-related chain with M09 (humble themselves) and M60 (forgive): seeking is the middle act -- following humbling and preceding turning -- that directs the humbled disposition specifically toward God's face/presence, making it the pivot that connects self-abasement to the divine forgiving response.

5243.text: In 2Chr.7.14, H1245 is the role-T3 operation: 'my people' (party) initiate the seeking, directed toward God's 'face' (representing the divine party) as part of the penitential sequence.

5260.text: In Isa.62.12 'Sought Out' functions as a passive-participle EPITHET/name for the restored city rather than describing an act of seeking performed by the city -- a nominalized, identity-conferring nuance distinct from the active-seeking sense elsewhere; the impact is to make the city's new identity itself the proof that it is desired/valued rather than forsaken.

5265.text: In Isa.62.12, H1875 ('Sought Out') is tightly related to M61 (Holy) and M79 (Redeemed): together they form a triad of covenant-identity epithets for the restored city -- holy status, redeemed status, and sought-out status jointly constitute the new name replacing the old reproach; being 'sought out' specifically supplies the relational proof that the city is now wanted rather than abandoned.

5313.text: 1Chr.22.19 'seek the Lord' is the classic devotional sense (1a3a), squarely within the base gloss.

5318.text: In 1Chr.22.19, darash (seek the Lord) sits alongside M47 (heart/mind, 'set your mind and heart to seek') and M44 (covenant, the ark of the covenant) -- the seeking here is explicitly heart-directed, showing darash functions as the outward enactment of an inward disposition (heart/mind) toward covenant faithfulness.

5370.text: Eccl 7:25's 'seek' (wisdom) is the standard intellectual-pursuit sense of baqash, well within its base gloss; no notable divergence.

5374.text: In Eccl 7:25, baqash (seeking wisdom) co-occurs with M16 (wisdom/folly terms), M43 (scheme/devices), M58 (wickedness), M66 (madness) and M15 (knowing). This characteristic's vantage: seeking is the METHOD by which the Preacher pursues and tests wisdom and folly — it is the investigative operation binding the other M-codes together as objects of inquiry rather than being one of them itself.

5393.text: Isa 16:5's 'seeks justice' sits within the base gloss of darash as habitual pursuit/exercise of a quality by a ruler; no unusual divergence.

5394.text: Hos 10:12's 'seek the Lord' and 1Chr 10:14's negated 'did not seek the Lord' both sit within darash's standard covenantal-seeking sense; no notable divergence beyond polarity (positive command vs. negative narrative report).

5395.text: In Isa 16:5, darash ('seeks justice') co-occurs with M72 (throne), M23 (established), M07/M50 (steadfast love), M13 (faithfulness), M63 (judges), M12 (justice/righteousness). This characteristic's vantage: seeking-justice functions as the active verb binding the throne's establishment (M23) to the moral qualities (M07 love, M13 faithfulness) that legitimate it — the ideal ruler's seeking is what operationalizes the other static virtue-nouns into royal practice.

5396.text: In Hos 10:12, darash ('seek the Lord') co-occurs with M12 (righteousness x2), M07/M50 (steadfast love), M05 (rain — a co-occurring but unrelated M-code here tagged to a different sense). This characteristic's vantage: seeking the Lord is presented as the temporal hinge-action ('it is time to seek') that must accompany sowing righteousness and reaping steadfast love — seeking is the posture that opens the way for God's response.

5399.text: In Isa 16:5, the seeking-justice operation is initiated by the enthroned Davidic ruler (party) and directed toward 'justice' as its object/goal — the ruler's judicial seeking benefits the people under judgment.

5400.text: In Hos 10:12, the seeking operation is initiated by Israel (addressed 'yourselves', party) and directed toward the Lord (party, T7) as the one to be sought before he comes to rain righteousness.

5462.text: In Ezek 3:20 baqash is rendered 'require' rather than the more common 'seek' -- the surface sense shifts from search-for to judicially exact/demand (blood-guilt accounting), a notable divergence from the base gloss of searching, carrying forensic weight (accountability for a death) rather than pursuit of an object; compare its hostile-pursuit sense in 1 Kgs 11:40 and its benign sense in Gen 43:30 -- here it is neither pursuit nor benign search but reckoning.

5463.text: In Exod 4:24, 1 Kgs 11:40, 2 Sam 20:19, and Ps 37:32 baqash is used in the well-attested idiomatic sense 'seek to kill/destroy' -- this is a recognized extension already covered by the base gloss's own range (seek, desire, exact), not a fresh divergence peculiar to a single occurrence.

5469.text: M58 (wicked, H7563), M74 (watches, H6822 -- front-loaded below), and M12 (righteous, H6662) are present in Ps 37:32 but characterize the subject (the wicked one) and the object (the righteous), while the seeking-to-kill is the operation connecting them; seeking is the hostile verb bridging the wicked-pole and righteous-pole characteristics without itself being one of those qualities.

5470.text: Ezek 3:20 contains M12 (righteous/righteousness/righteous deeds, H6662/H6664G/H6666), M56 (sin, H2403B), M77 (stumbling block, H4383), and M81 (turns/remembered, H7725O/H2142); the seeking-as-requiring (baqash, 'I will require... at your hand') is the culminating judicial-accounting operation that presupposes all these prior moral categories -- it is the mechanism by which righteousness, sin, and turning are weighed and the blood-debt assigned, standing structurally downstream of and dependent upon them rather than parallel to any single one.

5475.text: In Ps 37:32 the operation 'watches' (H6822, role-T3 in cluster, though tagged M74 here) is initiated by the wicked party toward the righteous party; the seeking-to-put-to-death (H1245) is the same wicked party's escalated intent directed at the same righteous target.

5476.text: In Ezek 3:20 the requiring (H1245, 'I will require... at your hand') is initiated by God (the speaking party, 'I') and directed toward the watchman ('your hand') -- the blood-debt is exacted from the addressed party for failing to warn, making God the initiator and the watchman the party toward whom the operation is directed.

5523.text: In 2Sam.4.11 'require' renders H1245 in its legal-demand sense (1a5 'to require, exact'), squarely within the base gloss's semantic range covering blood-guilt exaction; no unusual divergence from the base gloss is present.

5529.text: In 2Sam.4.11 the operation 'require' (H1245, role-T3-adjacent as the verse's core verb of speaker's intent) is initiated by the speaker (David) and directed toward the wicked men who killed the righteous man, demanding their blood at their hand - a party-to-party accountability operation.

5535.text: In 2Sam.4.11, H1245 (require) co-occurs with M58 (wicked), M12 (righteous), M23/M72 (hand), M16 (destroy); this characteristic's own vantage: 'require' names the retributive-justice operation that formally links the wicked party's guilt (M58) to the righteous victim (M12) via blood-accounting, distinct from M16's destructive consequence which follows rather than constitutes the seeking-act itself.

5553.text: In Ps.119.155 'seek' (do not seek your statutes) applies the base sense 'to seek with application/study' (1a7) to the psalmist's contrast between the wicked and the diligent; sits squarely within the base gloss.

5556.text: In Ezek.20.40 'require' shifts to the base sense 'to seek (with a demand), demand, require' (1a4) applied to cultic contributions/gifts - a distinctly legal-cultic exaction nuance compared to the devotional-seeking sense dominant elsewhere in the arc (e.g. Ps.119.155, 2Chr.30.19); here the impact is to frame God's acceptance of Israel's worship as itself an act of formally demanding their offerings, intensifying the transactional-covenantal register of the verse.

5557.text: In Ps.119.155, no operation-tagged (role-T3) word co-occurs with H1875 in the role list provided (the verb 'do' negation carries T5, not T3); D7.7.1 is not applicable here.

5560.text: In Ezek.20.40, the operation 'require' (H1875) is initiated by the Lord God (T7-tagged party) and directed toward the house of Israel (T11-tagged party), demanding their contributions and offerings - a divine-to-covenant-people exaction operation.

5561.text: In Ps.119.155, H1875 (seek) co-occurs with M58 (wicked) and M79 (salvation); this characteristic's vantage: the negated seeking ('do not seek your statutes') is presented as the causal reason salvation (M79) remains far from the wicked (M58) - H1875 functions as the missing condition linking the negative moral state to the absent positive outcome.

5564.text: In Ezek.20.40, H1875 (require) co-occurs with M61 (holy/sacred offerings), M08 (height), M42 (declares), M36 (serve), M39 (accept); this characteristic's vantage: 'require' is the concluding transactional act that formally claims the sacred contributions (M61) after acceptance (M39) of the people's service (M36), closing the covenantal exchange sequence.

5570.text: In 2Sam.4.11 'destroy' renders the Hiphil sense 'to consume (destroy)' (1c3) applied to David's vow to remove the murderers from the earth - a figurative extension of the burning-root to total eradication, consistent with the tree's own listed Hiphil sense; no unexpected divergence beyond that established figurative range.

5576.text: In Ezek.20.40 'height' functions as a qualifier of 'mountain' (the mountain height of Israel), specifying the elevated topographical status of the sanctuary-mountain rather than naming an independent quality; a modifying rather than standalone use.

5613.text: In Isa.51.1, Eccl.12.10, Amos.8.12, and Dan.1.20, baqash carries its ordinary sense of active searching/inquiring with no notable divergence from the base gloss.

5614.text: In Isa.51.1, M12 (righteousness, 'pursue righteousness') co-occurs with M83 (seek the Lord) in synonymous parallelism -- both describe the same devoted pursuit posture, seeking functioning as the relational counterpart to pursuing righteousness, oriented toward the Lord as source.

5615.text: In Eccl.12.10, M65 (words) and M18 (delight) and M13 (truth) and M12 (uprightly) are present but describe the object and manner of the Preacher's writing rather than being directly tied to the seeking-act itself; seeking here is the means by which fitting words are pursued, not a disposition shared with these other M-codes.

5620.text: In Isa.51.1, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by the addressed hearers/party ('you who pursue... you who seek') and directed toward the Lord as object of pursuit.

5621.text: In Eccl.12.10, H1245 (sought) is initiated by the Preacher (party) and directed toward finding words of delight -- an internal literary operation rather than an interpersonal one.

5693.text: Mal.2.15's 'seeking' (what was God seeking? Godly offspring) shifts the base gloss toward a purposive divine intent/design nuance -- not neutral searching but a stated relational goal for the covenant union, distinguishing it from hostile-seeking senses elsewhere (1Sam.20.16, Ps.4.2).

5696.text: Mal.2.15 pairs baqash (seeking godly offspring) with M47 (spirit) present twice in the verse and M14 (faithless/treacherous dealing) and M74 (guarding). From seeking's vantage: the divine seeking-goal (godly offspring) stands as the positive aim that M14's faithlessness threatens to undo, and M74's self-guarding is the human response required to protect that sought outcome -- seeking here functions as the stated divine purpose against which the other characteristics are measured.

5712.text: Isa.26.9's 'earnestly seeks' sits squarely within shachar's base intensive-devotional gloss -- no additional nuance beyond the term's characteristic sense.

5713.text: Isa.26.9 pairs shachar (earnestly seeking God) with M47 (soul/spirit, twice) and M12/M26 (judgments) and M12 (righteousness). From seeking's vantage: the intensive devotional seeking is the inward disposition (soul/spirit) that anticipates and responds to God's outward judgments producing righteousness in the world -- seeking here is the relational bridge between inward longing and the world's moral learning.

5728.text: Mark.14.1 and Acts.17.5 both use zeteo in the idiomatic Hebraic sense 'seek [someone] to kill/arrest' -- a lethal-hostile-pursuit nuance distinct from the base gloss of neutral searching, showing the term's capacity to carry murderous intent when its object is a targeted person.

5730.text: Acts.17.5 pairs zeteo (seeking to bring Jason's guests out) with M69 (jealous) and M58 (wicked). From seeking's vantage: the hostile seeking-action is the operational outworking of the mob's jealousy, using wicked men as instruments -- zeteo names the directed pursuit-act that jealousy motivates and wickedness executes.

5753.text: In Isa.26.9 shachar ('earnestly seeks') is the operation, initiated by the speaker's own spirit (first-person), directed toward God (2ms 'you') -- an inward-to-divine directed act.

5754.text: In Mal.2.15 baqash ('seeking') is the operation, initiated by God (the 'one'), directed toward the desired outcome of godly offspring from the marital union -- a divine-to-outcome directed act.

5758.text: In Acts.17.5 zeteo ('seeking') is the operation, initiated by the jealous Jews and their mob, directed toward Jason's household guests (Paul and companions) whom they intend to bring out to the crowd.

5793.text: In Isa.58.2, Ezra.6.21, and 1Chr.28.9 'seek/worship' sits squarely within the base cultic-consultation/devotion sense of H1875, with no further distinguishing nuance beyond ordinary devotional seeking of God.

5796.text: Numerous M-codes co-occur in Isa.58.2 (M18 delight, M15 know, M76 ways, M12 righteousness/judgment, M21 ask); H1875's own vantage is that 'seeking' functions as the umbrella act framing all these other qualities as its objects/means -- the people seek God's ways, delight, and righteousness together, with H1875 supplying the overarching pursuit-verb that the other M-codes qualify or specify.

6025.text: In Matt.6.33 'seek' functions as an imperative of prioritized spiritual pursuit ('seek first the kingdom') -- a moral-directive nuance elevating the term beyond simple literal search, impacting the verse as a call to reorder priorities; contrasts with the more neutral/literal 'search' senses elsewhere (e.g. Matt.13.45, Matt.18.12).

6032.text: The addressee ('you', imperative subject) initiates the seeking-operation directed toward 'the kingdom of God and his righteousness' as the object of pursuit, with God as the ultimate relational referent.

6039.text: M72 (kingdom, G0932) and M12 (righteousness, G1343) are both present and are the direct objects of the M83 seeking-operation; this seeking-characteristic functions here as the active means by which the kingdom and righteousness characteristics are to be pursued and prioritized, subordinating M83 as instrumental to attaining M72/M12.

6298.text: Here zeteo carries a negative nuance not present in its base gloss: 'seeking to establish' their own righteousness is a misdirected, self-reliant striving contrasted with submission; this diverges from the neutral/positive 'seek' sense (as in Rom.2.7's seeking glory) by casting the pursuit as spiritually futile and opposed to God's righteousness -- a rare negative-object use of the term.

6299.text: The operation zeteo is initiated by 'they' (unbelieving Israel, ignorant of God's righteousness) and is directed toward establishing 'their own' righteousness, in implicit contrast to God as the party whose righteousness they fail to submit to.

6300.text: Seeking here is entangled with ignorance (M63) of God's righteousness (M12) and failure to submit (M23): the seeking is the misapplied energy that substitutes for submission, showing this characteristic can function destructively when its object is self rather than God -- first relational pass for this verse.

6547.text: In Ps.37.25 'begging' renders baqash for a child seeking bread out of want, a specific nuance of desperate physical need rather than the more common senses of hostile pursuit or devotional seeking found elsewhere (e.g. Ps.27.4, Ps.35.4); the impact here is to underscore God's providence toward the righteous by contrast, since such begging is said never to be observed.

6560.text: Other M-codes present in Ps.37.25: M12 (righteous), M30/M59 (forsaken). Baqash (begging) describes the hypothetical desperate act of a righteous person's child; it stands in negated contrast to being forsaken (M30/M59), illustrating what does NOT happen to the righteous (M12), but does not itself modify those terms.

6572.text: In Ps.37.25, H1245 (begging) is an operation hypothetically initiated by 'his children' (the righteous person's offspring), directed toward obtaining bread — but the verse denies this ever occurs, so the operation is negated rather than actually enacted.

6638.text: In Eccl.7.29 the Piel form again denotes ordinary human seeking (schemes/devices), matching the base gloss without special divergence.

6669.text: In Eccl.7.29 the seeking is initiated by 'they' (mankind generally) and directed toward 'many schemes' (H2810) -- humanity as agent, self-devised contrivances as the object sought out.

6681.text: M12 (uprightness, on 'upright' describing man as God made him) and M14 (schemes/devices) frame this verse's contrast: seeking (M83) here is directed toward corrupt self-devised schemes rather than toward the uprightness God originally gave -- seeking functions as the corrupted response to a prior good given state.

7058.text: H7836 (shachar) shares the subgroup's general 'intensive/earnest seeking' theme with G1567/G1934 conceptually (both Greek terms and shachar converge on devotional 'seek God/wisdom diligently' senses: shachar in Ps.63.1, Isa.26.9, Job.8.5, Prov.8.17, Ps.78.34 parallels ekzeteo in Acts.15.17/Heb.11.6/Rom.3.11 and epizeteo's aspirational uses), but there is no lexical or morphological relationship -- shachar is a distinct Hebrew root (tied etymologically to 'dawn/early') with no direct Greek cognate among this subgroup's members, and unlike ekzeteo/epizeteo it never carries a judicial 'demand an account/blood' sense; its 'demanding' pole (Job.7.21, God seeking Job) is ironic-reversal rather than legal exaction.

7075.text: The 'require' surface form (Deut.18.19, Ezek.34.10, Mic.6.8, Ezek.20.40, Ezek.33.6, Deut.23.21, Gen.9.5) diverges sharply from the consultation sense: here H1875 denotes a superior party (God) formally demanding an accounting, exacting a debt, or requiring conduct/contributions from an inferior party -- the direction of the inquiry is inverted (God is the one requiring, not the one consulted), showing this single root spans both 'humans formally consulting a superior' AND 'a superior formally demanding of an inferior,' unified by the notion of a binding, authoritative claim being pressed rather than a casual search.

7084.text: Isa.16.5's 'seeks' (participle, 'one who...seeks justice') applies darash to an abstract ethical/judicial object (justice, mishpat) rather than a person or deity -- the ruler's habitual disposition of pursuing justice, distinct from the more common person-or-deity-directed senses.

7093.text: Ps.10.13 and Ps.10.15 both render darash as legal-accountability terms ('call to account'/'account') within the same psalm, applying the forensic-demand sense of darash to God's judicial reckoning with the wicked -- consistent with the Gen.9.5/Gen.42.22 'reckoning' pattern but here directed at moral wickedness rather than bloodshed specifically.

7099.text: Isa.62.12's 'Sought Out' functions as a passive-participle EPITHET/name for the restored city rather than describing an active act of seeking performed by anyone in the verse -- a nominalized, identity-conferring nuance unique among this pass's occurrences, making darash itself the substance of a proper name/title.

7113.text: Several occurrences orient the seeker toward a future fullness not yet possessed: Heb.11.14 and Heb.13.14 speak of seeking a homeland/city 'that is to come'; Isa.26.9 links earnest seeking to a future in which the world's inhabitants 'learn righteousness' when God's judgments come. This forward-orientation frames the seeking-characteristic as pilgrim/eschatological rather than merely present-satisfying.

7135.text: The pattern shows the characteristic engaging soul/spirit level pervasively (Ps.63.1 'my soul thirsts,' Isa.26.9 'my spirit within me earnestly seeks') and occasionally the body as an expressive overflow (Ps.63.1 'my flesh faints'), but the body link is expressive/indicative rather than causally central -- the body registers the intensity of the soul/spirit's seeking rather than itself seeking. The characteristic never engages a purely bodily mechanism independent of soul/spirit direction.

7157.text: Yes -- seeking produces finding, by the mechanism of diligent, sustained pursuit meeting a responsive object: 'those who seek me diligently find me' (Prov.8.17). It can also produce learned righteousness at a corporate scale when paired with divine judgment (Isa.26.9, 'when your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness').

7167.text: The subgroup shows clear future-fullness orientation: Heb.11.14 and Heb.13.14 (epizeteo) name a 'homeland' and 'city that is to come' not yet possessed; Acts.15.17 (ekzeteo) envisions Gentiles yet to seek the Lord eschatologically; Isa.26.9 (shachar) links earnest seeking to a future state when 'the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.' The movement is consistently toward something the person does not yet have -- a not-yet-attained relational or covenantal completeness.

7173.text: In devotional occurrences the felt quality is intense and bodily: Ps.63.1 pairs 'earnestly I seek' with 'my soul thirsts... my flesh faints,' and Isa.26.9 pairs it with 'my soul yearns... in the night.' These are not settled dispositions alone but acute, felt longing, expressed through explicit bodily/emotional language (thirst, fainting, yearning at night).

7191.text: The evidence engages spirit/soul-level seats primarily (Ps.63.1: 'my soul thirsts'; Isa.26.9: 'my spirit within me earnestly seeks') with body given expressive rather than causal role ('my flesh faints for you' as an outward sign of the soul's longing, not a bodily-originated act). The judicial/demand occurrences (Luke.11.50-51, Matt.16.4) engage no inner-constitutional level explicitly, operating instead at the level of corporate/legal accountability. The body link where present is expressive/indicative -- signaling the intensity of soul-level longing -- never the seat or origin of the seeking itself.

7193.text: The evidence shows movement primarily spirit/soul-to-behavior (inward longing producing the outward act of seeking, Isa.26.9, Ps.63.1) and, distinctly, movement onto the person from an external source in the judicial occurrences -- God's demand/requirement is imposed externally upon 'this generation' (Luke.11.50-51) rather than arising from within the person. No angelic or adversarial-spirit movement is attested anywhere in this subgroup's evidence.

7272.text: In Ps.10.4 the wicked's failure to seek God reveals his conclusion 'There is no God' -- the absence of inquiry is itself diagnostic of a settled unbelief; the characteristic here reveals a negative judgement about God's non-existence or irrelevance.

7275.text: Across the verses both patterns occur: seeking/inquiring often precedes a resulting belief or outcome (e.g. 2Chr.14.7 'we have sought the Lord... he has given us peace', Ps.34.4 'I sought the Lord, and he answered me'), while elsewhere the failure or presence of seeking follows from an already-settled disposition (Ps.10.4's pride precedes and explains the non-seeking; 2Chr.12.14's evil is explained by not having set the heart to seek). The characteristic functions bidirectionally as both antecedent to and consequence of belief/judgement.

7284.text: In 1Chr.22.19 and 2Chr.15.12 seeking is framed as a settled, wholehearted disposition ('set your mind and heart to seek', 'seek the Lord... with all their heart and with all their soul') rather than a transient emotional reaction -- the language of heart/soul signals an internalized, durable orientation.
