7285.text: The felt quality of seeking varies by context: it is crisis-driven and emotionally anguished in Ps.77.2 and 2Chr.20.3 (trouble, fear), yet presented as a settled, wholehearted covenantal disposition in 1Chr.22.19, 2Chr.15.12, and 2Chr.22.9 ('sought the Lord with all his heart') -- the same term covers both transient emotional response and durable devotional orientation depending on narrative occasion.

7288.text: Seeking takes hold rightly under conditions of wholeheartedness and sincerity: 'set your mind and heart to seek' (1Chr.22.19), 'with all their heart and with all their soul' (2Chr.15.12), and freedom from co-present idolatry -- in Ezek.14.7 the presence of idols in the heart is what disqualifies otherwise-outward consultation. Genuine seeking requires an undivided heart free from rival objects of devotion.

7289.text: Seeking is blocked or nullified when the heart harbors idols or a stumbling block of iniquity even while outwardly consulting God -- Ezek.14.3, 14.7 explicitly describe men who 'have taken their idols into their hearts' yet 'come to a prophet to consult me' -- God declares he will not let himself be consulted (or will answer in judgment) in such cases; similarly pride (Ps.10.4 'in the pride of his face') suppresses seeking altogether.

7294.text: The characteristic's presence marks a person as rightly oriented toward God in covenant fidelity, and its absence marks corruption or apostasy (Ps.10.4, 1Chr.10.14 'He did not seek guidance from the Lord... the Lord put him to death'); this indicates that the capacity to seek/inquire is part of humanity's created relational orientation toward God, and its exercise or neglect functions as a diagnostic marker of the divine image's proper functioning or its corruption in the person.

7299.text: Where seeking is present in a person (2Chr.22.9 'sought the Lord with all his heart'), it indicates the divine image is functioning rightly in relational orientation toward God; where absent (Ps.10.4, 1Chr.10.14), it indicates a corrupted or suppressed image-bearing capacity, evidenced by pride and covenant unfaithfulness leading to death.

7300.text: The evidence shows seeking engages the heart/soul level most deeply and consistently ('with all their heart and with all their soul', 2Chr.15.12; 'set your mind and heart', 1Chr.22.19), with the body's role limited to expressive gesture (Ps.77.2's stretched-out hand) rather than being the seat of the characteristic itself. The pattern indicates seeking's depth and seat is the heart/soul (volitional-affective center), while the body-link (where present) is expressive/indicative of the inner state rather than mediating or generative of it -- darash never engages purely bodily/instinctive levels without heart involvement in these texts.

7311.text: The pattern of engagement shows heart/soul faculties (mind, will, affection) consistently engaged when seeking is genuine (1Chr.22.19 'set your mind and heart', 2Chr.15.12 'with all their heart and with all their soul'), while purely external/ritual engagement without heart involvement is exposed as illegitimate (Ezek.14.3-7) -- indicating the characteristic's nature is fundamentally a volitional-relational act requiring the engagement of the inner faculties, not a mechanical or merely verbal performance.

7314.text: The structural opposite of seeking is forsaking/neglecting -- explicitly named as the contrastive pole in 1Chr.28.9 ('if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever') and implied by negation in Ps.10.4 ('does not seek') and 1Chr.10.14 ('did not seek guidance') -- the inner-being reality that excludes seeking is self-sufficient neglect or active abandonment of the source that ought to be consulted.

7315.text: At its edge, seeking excludes casual, passive, or half-hearted attention -- it resists mere outward performance without inner devotion (Ezek.14.3-7's idol-hearted consulters are the negative exemplar), and it excludes self-sufficiency/pride that renders inquiry unnecessary (Ps.10.4).

7317.text: Adjacent characteristics appearing alongside seeking include 'heart/mind' (M47, frequently paired as the seat/manner of seeking, e.g. 1Chr.22.19, 2Chr.15.12, Ps.119.2/10), 'trust' (M19, Ps.9.10, Isa.31.1), and 'forsake' (M30/M59, as antithetical pairing, Ps.9.10, 1Chr.28.9) -- these co-occur with notable frequency, showing seeking is characteristically bound to heart-language and its antithesis, forsaking.

7323.text: Seeking is a constituent element of the larger characteristic of 'setting the heart' (2Chr.19.3, 2Chr.30.19, 1Chr.22.19 all pair 'set the heart/mind' with 'to seek') -- the heart-setting act supplies the internal disposition of which seeking is the outward-directed enactment, making seeking a component within the fuller act of wholehearted devotion.

7386.text: Whole network: innocence is the terminal node the entire grief-cascade (earnestness, indignation, fear, longing/zeal, punishment) converges to produce and demonstrate.

7387.text: The operation "proved" (G4921) is initiated by the Corinthians themselves, directed toward demonstrating their own innocence in the matter.

7408.text: Earnestness is the first-named fruit godly grief produced in the Corinthians, leading them toward proving themselves innocent in the matter.

7409.text: The most immediate response shown is an eagerness to clear themselves, following directly from the earnestness godly grief produced.

7410.text: Over the course of the verse earnestness establishes a demonstrated innocence -- a settled state of proven blamelessness in the matter.

7411.text: Earnestness marks a change from indifference/sin to active corrective concern; the verse frames it as a lasting, proven change ("at every point... innocent"), both in condition and orientation.

7412.text: Sequence shown: godly grief (before) produces earnestness and its companion states (during), resulting in proven innocence (after).

7413.text: The mechanism is an encounter with godly grief that produces earnestness as sudden, sharp response rather than gradual formation.

7414.text: Earnestness originates as the product of godly grief within the Corinthians -- generated within the person as an effect of that grief.

7415.text: Earnestness is not directly predicated of God here; it is the human fruit produced by godly grief in the Corinthians toward Paul.

7416.text: Godly grief serves the purpose of leading the Corinthians to repentance-shaped earnestness and ultimately to proven innocence.

7417.text: The mechanism is an encounter -- Paul's rebuking letter -- that produced this godly grief, which in turn produced the whole list of responses.

7418.text: Grief is qualified as "godly," relating it to God as the standard/source shaping its character, distinguishing it from worldly grief.

7419.text: Indignation is one of the fruits godly grief produced, contributing to the Corinthians proving themselves innocent.

7420.text: Indignation engages moral evaluation and affect -- a felt reaction of vexation at the wrongdoing that had occurred among them.

7421.text: Longing is one of the produced effects reflecting the Corinthians' desire to be reconciled with Paul, contributing to their proven innocence.

7422.text: Longing engages affect and relational capacity -- an earnest emotional desire directed toward restored relationship.

7423.text: Zeal is one of the produced effects showing renewed ardent commitment, contributing to the Corinthians' proven innocence.

7424.text: Zeal engages volition and affect -- an energetic will to act rightly and a passionate emotional investment in doing so.

7425.text: Fear here serves as one of the produced effects showing the seriousness with which the Corinthians took the matter, contributing to their proven innocence.

7426.text: Fear engages affect and conscience -- a felt apprehension tied to awareness of wrongdoing and its consequences.

7427.text: Punishment/readiness to see justice done is the final produced effect, completing the case that supports the Corinthians' proven innocence.

7428.text: Punishment/vindication engages moral evaluation -- the Corinthians' willingness to see the wrong justly addressed.

7429.text: Being found "innocent" is the culminating verdict/effect the whole grief-cascade served to establish for the Corinthians.

7430.text: Marks the completed change: from implicated in wrongdoing to proven innocent; the verse's own wording ("at every point") signals this is a settled, not merely temporary, outcome.

7615.text: Whole network: knew is the evidentiary anchor grounding the master's (M72) dual verdict of wicked/slothful (M58/M67) against the servant, delivered through answering (M41).

7633.text: This occurrence matches the term's usual factual/cognitive-knowledge sense (know that X is the case); no divergent nuance is carried here beyond the standard usage.

10564.text: As one item in the rhetorical catalogue of effects, indignation is directional -- reacting against the offense itself, distinct from fear (directed at consequence) or longing (directed toward reconciliation).

10565.text: Root sense of vexation/physical-then-emotional irritation shows the term operating here as an intensified negative reaction against the wrong committed.

10566.text: This is the term's sole NT occurrence, but its sense here (vexation/indignation) matches ordinary classical usage (e.g. Thucydides' 'vexation'); no special divergence.

10567.text: As an accusative singular feminine noun, it functions as one of the parallel direct objects governed by 'what', naming a discrete emotional outcome rather than an ongoing action.

10568.text: Within the range from physical irritation to divine wrath, this occurrence sits at the human 'vexation at wrongdoing' point in the range, fitting the moral context of the letter.

10569.text: This occurrence expresses an act/reaction produced in the hearers -- indignation as one of the specific outcomes of the grief, not a settled disposition or received quality.

10570.text: No structural opposite term (e.g. complacency/apathy) for aganaktesis is present among the related terms listed in this verse.

10571.text: No person-type term for one who habitually feels indignation is present among related terms in this verse.

10572.text: No supplication/seeking-term for indignation is present among related terms in this verse.

10573.text: As a NT Greek hapax in Paul, the term carries over its classical secular sense of vexation without added theological freight of its own, though the surrounding context moralizes it as a righteous response.

10574.text: Aganaktesis is attested pre-NT in Plato and Thucydides ('vexation'); not a NT coinage, though this is its only NT occurrence.

10575.text: As accusative noun (N-ASM), 'fear' here names the trembling concern the Corinthians felt regarding the seriousness of the offense and its correction.

10576.text: Here phobos denotes trembling concern/apprehension -- a felt anxiety about consequences that motivated the Corinthians' corrective response, matching the sense used again in v.15.

10577.text: As one item among the produced reactions, fear here is directional -- oriented toward the seriousness of the matter and the possible relational rupture with Paul, driving urgency to make things right.

10578.text: Root sense tied to panic/dread shows the term operating here in its milder, moralized 'trembling concern' register rather than sheer terror.

10579.text: This occurrence's sense (trembling concern about the matter) matches its use in the very next verse (7:15) and other Pauline uses in this letter; no divergence.

10580.text: As an accusative singular masculine noun, it stands as one of the parallel objects in the list, naming a discrete emotional/moral outcome of the grief.

10581.text: Within the range from panic-terror to reverential awe, this occurrence sits at the 'trembling concern' point, appropriate to a moral/relational crisis rather than physical danger.

10582.text: This occurrence expresses a produced act/reaction -- fear as one specific outcome generated by the grief -- rather than an abiding disposition.

10583.text: No structural opposite term (e.g. boldness/confidence) for phobos is present among the related terms listed in this verse.

10584.text: No person-type term for a fearful/reverent person is present among related terms in this verse.

10585.text: No supplication/seeking-term for fear is present among related terms in this verse.

10586.text: As NT Greek, phobos here carries the same range attested in classical usage; the moral/relational Christian context specifies fear-of-consequence-for-sin rather than altering the base lexical sense.

10587.text: Phobos is attested from Homer onward across classical Greek literature; not a NT coinage.

10588.text: As accusative noun (N-ASF), 'longing' names an earnest desire/strong affection produced in the Corinthians -- toward renewed relationship with Paul.

10589.text: Here epipothesis denotes earnest desire/strong affection -- a yearning quality, paired with its cognate use in 7:7 describing the Corinthians' longing for Paul.

10590.text: As one produced effect in the list, longing is relationally directional -- oriented toward restored fellowship/reconciliation with Paul, distinct from indignation's orientation against the wrong itself.

10591.text: Root sense 'longing after' shows the term operating here as strong affectionate desire directed at restoring the relationship.

10592.text: This occurrence's sense (earnest longing/affection) matches its only other NT use at 7:7 in the same letter; no divergence.

10593.text: As an accusative singular feminine noun paralleling the other listed objects, it names a discrete affective outcome rather than a verbal action.

10594.text: Within a narrow semantic range essentially limited to 'earnest desire/longing', this occurrence sits centrally, showing the relational-affection sense of the term.

10595.text: This occurrence expresses a produced act/disposition -- a longing generated by the grief, oriented toward restoring the relationship, not a received condition.

10596.text: No structural opposite term (e.g. indifference/aversion) for epipothesis is present among related terms in this verse.

10597.text: No person-type term for one characterized by longing is present among related terms in this verse.

10598.text: No supplication/seeking-term distinct from the longing itself is present among related terms in this verse.

10599.text: As NT Greek, epipothesis appears only in this Pauline letter and carries no distinct OT/Hebrew background to weigh against; its sense is drawn directly from Paul's own usage.

10600.text: LSJ cites epipothesis only in NT (2 Cor 7:7, 7:11) and later authors (Aquila, Damascius); it has no earlier classical attestation, marking it as effectively a NT-period term.

10601.text: As accusative noun (N-ASM), 'zeal' names the fervent, ardent commitment the Corinthians displayed in support of Paul and against the wrong.

10602.text: Here zelos denotes ardent affection/enthusiasm in the good sense -- earnest concern for the right outcome, distinct from its bad-sense use elsewhere (jealousy/envy).

10603.text: As a produced effect near the climax of the list, zeal is directional -- fervent energy channeled toward vindicating Paul and resolving the offense, just before 'punishment' names the corrective outcome.

10604.text: Root sense of intense rivalry/fervour shows the term operating here as positive, ardent commitment rather than the jealousy/envy sense the same root can carry.

10605.text: Zelos can mean jealousy/envy in a bad sense elsewhere (Acts 13:45; Rom 13:13), but this occurrence's surface use as a positive fruit of godly grief renders it as commendable zeal/ardor, aligning with its good-sense use in Jn 2:17 and Rom 10:2 rather than the negative pole.

10606.text: As an accusative singular masculine noun in the list, it names a discrete produced quality/reaction, in parallel with the other objects governed by 'what'.

10607.text: Within a range spanning jealousy/rivalry to fervent zeal/enthusiasm, this occurrence sits at the positive fervent-commitment end, matching the good-sense usage seen in Jn 2:17.

10608.text: This occurrence expresses a produced act/disposition -- ardent zeal generated as a fruit of the grief, not a received or static quality.

10609.text: Zelos itself can function as its own structural opposite depending on sense (bad-sense jealousy vs good-sense ardor); here the positive pole is meant, standing against the jealousy/envy pole attested elsewhere for the same term.

10610.text: No distinct person-type term (e.g. 'zealot') for one who possesses zelos is present among related terms in this verse.

10611.text: No supplication/seeking-term for zeal is present among related terms in this verse.

10612.text: As NT Greek, zelos here draws on the classical eager-rivalry sense but is disambiguated by context toward the positive fervor sense rather than the jealousy sense also live in NT usage.

10613.text: Zelos is attested from Hesiod and classical Greek (Sophocles, Plato, Demosthenes) long before the NT; not a NT coinage.

10614.text: As accusative noun (N-ASF), 'punishment' names the readiness to see justice/retribution enacted against the wrongdoer, capping the list of produced effects.

10615.text: Here ekdikesis denotes vengeance/retributive justice/punishment -- the Corinthians' willingness to see the offender justly dealt with, matching its use elsewhere for vindication/retribution.

10616.text: As the final and most extreme item in the list, punishment is directional toward the offender -- the corrective, justice-restoring culmination of the whole chain of reactions.

10617.text: Root sense 'avenging/giving satisfaction' shows the term operating here as the community's readiness to see the matter set right through corrective justice.

10618.text: This occurrence's sense (retributive justice/punishment) matches its ordinary NT usage (Luke 21:22; Rom 12:19; 1 Pet 2:14); no divergence.

10619.text: As an accusative singular feminine noun, the final item in the parallel list of objects, it names the outcome-oriented disposition to see justice done rather than an action performed by the subject.

10620.text: Within a range from legal remedy/satisfaction to divine vengeance, this occurrence sits at the community-justice pole -- willingness to see the wrong punished within the church body.

10621.text: This occurrence expresses a produced disposition -- readiness for corrective justice generated as a fruit of the grief, not an act already carried out.

10622.text: No structural opposite term (e.g. mercy/pardon) for ekdikesis is present among related terms in this verse.

10623.text: No person-type term (e.g. avenger) for ekdikesis is present among related terms in this verse.

10624.text: No supplication/seeking-term for punishment is present among related terms in this verse.

10625.text: As NT Greek, ekdikesis here follows the sense already visible in the LSJ's cited NT usages (Luke, Acts) of legal/corrective satisfaction; the Testament context doesn't shift the sense further in this verse.

10626.text: Ekdikesis is attested pre-NT in Polybius (2nd c. BC) for 'giving satisfaction'; not a NT coinage.

10627.text: As accusative plural adjective (A-APM), 'innocent' describes the Corinthians themselves as proved pure/blameless in the matter, the outcome of the whole process described.

10628.text: Here hagnos denotes moral purity/blamelessness -- the state the Corinthians have proven themselves to be in regarding the offense, following their godly-grief-driven response.

10629.text: As the concluding predicate adjective applied to the Corinthians, it constitutes the verse's final verdict -- the whole chain of reactions is shown to have vindicated them as pure in the matter.

10630.text: Root sense of ritual/moral purity shows the term operating here as declared moral blamelessness, established through the community's corrective response.

10631.text: This occurrence's sense (morally pure/blameless/innocent) matches the term's usual NT ethical usage; no divergence.

10632.text: As an accusative plural adjective modifying 'yourselves', it functions predicatively, ascribing the quality of innocence to the Corinthians as the proven result of the proceeding events.

10633.text: Within a range from cultic/ritual purity to general moral uprightness, this occurrence sits at the ethical-innocence end, describing exoneration from complicity in the wrongdoing.

10634.text: This occurrence expresses a proven quality/condition (innocence established), not an act or a received quality bestowed from elsewhere.

10635.text: No structural opposite term (e.g. guilt/defilement) for hagnos is present among related terms in this verse.

10636.text: No person-type term for one who habitually possesses hagnos-purity is present among related terms in this verse.

10637.text: No supplication/seeking-term for purity/innocence is present among related terms in this verse.

10638.text: As NT Greek, hagnos here carries forward the classical sense of purity/chastity but is applied ethically to communal innocence in a dispute, a specifically Pauline moral extension rather than the cultic/ritual purity common in classical usage.

10639.text: Hagnos is attested from Homer onward (Odyssey, Pindar, Sophocles); not a NT coinage.

12481.text: God chooses a person for a task or office: priests and Levites, the king, David, Solomon, the servant, witnesses. Choosing goes with bringing near: "The one whom he chooses he will bring near to him" (Num 16:5); "Blessed is the one you choose and bring near" (Psa 65:4). The choice is shown, not argued: "the staff of the man whom I choose shall sprout" (Num 17:5). It is followed by a charge: "the Lord has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary; be strong and do it" (1Ch 28:10). In the servant it is joined to God's soul and Spirit: "my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him" (Isa 42:1; Mat 12:18).

12482.text: God chooses a people, and the verses give love as the ground and deny number: "It was not because you were more in number than any other people that the Lord set his love on you and chose you" (Deu 7:7); "the Lord set his heart in love on your fathers and chose their offspring" (Deu 10:15). The choosing makes them "a people for his treasured possession" (Deu 7:6) and "his chosen ones" (Psa 105:6). It is joined to not casting off, "I have chosen you and not cast you off" (Isa 41:9), and to a purpose: "that you may know and believe me" (Isa 43:10).

12483.text: God chooses a place "to make his name dwell there" (Deu 12:11), and the choosing carries his own presence: "My eyes and my heart will be there for all time" (2Ch 7:16). The people's offerings, eating, rejoicing, judgement, reading of the law and prayer are all directed to the place he chooses. The choice can be cast off, "I will cast off this city that I have chosen" (2Ki 23:27), and made again: "the Lord will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem" (Zec 1:17).

12484.text: A person chooses the Lord, his ways and the good: "choose this day whom you will serve" (Jos 24:15), and the choice is witnessed: "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the Lord" (Jos 24:22); "I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I set your rules before me" (Psa 119:30); "who choose the things that please me and hold fast my covenant" (Isa 56:4). Choosing needs knowing and instruction: "when he knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good" (Isa 7:15); "Him will he instruct in the way that he should choose" (Psa 25:12). It can be done together: "Let us choose what is right; let us know among ourselves what is good" (Job 34:4). Preference is stated: "I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God" (Psa 84:10); "choosing rather to be mistreated with the people of God than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin" (Heb 11:25).

12487.text: Inner-being words stand beside choosing: God's heart in what he chooses, "My eyes and my heart will be there for all time" (2Ch 7:16); his soul in his chosen servant, "my chosen, in whom my soul delights" (Isa 42:1; Mat 12:18); the people's heart and soul turned toward the chosen city in repentance (1Ki 8:48; 2Ch 6:38); the soul's delight in chosen ways (Isa 66:3); the soul choosing death (Job 7:15); the heart given a worth (Pro 10:20); the soul's appetite, "whenever you desire" (Deu 12:21; Deu 18:6); the self humbled in a fast God does not choose (Isa 58:5); "one deeply despised" whom the Lord has chosen (Isa 49:7).

12490.text: "Choice" as worth preferred over another: "To get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver" (Pro 16:16); "A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches" (Pro 22:1); "The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; the heart of the wicked is of little worth" (Pro 10:20); also Pro 8:10, 8:19 and Song 5:15.

12492.text: God chooses what he wants: "Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of wickedness" (Isa 58:6), set against a fast of bowing the head (Isa 58:5); "To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice" (Pro 21:3); "I will appoint over her whomever I choose. For who is like me?" (Jer 49:19; Jer 50:44).

12495.text: The willing heart and spirit (nādîb): "Whoever is of a generous heart, let him bring" (Exo 35:5); "All who were of a willing heart brought" (Exo 35:22), after "everyone whose heart stirred him" (35:21); after consecration, "all who were of a willing heart brought burnt offerings" (2Ch 29:31); with God's plan for the temple, "with you in all the work will be every willing man who has skill" (1Ch 28:21); and asked of God, "uphold me with a willing spirit" (Psa 51:12).

12499.text: A refusal that keeps faith: "the servants of the king would not put out their hand to strike the priests of the Lord" (1Sa 22:17); David, "I would not put out my hand against the Lord's anointed" (1Sa 26:23); David longed for the water of Bethlehem, "But he would not drink of it. He poured it out to the Lord" (2Sa 23:16), "Shall I drink the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" (2Sa 23:17; 1Ch 11:18-19). The faithful refuse enticement and demand: "you shall not yield to him or listen to him" (Deu 13:8); "if sinners entice you, do not consent" (Pro 1:10); "Do not listen or consent" (1Ki 20:8).

12507.text: The counting word is used for what is credited or imputed to a person before God: "neither shall it be credited to him" (Lev 7:18); "bloodguilt shall be imputed to that man" (Lev 17:4); "your contribution shall be counted to you" (Num 18:27, 30); Phinehas, "that was counted to him as righteousness from generation to generation forever" (Psa 106:31).

12514.text: The looking-ahead words are used most often against another person. It is placed in the heart: "let none of you devise evil against another in your heart" (Zec 7:10), "do not devise evil in your hearts against one another" (Zec 8:17). It is done together: "Come, let us make plots against Jeremiah" (Jer 18:18); "In Heshbon they planned disaster against her" (Jer 48:2); "they made plans to put him to death" (Joh 11:53), and Lazarus as well (Joh 12:10); "The soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners" (Act 27:42). It is aimed at the righteous and the weak: "The wicked plots against the righteous and gnashes his teeth at him" (Psa 37:12); "who have planned to trip up my feet" (Psa 140:4). It hides behind a friendly word: "Come and let us meet together" "But they intended to do me harm" (Neh 6:2); Saul's bride-price, "Saul thought to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines" (1Sa 18:25). It is pinned on the other side: "you and the Jews intend to rebel" (Neh 6:6). Another pleads against it: Esther "pleaded with him to avert the evil plan of Haman" (Est 8:3; 9:24).

12517.text: In the Greek the will is weighed against another's: "Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released for them Barabbas" (Mar 15:15), after "do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?" (Joh 18:39); "when Paul wished to go in among the crowd, the disciples would not let him" (Act 19:30); "when he wished to cross to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him" (Act 18:27); "they wished to set me at liberty" (Act 28:18), until the Jews objected; Diotrephes "stops those who want to and puts them out of the church" (3Jo 10); Paul "would have been glad to keep him with me" (Phm 13), and left the consent to Philemon.

12521.text: The will word also carries wanting to know and stated wishes: "desiring to know the real reason" (Act 22:30; 23:28); "We wish to know therefore what these things mean" (Act 17:20); "I would like to hear the man myself" (Act 25:22); "I refuse to be a judge of these things" (Act 18:15). Paul's wishes in teaching each come with their reason: "I desire then that in every place the men should pray, lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling" (1Ti 2:8); "So I would have younger widows marry" (1Ti 5:14); "I want you to insist on these things, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works" (Tit 3:8); "I want you to know" (Phi 1:12); "so that our joy may be complete" (2Jo 12); "I want to remind you" (Jude 5).

12524.text: His purpose is before the ages and not from works: "because of his own purpose and grace, which he gave us in Christ Jesus before the ages began" (2Ti 1:9); "in order that God's purpose of election might continue, not because of works but because of him who calls" (Rom 9:11); "according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will" (Eph 1:11); "the mystery of his will, according to his purpose, which he set forth in Christ" (Eph 1:9); "the eternal purpose that he has realized in Christ Jesus our Lord" (Eph 3:11); "whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood" (Rom 3:25).

12525.text: Holiness rules with little inner act: priests are to "abstain from the holy things of the people of Israel, which they dedicate to me, so that they do not profane my holy name" (Lev 22:2); "Thus you shall keep the people of Israel separate from their uncleanness, lest they die in their uncleanness by defiling my tabernacle" (Lev 15:31); "Aaron was set apart to dedicate the most holy things" (1Ch 23:13).

12526.text: Among the vowed gifts, a person dedicates what is his own: "When a man dedicates his house as a holy gift to the Lord, the priest shall value it as either good or bad" (Lev 27:14); part of his land, "the valuation shall be in proportion to its seed" (27:16), from or after the jubilee (27:17-18); a field he has bought (27:22). The gift can be taken back at a cost: "if the donor wishes to redeem his house, he shall add a fifth" (27:15; 27:19). If it is not redeemed, "it shall not be redeemed anymore" (27:20).

12528.text: The same giving can be turned to an idol. Micah's mother: "I dedicate the silver to the Lord from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a metal image" (Judg 17:3), in days when "Everyone did what was right in his own eyes" (17:6). Israel "came to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to the thing of shame, and became detestable like the thing they loved" (Hos 9:10), after "Like grapes in the wilderness, I found Israel". And one "who separates himself from me, taking his idols into his heart" (Eze 14:7), whose heart God means to "lay hold of" (14:5).

12533.text: "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations" (Jer 1:5). Jeremiah answers, "Ah, Lord God! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth" (1:6), and is told, "Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you" (1:8).

12535.text: STEP sets the surface on the neighbouring English word in a few verses: Mic 7:17 gives H7264 "turn" and H6342 "come trembling"; Gen 27:33 gives H2731 "said"; Psa 14:5 and 53:5 give H6343 "great"; Job 3:25 gives H6343 "thing". The face was read from the verse, not from the surface word.

12537.text: Face B, felt before God's presence, act or word, or a spirit: dread, terrified, trembled and trembling, with God's presence, his voice in the thunder, his word read aloud, a vision or his act as the object; once a spirit in the night.

12539.text: Face D, fearing or trembling before God as a standing: trembling at his word; "let him be your dread"; fearing "always"; awe of his words.

12542.text: Face I, not fearing: no fear of God; not afraid at his word; not trembling before a man; creatures without fear.

12553.text: Face T, trembling called for: a summons or decree to the earth, the peoples, the complacent and the heavens.

12554.text: Dread and trembling arise before God's presence, voice, word and act: "I am terrified at his presence; when I consider, I am in dread of him" (Job 23:15-16); "At this also my heart trembles" at the thunder (Job 37:1); "all the people in the camp trembled" at Sinai (Exo 19:16); at Daniel's vision "I stood up trembling" (Dan 10:7, 10-11); "they turned trembling to one another, saying, 'What is this that God has done to us?'" (Gen 42:28); "The sinners in Zion are afraid" (Isa 33:14); "I was in terror of calamity from God" (Job 31:23); "Will not his majesty terrify you" (Job 13:11).

12561.text: Trembling is called for and decreed: "tremble before him, all the earth!" (Psa 96:9; 1Ch 16:30); "let the peoples tremble!" (Psa 99:1); "Tremble, O earth, at the presence of the Lord" (Psa 114:7); "Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble" (Joe 2:1); "Tremble, you women who are at ease" (Isa 32:9-11); Darius, "people are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel" (Dan 6:26); "Be appalled, O heavens" (Jer 2:12).

12565.text: What it is turned toward: dread is forbidden toward what the people dread and commanded toward the Lord, in consecutive verses (Isa 8:12-13).

12573.text: Face C, fear spoken against: "Do not fear", "Fear not", "I will not fear", "not afraid"; a speaker (God, an angel, a prophet, a leader, a midwife, Boaz, Jael, Absalom, the psalmist to himself) addresses the fear and a ground is given.

12574.text: Face D, fearing God as a way of life: fear, fears, feared, fearing, reverence, God-fearing and worship; not a passing state but a standing, commanded, learned, taught, given, lived, joined with walking, serving, keeping and turning from evil.

12580.text: Face J, other faces: fear rendered as a manner of acting (cautious, shuns, reveres, the word feared).

12581.text: "Do not fear" nearly always comes with a ground, introduced by "for": "for I am with you" (Gen 26:24; Isa 41:10; 43:5; Jer 1:8; Jer 42:11; Deu 20:1; Deu 31:8); "I have given him into your hand" (Num 21:34; Deu 3:2; Jos 8:1; 10:8; 11:6); "I have redeemed you" (Isa 43:1); "I am your shield" (Gen 15:1); "God has heard the voice of the boy" (Gen 21:17); "you have borne a son" (Gen 35:17; 1Sa 4:20); "I will show you kindness" (2Sa 9:7); "those who are with us are more than those who are with them" (2Ki 6:16); idols "cannot do evil" (Jer 10:5); "am I in the place of God? ... I will provide for you" (Gen 50:19, 21); "for God has come to test you" (Exo 20:20).

12582.text: "Do not fear" is paired with other commands: "be strong and courageous" (Deu 31:6; Jos 10:25; 1Ch 22:13; 28:20; 2Ch 32:7); "do not be dismayed" (Deu 1:21; 31:8; Jos 8:1; 2Ch 20:15, 17; Isa 41:10); "stand firm, and see the salvation of the Lord" (Exo 14:13); "Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome" (Neh 4:14); "remember what the Lord your God did" (Deu 7:18); "Be careful, be quiet" (Isa 7:4); "let your hands be strong" (Zec 8:13); "let not your hands grow weak" (Zep 3:16); "Peace be with you" (Dan 10:19); "Peace to you" (Gen 43:23; Judg 6:23).

12583.text: What God does toward those who fear him, one verse each: steadfast love (Psa 103:11, 17); compassion "as a father shows compassion" (Psa 103:13); "The friendship of the Lord is for those who fear him" (Psa 25:14); he instructs (Psa 25:12); "the eye of the Lord is on those who fear him" (Psa 33:18); "The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him" (Psa 34:7); no lack (Psa 34:9); food (Psa 111:5); "fulfills the desire ... hears their cry" (Psa 145:19); "takes pleasure in" (Psa 147:11); goodness stored up (Psa 31:19); salvation near (Psa 85:9); a banner (Psa 60:4); a heritage (Psa 61:5); the book of remembrance (Mal 3:16); "the sun of righteousness shall rise" (Mal 4:2).

12585.text: Turned onto what is feared, the root describes: God himself, "the great, the mighty, and the awesome God" (Deu 10:17; 7:21), the great and awesome God "who keeps covenant and steadfast love" in three prayers (Neh 1:5; 9:32; Dan 9:4); his name (Psa 99:3; 111:9; Deu 28:58); his deeds (Psa 66:3, 5; 145:6; 106:22; Exo 34:10; Isa 64:3); his day, "great and very awesome; who can endure it?" (Joe 2:11, 31; Mal 4:5); a place (Gen 28:17); an angel's appearance (Jdg 13:6); the wilderness, "great and terrifying" (Deu 1:19; 8:15); an invading nation, "dreaded and fearsome" (Hab 1:7); a people "feared near and far" (Isa 18:2, 7); the living creatures' rims and the crystal expanse (Eze 1:18, 22); the human frame, "I am fearfully and wonderfully made" (Psa 139:14).

12587.text: The root is rendered as a manner of acting: "One who is wise is cautious and turns away from evil, but a fool is reckless" (Pro 14:16); "he who shuns an oath" (Ecc 9:2); "he who reveres the commandment will be rewarded" (Pro 13:13); among Pharaoh's servants "whoever feared the word of the Lord ... hurried his slaves and his livestock into the houses" (Exo 9:20).

12609.text: Face AJ. Jesus' own distress and reverence (2 / 2 hits and verses, units 4): | Mar 14:33; Heb 5:7

12619.text: Face C. Spoken against ("Fear not") (153 / 139 hits and verses, units 1–4): Nearly always with a ground

12621.text: Face I. Not fearing (30 / 29 hits and verses, units 1–4): Of God, or of consequence; by faith not afraid

12624.text: Face D. Fearing God as a standing (177 / 170 hits and verses, units 1–4): Commanded, learned, given, owed, lived

12625.text: Face T. Called for (24 / 20 hits and verses, units 2–4): A summons or decree

12636.text: What it is turned toward: The same people, the same root: "they feared greatly" at Egypt; after the crossing, "the people feared the Lord, and they believed". In the boat: afraid in the storm, then "filled with great fear" and "Who then is this". "do not fear what they fear … Let him be your fear"

12638.text: Who speaks "fear not", and on what ground: God: "for I am with you"; Jesus: "it is I"; an angel: "for your prayer has been heard". Jael: "do not be afraid", before the tent peg

12643.text: Who meets it: one event, two responses: "When justice is done, it is a joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers"; one scroll, the officials "turned one to another in fear", "neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid"; "people fainting with fear" and "straighten up and raise your heads"

12649.text: One root, many renderings: rāgaz (to tremble) rendered "Be angry", "deeply moved", "quarrel"; paḥad (to dread) rendered "thrill"; phobos (fear) rendered "terror", "respect", "reverence", "awe"; ekthambeō (to be alarmed) rendered "greatly amazed", "troubled", "alarmed"; eulabeomai (to be reverent) rendered "afraid", "reverent fear"

12651.text: Forbidden and asked for, close together: "Have no fear of them" … "with gentleness and respect"; "do not fear what they fear" … "Let him be your fear"

12667.text: Fear leads to sending away: "asked him to depart from them"; Felix: "Go away for the present"

12683.text: Fear and Wickedness (M58); righteousness (M12): Fear of God joined with turning from evil; justice "a joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers" (verses shared or near: 44 / 22; 52 / 32).

12692.text: Fear and Turning and repentance (M11): Fear among the fruits of "godly grief" that "produces a repentance" (verses shared or near: 24 / 10).

12700.text: Face C. Spoken against (5 / 5 hits and verses; surfaces intimidated · afraid · fear · amazed): Each with a ground: the judgment is God's; the word did not come true; "Is there a God besides me?"; a higher watcher.

12706.text: Face K. Terror that comes upon (17 / 17 hits and verses; surfaces terror · terrors · dread · dreads · fears · horror · dismay · confusion · panic · anguish · afraid): Comes as event, curse, cup, stroke on the mind; once instead of the peace looked for.

12707.text: Face L. None to make afraid (1 / 1 hits and verses; surfaces terror): Promised: "it shall not come near you".

12726.text: Face J. Other (no fear in the English) (3 / 3 hits and verses; surfaces oppression · gullies · barn): Data only.

12727.text: Who meets it: one event, joy to one and terror to another.

12738.text: Face B. Felt before God's presence, act or word, or a messenger (21 / 19 hits and verses; surfaces fear · afraid · terrified · terror · frightened · alarmed · trembled · tremble · trembling · awe): An angel; the voice from the cloud; the burning bush; Sinai; an act of judgment heard of; a word about judgment.

12739.text: Face C. Spoken against (33 / 32 hits and verses; surfaces Fear [not] · afraid · fear · frightened · terrified · alarmed): Spoken by Jesus, an angel, the Lord in a vision, Peter, Paul, a letter; once self-spoken. Nearly always with a ground.

12740.text: Face D. Fearing God as a standing (20 / 19 hits and verses; surfaces fear · fears · feared · fearing · reverence · reverent fear · awe): God-fearing as a description of a person; walking, conduct, holiness, worship.

12741.text: Face E. Awe, respect or reverence toward people (7 / 6 hits and verses; surfaces respect · respectful · respects · feared): The fear root rendered "respect": to rulers, masters, husbands, any who ask; Herod toward John.

12744.text: Face J. Other (rendered as a manner of acting) (2 / 2 hits and verses; surfaces reverent · godliness): No fear in the English.

12751.text: Face AJ. Jesus' own distress and reverence (2 / 2 hits and verses; surfaces troubled · reverence): Gethsemane; "heard because of his reverence".

12757.text: G5401 phobos (46): fear 35 (+ Fear) · respect 3 · respect is owed · respectful · reverence (Eph 5:21) · awe 2 (Luk 5:26; Act 2:43) · terror (Rom 13:3). Terror and respect in one passage: Rom 13:3 and 13:7 (FE-122).

12759.text: G2125 eulabeomai (2): afraid (Act 23:10, a tribune) · reverent fear (Heb 11:7, Noah). Fear for a prisoner's life; reverence that builds an ark.

12764.text: Forbidden and asked for, two verses apart: "Have no fear of them" … "with gentleness and respect".

12766.text: What fear before the holy leads to: glorifying God, or "depart".

12770.text: One root, reverence and fear for a life: Noah's "reverent fear"; a tribune "afraid".

12787.text: Psa 103:8-18 says "those who fear him" three times: the love "as high as the heavens" (103:11), the Father's compassion (103:13), and the steadfast love "from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him" (103:17).

12790.text: Psa 103:17-18 joins fear to keeping and remembering: those who fear him are "those who keep his covenant and remember to do his commandments".

12795.text: The root ḥûl, "to twist, whirl", is rendered as trembling, of the earth and of people: "tremble before him, all the earth" (Psa 96:9); "who shall hear the report of you and shall tremble and be in anguish because of you" (Deu 2:25).

12799.text: The root ḥûl, "to twist, whirl", is rendered as dance, whirl, storm: the daughters of Shiloh "dance in the dances" (Judg 21:21); "a whirling tempest" (Jer 23:19).

12817.text: Fear and M48 Astonishment & Wonder: in 13 verses (7 within three words) the commonest near pairs are revere + wonder (Exo 15:11, Psa 139:14, Mar 16:8).

12819.text: H3372H "to fear: revere" is rendered awesome (20): Deu 7:21, Deu 10:17, Neh 1:5, Psa 66:3, Psa 99:3, Gen 28:17 ….

12822.text: H3372H "to fear: revere" is rendered reverence (2): Lev 19:30, 26:2.

12833.text: The Greek fear words G5401 and G5399 is rendered respect: Rom 13:7, 1Pe 2:18, 3:15.

12836.text: The Greek fear words G5401 and G5399 is rendered reverence: Eph 5:21.

12857.text: H6343 "dread" is rendered "in great terror": Psa 14:5, 53:5.

12866.text: H6125 is tagged M01 but the English renders another face: oppression (Psa 55:3).

12876.text: The inner word is often named in the other party, or in the contrast figure: the opponents' hardened heart (Mar 3:5); the builders' "mind to work" (Neh 4:6); "his heart is steady" (Psa 112:8); Daniel "resolved" (Dan 1:8); Stephen "full of the Holy Spirit" (Act 7:55).

12880.text: The heavy hand is felt from beneath, and the text corrects the feeling: "he does not afflict from his heart"; "I knew you to be a hard man", said from fear and condemned; the heaviness ended at confession.

12884.text: Nations rage and peoples plot, in one line.

12895.text: Face of aph (H0639), The face lifted in pride: The face/nose raised (Psa 10:4 ("In the pride of his face the wicked does not seek him")). Pride is the nose held high (S, lexical).

12898.text: Face of aph (H0639), Smoke in God's nostrils: Said of those who say "I am too holy for you" (Isa 65:5). Self-holiness is what God's nostrils cannot bear (S).

12901.text: charah (H2734): anger kindled · "fret" = heat yourself (Gen 4:5; Jon 4:1, 4, 9; Psa 37:1, 7, 8; Pro 24:19). Turned on another, it burns outward. Turned inward at the wicked's success, it "tends only to evil" (S).

12904.text: za'am (H2194/2195): indignation · to denounce or curse (Num 23:7–8; Pro 24:24; Isa 10:5). Void when it goes beyond God's verdict (Balaam); valid when it follows justice (Pro 24:24) (S).

12908.text: orgē / orgizō: human anger to be put away · "be angry and do not sin" · Jesus's anger · God's wrath revealed, stored, remaining · the authority as God's servant of wrath · "leave it to the wrath of God" (Col 3:8; Eph 4:26; Mar 3:5; Rom 1:18; 2:5; Joh 3:36; Rom 13:4; 12:19). Who bears it, and what it serves. Jesus's anger heals; the same chapter's opponents plot (S).

12911.text: aganakteō / -ēsis: the disciples indignant at waste, at rivals · Jesus indignant for the children · indignation as the fruit of godly grief (Mat 26:8; 20:24; Mar 10:14; 2Co 7:11). On behalf of a norm, a rival, a child, or one's own wrong (S).

12916.text: Factor Heart state: Confirmed. the lifted heart before anger (2Ch 26:16); the heart already set (Dan 11:28); the godless heart that cherishes it (Job 36:13).

12919.text: Factor What comes back: Confirmed. the cup comes round (Hab 2:16); provocation shames the provoker (Jer 7:19); "the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God" (Jam 1:20).

12934.text: It moves and has a span: "wrath has gone out against you from the Lord"; "For his anger is but for a moment, and his favor is for a lifetime"; "with them the wrath of God is finished"; "the wrath of God remains on him"; Edom "kept his wrath forever".

12936.text: It is drunk: "you who have drunk from the hand of the Lord the cup of his wrath"; "he also will drink the wine of God's wrath, poured full strength into the cup of his anger".

12937.text: What human anger is said to do and not do: "for the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God"; "anger lodges in the heart of fools"; "Cursed be their anger, for it is fierce, and their wrath, for it is cruel!"; "Wrath is cruel, anger is overwhelming, but who can stand before jealousy?".

12939.text: God's anger named with who God is: "The Lord, the Lord, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger"; "I will not execute my burning anger … for I am God and not a man"; "until he has executed and accomplished the intents of his heart"; "I have no wrath".

12940.text: Named by its absence: "lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling"; love "is not irritable or resentful"; the overseer "must not be arrogant or quick-tempered".

12942.text: The verses speak of anger in the same words for God and for people, and keep some words almost wholly for God (ḥārôn, zaʿam, qeṣep̄, and orgē in the Greek); the same pictures (kindled, burning, poured, drunk) are used on both sides, and where the verses mark a difference they mark it in restraint: "for I am God and not a man" (Hos 11:9).

12943.text: Form of anger, With his people, or with those who do wrong: the cause named (144 / 94 hits and verses; faces A, 2A, 3A, 4A, 5A; units 1–5).

12945.text: Form of anger, Restrained, held back, turned; for a moment (31 / 23 hits and verses; faces D, 2F, 3D, 4F; units 1–4).

12947.text: Form of anger, The day of wrath; the wrath to come, and deliverance (19 / 19 hits and verses; faces 4J, 5C, 5F; units 4, 5).

12948.text: Form of anger, The cup, the winepress, the bowls (16 / 13 hits and verses; faces 2H, 5G; units 2, 5).

12953.text: Form of anger, On the false prophets and the wicked (the storm) (5 / 4 hits and verses; faces 2B; units 2).

12959.text: Form of anger, Meribah: the quarrel kept in a place (11 / 9 hits and verses; faces 4O; units 4).

12977.text: Form of anger, Indignation: for one wronged, at waste, at good done, at idols, at one's own wrong (19 / 16 hits and verses; faces R, 3N, 2U, 5Q, 5S, 5U, 5V; units 1–3, 5).

12978.text: Form of anger, Put away and governed (the Greek lists and sayings) (19 / 13 hits and verses; faces 5L, 5M; units 5).

12987.text: Form of anger, "Fret not yourself" (4 / 4 hits and verses; faces 3W; units 3).

12990.text: Form of anger, Against one suspected or set against (4 / 4 hits and verses; faces 4S; units 4).

12997.text: Who is angry: The same words for God and people; some words kept for God (part A). In restraint God sets himself against a man: "for I am God and not a man".

13001.text: What it is joined with in the verse: Jealousy (Deu 6:15); grief: Jonathan "was grieved for David", Jesus "looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart"; the Spirit (1Sa 11:6); "the anger and envy that you showed because of your hatred" (Eze 35:11); fear: "he shall be afraid and withdraw, and shall turn back and be enraged"; compassion set against it (Hos 11:8–9).

13011.text: The same words in different settings: One storm sentence among the false prophets and among the promises (Jer 23:19 = 30:23); the Exodus "a mighty hand and an outstretched arm" with "wrath poured out" added, aimed at Israel; provocation as threat and as a question inside a lament ("Why have they provoked me to anger with their carved images"); kaʿas as what "kills the fool" and as the "Sorrow" that "is better than laughter".

13013.text: One root, different things: ʾaph: "pressing the nose produces blood, and pressing anger produces strife"; ḥēmāh: wrath, "the venom of asps", "the heat of wine"; ʿebrāh: wrath and "arrogant pride"; zāʿam: anger and "How can I denounce"; zāʿap̄: Uzziah's anger and "Why are your faces downcast today?"; ʿāšan: "Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke" and "Why does your anger smoke"; kāʿas: provoking God and Hannah's "vexation"; thymos: God's "wrath" and Babylon's "passion"; paroxysmos: "a sharp disagreement" and "stir up one another to love".

13016.text: The measure: "to increase still more the fierce anger of the Lord"; "Ahab did more to provoke the Lord … than all the kings"; "storing up wrath for yourself"; "so as always to fill up the measure of their sins" is the setting of "wrath has come upon them at last".

13020.text: Prayer and anger meet (v2, U2 §65 points 5 and 7): "how long will you be angry with your people's prayers?"; "you have wrapped yourself with a cloud so that no prayer can pass through"; "As for you, do not pray for this people"; "There is no one who calls upon your name"; "As I called, and they would not hear, so they called, and I would not hear"; "we do not present our pleas before you because of our righteousness, but because of your great mercy".

13049.text: A person's anger leads to not the righteousness of God; judgment: "for the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God"; "everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment".

13050.text: A person's anger leads to shame, for the incensed: "to him shall come and be ashamed all who were incensed against him".

13052.text: The same outcome is named on both sides: terror or fear (Psa 2:5; 2Sa 6:9), shame (Jer 12:13; Isa 45:24), and the body (Psa 38:3; 1Ki 21:4); no verse draws the parallel.

13107.text: Sequence in 2Ch 26:16–21: strength → "he grew proud" (Hebrew his heart was lifted up) → trespass → withstood → anger → leprosy in the act.

13111.text: Sequence in Job 32:1–20: the friends fall silent → anger ×3 → waiting from deference and fear → "the spirit in man" → belly like wine with no vent → "I must speak, that I may find relief".

13112.text: Sequence in Psa 37:1–9: seeing the wicked prosper → heating oneself (fret) + envy → "trust … commit … be still … wait" → "refrain from anger" → the wicked fade, the waiting inherit.

13113.text: Sequence in Psa 55:3–5: the enemy's noise → their anger bears a grudge → "my heart is in anguish within me" → terrors of death → fear and trembling.

13123.text: Sequence in Act 7:53–58: accusation heard → sawn through in their hearts → teeth ground → Stephen full of the Spirit sees glory → they stop their ears → rush, cast out, stone.

13125.text: Sequence in Exo 32:10–14; Deu 9:7–22: provocation → anger → "let me alone" → intercession from fear, with fasting → relented → the memory made into a warning against self-righteousness.

13137.text: Sequence in Psa 106:19–45: forgot God → Moses in the breach → despised the land → Peor → Phinehas, "counted to him as righteousness" → Meribah, Moses' loss → child sacrifice → given to nations → "he heard their cry … relented".

13139.text: Sequence in Isa 9:8–10:7: pride in rebuilding → struck → "did not turn" → leaders mislead → self-devouring → "his hand is stretched out still" (×5) → Assyria as rod, with a heart of its own.

13141.text: Sequence in Isa 57:14–18: God dwells with the contrite spirit → "nor will I always be angry; for the spirit would grow faint before me" → struck, hid face → backsliding "in the way of his own heart" → "I will heal him".

13142.text: Sequence in Isa 63:1–64:12: no one to help → God's arm alone → "I will recount the steadfast love" → "you were angry, and we sinned" → no one who calls → "we are the clay … please look".

13150.text: Sequence in Eze 22:17–31: dross → melted in the furnace → every rank has failed → "I sought for a man … and stand in the breach … but I found none" → indignation poured out.

13153.text: Sequence in Rom 1:16–2:10: gospel, righteousness by faith → wrath revealed against suppression of the truth → without excuse → judging others → presuming on kindness → hard heart storing up wrath → to each by works.

13169.text: Anger and Fear (M01): Moses afraid of the anger, and heard; afraid, then enraged; angry, then afraid; "do not fear" at another's fierce anger; "not being afraid of the anger of the king"; indignation and fear in one verse.

13171.text: Anger and Prayer (M42): "how long will you be angry with your people's prayers?"; Samuel "cried to the Lord all night"; "lifting holy hands without anger".

13172.text: Anger and Grief and lament (M03): "grieved for David"; "with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart"; a lament raised for "the generation of his wrath"; the provocation asked about inside a lament; godly grief produced indignation; kaʿas rendered "grief".

13176.text: Anger and Turning and repentance (M11): "Who knows? God may turn and relent"; "when he humbled himself the wrath of the Lord turned from him"; "Bear fruit in keeping with repentance"; godly grief "produces a repentance".

13192.text: Anger and Turning (M11), side by side with fear: fear side, fear among the fruits of godly grief (2Cor 7:10–11); anger side, godly grief "produces a repentance", and indignation (2Cor 7:10–11).

13194.text: Anger and Each other, side by side with fear: fear side, rāgaz (to tremble) rendered "Be angry" (Psa 4:4); fear and wrath in one verse (Psa 90:11); anger side, Moses afraid of the anger (Deu 9:19); afraid, then enraged (Dan 11:30); not afraid of the king's anger (Heb 11:27).

13195.text: The two strands share a verse in Deu 9:19, Psa 90:11, Dan 11:30 and Heb 11:27, and in 2Cor 7:11, where indignation and fear stand in one list.

13196.text: What sets God's anger off: broke the covenant → anger → given over (Judg 2:14, 20); heard → anger → fire (Num 11:1); hearts diamond-hard, lest they hear → therefore great anger (Zec 7:12); blood left uncovered → wrath roused (Eze 24:8); mocking the messengers → wrath rose → no remedy (2Ch 36:16); proud heart → wrath came (2Ch 32:25); suppress the truth → wrath revealed (Rom 1:18).

13197.text: What sets a person's anger off: demand → anger → "Am I in the place of God" (Gen 30:1–2); no regard → very angry → face fell (Gen 4:5); saw no homage → filled with fury → sought to destroy all the Jews (Est 3:5–6); "I thought" → rage (2Ki 5:11–12); afraid → withdraw → enraged (Dan 11:30); heard → filled with wrath → drove him out (Luk 4:28–29); passions at war within → quarrels (Jam 4:1).

13199.text: What restrains it, by the verse's reason: compassionate → did not stir up all his wrath (Psa 78:38); "I said I would pour out my wrath" → acted for my name (Eze 20:8–9); heart recoils → will not execute burning anger, for I am God and not a man (Hos 11:8–9); not always angry, for the spirit would grow faint (Isa 57:16); feared the enemy's provocation → not wiped out (Deu 32:26–27).

13203.text: What turns or settles a person's anger: soft answer → wrath turned (Pro 15:1); good sense → slow to anger (Pro 19:11); Aaron's answer → Moses heard → approved (Lev 10:16–20); servants' question → dipped → flesh restored (2Ki 5:13–14); poured out her soul, "Go in peace" → ate, face no longer sad (1Sa 1:15–18); sold me → angry with yourselves → do not, for God sent me (Gen 45:5); remember your brother has something against you → first be reconciled (Mat 5:23–24).
