19535.text: Act 6:5 | order (people choose by what is seen; "full" through to death); set against (accusers); opposition | batch 2

19536.text: Eph 1:4 | order (before the foundation; holiness as purpose; love is God's); faith and knowing (eyes of the heart); before whom; what changes the character (holiness) | batch 2

19537.text: Col 3:12 | called to (put on, turned to others); what changes the character (holiness as a name) | batch 2

19539.text: Tit 1:1 | faith and knowing (knowledge that accords with godliness); set against (profess and deny; minds defiled) | batch 2

19544.text: Choice: Joshua chooses first: *"as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord"* (v15).; The people choose the Lord, giving the reason from what he did: *"it is the Lord our God who brought us … up from the land of Egypt"* (v17); *"Therefore we also will serve the Lord, for he is our God"* (v18).; Joshua answers *"You are not able to serve the Lord, for he is a holy God"* (v19). They repeat the choice: *"No, but we will serve the Lord"* (v21).

19550.text: Choice: *"what they said pleased the whole gathering, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip …"* (v5). The pleasure is the gathering's response to the twelve's word, and the choosing follows it.

19553.text: Choice: *"it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch"*. The men are *"Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas"* (v22).; In the letter: *"it has seemed good to us, having come to one accord, to choose men and send them"* (v25).; The same verb then carries the content of the letter: *"it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us"* (v28).

19564.text: Led to: The Lord's character: *"Good and upright is the Lord; therefore he instructs sinners in the way"* (v8).; The person's fear: *"Who is the man who fears the Lord? Him will he instruct in the way that he should choose"* (v12).; The psalmist's own plea just before: *"pardon my guilt, for it is great"* (v11).

19569.text: Led to: *"you who forsake the Lord, who forget my holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune"* (v11).; *"when I called, you did not answer; when I spoke, you did not listen"* (v12).

19586.text: Outcome: Elihu gives his own verdict at once: *"far be it from God that he should do wickedness"* (v10). The verse does not record the others' choice.

19591.text: Outcome: Given as the reason: *"for the devious person is an abomination to the Lord, but the upright are in his confidence"* (v32). The next verses set the Lord's curse and blessing side by side (v33–35).

19606.text: Psalm 105:43: "his chosen ones with singing": Psalm 105 is a call to remember. It is addressed to the chosen: *"Remember the wondrous works that he has done … O offspring of Abraham, his servant, children of Jacob, his chosen ones!"* (v5–6). It starts with the heart: *"let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice!"* (v3).; The psalm's reason is God's own remembering: *"He remembers his covenant forever"* (v8); *"For he remembered his holy promise, and Abraham, his servant"* (v42); The verse follows straight on: *"So he brought his people out with joy, his chosen ones with singing"* (v43). The joy and singing are set on the people brought out. They come with being brought out, and the bringing out comes from God remembering his promise. The chosen are told to remember (v5) because he remembered (v8, v42).; On the way there the psalm tells one man's inward testing: *"His feet were hurt with fetters … until what he had said came to pass, the word of the Lord tested him"* (v18–19). That man was Joseph, sent ahead of the chosen.; Psalm 105 tells nothing of the people's failures. It has *"none among his tribes who stumbled"* (v37). Its last verse states the purpose of the whole: *"that they might keep his statutes and observe his laws"* (v45).

19611.text: What the chosen are moved to: celebrating (2Sa 6:21); being strong in keeping (1Ch 28:7, 10); satisfaction in the goodness of God's house (Psa 65:4); joy and singing (Psa 105:43); gladness, which another asks to share (Psa 106:5); knowing, believing and understanding (Isa 43:10); not fearing (Isa 44:2); In 2Sa 6:21, 1Ch 28:10, Isa 43:10 and Isa 44:2 the verse names the being chosen as the ground or the reason. In Psa 65:4 the response follows the choosing in the same sentence. In Psa 105:43 and 106:5, "chosen ones" names the people whose joy it is; the verse does not make the choosing the cause.

19612.text: Being chosen comes before the inner act, not after it. In §2a, knowing, fear and teaching came before a person's own choosing (Isa 7:15; Psa 25:12). In Isaiah 43:10, God chooses first, and knowing is the purpose. The chosen were blind and deaf when chosen (43:8). In Psalm 65 they were chosen after their iniquity was atoned for (v3–4).

19613.text: Being chosen is not a guarantee. This is stated in the verses, not inferred: the condition put on Solomon, and the *"cast you off forever"* (1Ch 28:7, 9); the chosen people's forgetting, craving, jealousy and unbelief, and their despising the land (Psa 106:7–43); the chosen people weary of God, and not calling on him (Isa 43:22–24); In Psalm 106:24 the chosen *"despised"* (H3988A) what was given. This is the same word as the refusing in §2a.

19614.text: The return is the Lord's remembering. He remembered his covenant at their cry (Psa 106:44–45). He remembered his promise and brought them out with joy (Psa 105:42–43). He blots out their sins and will not remember them (Isa 43:25). The chosen are called to remember in turn (Psa 105:5; Isa 44:21).

19620.text: For batch 2: the 8 New Testament verses. In five of them (Eph 1:4, 2Th 2:13, Tit 1:1, Jam 2:5, 2Pe 1:10) the inner act is given as the purpose of the choosing, or as the call that follows it. Whether they keep the order seen in Isaiah 43:10, with the choosing first and the knowing after, is to be read from them.

19621.text: Numbers 17:5: "Thus I will make to cease from me the grumblings of the people of Israel": The verse closes a long dispute over who God has chosen. It begins in Numbers 16. Korah and 250 chiefs, *"chosen from the assembly, well-known men"* (16:2; *qārîʾ*, H7148, "called"), rise up: *"Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the Lord?"* (16:3). Moses answers with God's choosing: *"The one whom he chooses he will bring near to him"* (16:5), and *"the man whom the Lord chooses shall be the holy one"* (16:7).; Moses names what is underneath the complaint: *"is it too small a thing for you that the God of Israel has separated you … And would you seek the priesthood also?"* (16:9–10). What they already have is not enough. They seek more.; *"Therefore it is against the Lord that you and all your company have gathered together. What is Aaron that you grumble against him?"* (16:11). The grumbling at Aaron is against the Lord.; Psalm 106 names the same event with an inner word: *"When men in the camp were jealous of Moses and Aaron, the holy one of the Lord, the earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram"* (Psa 106:16–17).; Moses himself is *"very angry"* (16:15). The rebels are judged (16:31–35). The next day *"all the congregation of the people of Israel grumbled against Moses and against Aaron, saying, 'You have killed the people of the Lord'"* (16:41). A plague begins, and Aaron *"stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped"* (16:48).; Then God settles it with the staffs: *"And the staff of the man whom I choose shall sprout. Thus I will make to cease from me the grumblings of the people of Israel, which they grumble against you"* (17:5). The grumbling is against Moses and Aaron, and God calls it *"from me"*. In v10 it is *"their grumblings against me"*. The staff is kept *"as a sign for the rebels, that you may make an end of their grumblings against me, lest they die"* (17:10).; The grumbling turns to terror: *"Behold, we perish, we are undone, we are all undone. Everyone who comes near … shall die. Are we all to perish?"* (17:12–13).; "Grumble" is *lûn* (H3885B). The verse shows it as spoken complaint. I read the inner side from the passage: the seeking of the priesthood (16:10), and the jealousy that Psalm 106:16 names.

19624.text: 1 Samuel 20:30: "do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame": The chapter is the covenant between Jonathan and David, tested at Saul's table. Before the meal it says what binds the two men: *"Whatever you say, I will do for you"* (v4); *"you have brought your servant into a covenant of the Lord with you"* (v8); *"And Jonathan made David swear again by his love for him, for he loved him as he loved his own soul"* (v17); David knows Saul's mind before Jonathan does: *"Your father knows well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he thinks, 'Do not let Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved'"* (v3). Jonathan will not believe it: *"Far from it! … my father does nothing either great or small without disclosing it to me"* (v2). The test is set by Saul's anger: *"if he is angry, then know that harm is determined by him"* (v7).; At the table: *"Then Saul's anger was kindled against Jonathan, and he said to him, 'You son of a perverse, rebellious woman, do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame, and to the shame of your mother's nakedness?'"* (v30).; Saul names the choice and calls it shame. He gives the reason in the next verse: *"For as long as the son of Jesse lives on the earth, neither you nor your kingdom shall be established. Therefore send and bring him to me, for he shall surely die"* (v31). What Saul fears for is the kingdom of his house.; When Jonathan asks *"Why should he be put to death? What has he done?"* (v32), Saul turns his spear on his own son (v33). Now Jonathan knows: *"So Jonathan knew that his father was determined to put David to death"* (v33).; Jonathan's own anger follows: *"And Jonathan rose from the table in fierce anger and ate no food the second day of the month, for he was grieved for David, because his father had disgraced him"* (v34). His anger is not for himself, though the spear was thrown at him. It is grief for David.; The chapter ends with the two men weeping together and with the oath: *"we have sworn both of us in the name of the Lord, saying, 'The Lord shall be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring, forever'"* (v42).

19625.text: For OT-62 (anger and will together): Saul's anger is kindled at his son's choice. The chapter gives its reason: Jonathan's choice threatens Saul's kingdom (v31).; The anger speaks first in shame and insult (v30), then becomes a death sentence (v31), then a spear at his own son (v33).; Jonathan's anger answers it. It comes from grief for the one he chose, not from the attack on himself (v34).; The choice holds. Jonathan keeps it through his father's anger, and seals it by an oath before the Lord (v42).

19626.text: What this verse shows of others around the choosing: A choice made in love (v17) is named by another as shame (v30).; The other's anger rests on what the choice costs him: his house and kingdom (v31).; Knowing passes between the people in the chapter: Saul knows Jonathan's choice (v30), David knows Saul's mind (v3), and at last Jonathan knows it (v33).; The one who chose suffers for it, and holds to it.

19635.text: Proverbs 10:20: "The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; the heart of the wicked is of little worth": "Choice" is *bāḥar* (H0977) as a description: tried, refined silver. No one chooses in the verse. The proverbs around it are about speech: *"The one who conceals hatred has lying lips"* (v18), *"whoever restrains his lips is prudent"* (v19), *"The lips of the righteous feed many"* (v21).; The researcher ruled on Proverbs 8:10 (F2) that it is not HIB as choosing, because "choice" describes the gold. The same holds here: "choice" describes the tongue.; The heart is in the verse, weighed: *"of little worth"*. It is set against the tongue of the righteous.

19637.text: Isaiah 49:7: "to one deeply despised, abhorred by the nation … because of the Lord, who is faithful … who has chosen you": The servant speaks first: *"The Lord called me from the womb, from the body of my mother he named my name"* (v1). He also speaks of his own discouragement and his trust in the same breath: *"But I said, 'I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my right is with the Lord, and my recompense with my God'"* (v4).; Then the Lord speaks *"to one deeply despised, abhorred by the nation, the servant of rulers: 'Kings shall see and arise; princes, and they shall prostrate themselves; because of the Lord, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you'"* (v7).; The others' inner acts are two: *"deeply despised"*: *bāzâ* (H0959) with the soul (*nepeš*, H5315J). It is the same verb as Michal's *"despised him in her heart"* (2Sa 6:16). The ESV renders the phrase "deeply despised". The text does not settle whose soul is meant.; *"abhorred by the nation"*: *tāʿab* (*to abhor*; H8581); Set against both: kings will see and rise, and princes will bow. The verse gives the reason in two parts: *"because of the Lord, who is faithful"*, and *"who has chosen you"*.

19642.text: What others do around a choice, in these verses: grumble against the chosen man, and God counts it as against himself (Num 16:11; 17:5, 10); seek more than they were given, and are jealous (Num 16:10; Psa 106:16); name a choice as shame, and are angry at what it costs them (1Sa 20:30–31); despise the chosen in the heart, by the eyes of people (2Sa 6:16, 20); despise and abhor the chosen servant (Isa 49:7); conclude from the chosen people's ruin that God rejected them, and despise them in their own sight (Jer 33:24); ask to share the joy of the chosen (Psa 106:5); not know God, and still be called and equipped for the sake of the chosen (Isa 45:4–5); offer an inner act, the humbling of the soul, that God's choosing weighs and does not accept (Isa 58:3–5)

19646.text: Not about choosing: Judg 20:34 and Pro 10:20. Each has an inner-being note for another section (knowing and fear; speaking), noted and not placed.

19663.text: Kept open: The offer to turn stands inside the charge: *"let us reason together"* (1:18) and *"those in her who repent"* (1:27). A wrong choice does not close the matter.

19664.text: Psalm 25:12 — "Him will he instruct in the way that he should choose": The psalm is a prayer from someone in trouble. It begins *"To you, O Lord, I lift up my soul"*; *"O my God, in you I trust; let me not be put to shame"* (v1–2). It ends with that same person *"lonely and afflicted"*. Among the trouble: *"The troubles of my heart are enlarged"* (v17); *"how many are my foes, and with what violent hatred they hate me"* (v19); *"guard my soul … Let me not be put to shame"* (v20); Running through the whole psalm is the person's own guilt: *"Remember not the sins of my youth or my transgressions"* (v7); *"pardon my guilt, for it is great"* (v11); *"forgive all my sins"* (v18); The person who asks about the way is a sinner, and says so.; Before the verse about choosing, the psalmist asks for the way three times over: *"Make me to know your ways, O Lord; teach me your paths"* (v4); *"Lead me in your truth and teach me"* (v5); Then he says why he can expect it, from who the Lord is: *"Good and upright is the Lord; therefore he instructs sinners in the way. He leads the humble in what is right, and teaches the humble his way"* (v8–9). The Lord's instructing comes out of his goodness. It is given to sinners and to the humble.; Then comes the verse: *"Who is the man who fears the Lord? Him will he instruct in the way that he should choose"* (v12). The word "instruct" is the same in v8 and v12 (H3384B). The person who chooses here does not make up the way. The way to choose is taught, and the one who is taught it is the one who fears the Lord. The fear comes first, then the teaching, then the choice. The verse does not say the man chooses well on his own; it says the Lord instructs him in what he should choose.; What follows the choice is stated: *"His soul shall abide in well-being, and his offspring shall inherit the land"* (v13). "Well-being" here (H2896B) is the same word as *"the good"* in Isaiah 7:15, *"refuse the evil and choose the good"*. The man taught the way he should choose has his soul *"abide"*, lodge or stay, in the good.; *"The friendship of the Lord is for those who fear him, and he makes known to them his covenant"* (v14). The teaching goes further than a direction to take. The one who fears the Lord is brought into his friendship, and the covenant is made known (H3045, "know", as in v4).

19666.text: Isaiah 56:4 — "who choose the things that please me and hold fast my covenant": The oracle opens with a command and a reason: *"Keep justice, and do righteousness, for soon my salvation will come, and my righteousness be revealed"* (v1). Then a blessing on the one who *"holds it fast, who keeps the Sabbath, not profaning it, and keeps his hand from doing any evil"* (v2). The holding fast and the keeping from evil are already there before the choosing verse.; The verse is addressed to two people who speak about themselves: *"Let not the foreigner who has joined himself to the Lord say"*, *"The Lord will surely separate me from his people"*; *"let not the eunuch say"*, *"Behold, I am a dry tree"* (v3); Each one has a judgement about himself: shut out, and fruitless. The foreigner expects to be separated. The eunuch sees himself as a tree with no sap and no fruit, with no sons and daughters to carry his name. The Lord tells them both not to say it.; Then he describes the eunuchs he means: *"who keep my Sabbaths, who choose the things that please me and hold fast my covenant"* (v4). The word "please" is H2654A, the same word as *"delight"* in Isaiah 65:12 and 66:4 (*"chose what I did not delight in"*, *"chose that in which I did not delight"*). Here the choosing goes the other way. These choose what the Lord delights in. The measure is the same as in those two oracles, the Lord's delight, and here it is met.; The choosing stands between keeping and holding fast: *"keep my Sabbaths"*; *"choose the things that please me"*; *"hold fast my covenant"* (H2388H, the same word as *"holds it fast"* in v2); The choice is not one moment. It sits inside a keeping and a holding on.; The Lord's answer goes straight to what the eunuch said about himself: *"I will give in my house and within my walls a monument and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name that shall not be cut off"* (v5). The man who called himself a dry tree is given a name that outlasts children. The foreigner who feared being separated is brought in: *"these I will bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted"* (v7).

19667.text: Isaiah 56:4 — "who choose the things that please me and hold fast my covenant": The foreigners are described in inner terms as well: they *"join themselves to the Lord, to minister to him, to love the name of the Lord, and to be his servants"* (v6). Love of the name stands with the keeping and the holding fast.; What follows in the chapter is the opposite. Israel's own watchmen *"are all without knowledge"*. They are *"shepherds who have no understanding; they have all turned to their own way, each to his own gain"* (v10–11). "Their own way" is the same phrase as in Isaiah 66:3, *"These have chosen their own ways"* (H1870G). The outsiders who choose what the Lord delights in are brought in. The insiders turn to their own way.

19669.text: The way to choose is taught (Psa 25:8, 12). The Lord instructs sinners and the humble out of his goodness, and the one who fears him is taught *"the way that he should choose"*. This stands beside Psalm 119:29, where the psalmist asks God to put the false way far off. In both psalms the chooser does not stand alone.

19673.text: The choice is held, not just made. It is set between keeping and holding fast (Isa 56:2, 4, 6), and between eyes turned to the Lord and waiting (Psa 25:15, 21). This sits with the test readings: the heart inclined after the choice (Jos 24:23), and clinging to the testimonies (Psa 119:31).

19675.text: Outcomes reach the inner being on the right side too. Batch 1 recorded shame and fears for the wrong choice. Here: the soul abides in the good, and is given friendship with the Lord and the knowing of his covenant (Psa 25:13–14); joy in his house, and a name not cut off (Isa 56:5, 7)

19676.text: Kept open: Psalm 25 ends still waiting and still in trouble (v16–22). The right choosing does not remove the trouble in the psalm. It is held while waiting.

19677.text: For the next batches: batch 3 is people choosing of their own accord, and choosing together (Deu 23:16, 2Sa 19:38, 2Cor 8:17, Act 6:5, Act 15:22 and 25), with the wisdom sayings Pro 3:31 and 16:16. These are mostly not choices between God and other gods. Whether they show the same tie to what the eyes see, to delight and to knowing is to be read from them.

19682.text: Acts 6:5 — "what they said pleased the whole gathering, and they chose Stephen": The choice is made at a point of division: *"a complaint by the Hellenists arose against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution"* (v1). The twelve do not choose. They give the gathering the choice and the measure for it: *"pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom"* (v3).; The gathering's response is inward before it is an act: *"what they said pleased the whole gathering"* (G0700). Then *"they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit"*, and six others (v5). The choosing comes from the whole gathering being pleased, and it follows the measure they were given: the men are known for what is in them (Spirit, wisdom, faith), not for rank.; The outcome: *"These they set before the apostles, and they prayed and laid their hands on them"* (v6). The narrative goes straight on: *"the word of God continued to increase, and the number of the disciples multiplied greatly"* (v7). It places the increase next to the choosing; it does not say one caused the other.

19683.text: Acts 15:22, 25 — "it seemed good … having come to one accord, to choose men": The choosing ends a dispute that went to the heart of the faith. Some taught *"Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved"* (v1), and there was *"no small dissension and debate"* (v2).; At the council the first word about choosing is God's. Peter says *"Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among you, that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel and believe"* (v7). It is the same verb as the church's later choosing (G1586). He goes on: *"God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them, by giving them the Holy Spirit … having cleansed their hearts by faith"* (v8–9). The assembly *"fell silent"* and *"listened"* (v12). James gives his judgement from the prophets (v13–21).; Then the church chooses: *"it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch"* (v22). The letter says how they came to it: *"it has seemed good to us, having come to one accord, to choose men and send them to you"* (v25). "One accord" (G3661) is a single shared mind. The same verb for "seemed good" (G1380) then joins them to the Spirit: *"it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us"* (v28).; So the church's choosing: follows God's choosing, in the same verb; follows listening in silence; comes from one accord; is joined to what seemed good to the Holy Spirit; The outcome is in the hearers' hearts: *"when they had read it, they rejoiced because of its encouragement"* (v31). Judas and Silas *"encouraged and strengthened the brothers"* (v32), and were *"sent off in peace"* (v33). The letter answers the *"unsettling"* of their *"minds"* (v24).

19689.text: Choosing together. The church chooses out of a shared inward response (*"pleased the whole gathering"*) and in *"one accord"*. Its choosing follows God's own choosing, uses the same verb, and is joined to what *"seemed good to the Holy Spirit"* (Act 6:5; 15:7, 22, 25, 28). The outcome is in hearts: joy, encouragement, peace.

19693.text: The Lord’s confidence as the outcome. The upright are *"in his confidence"* (Pro 3:32), the same word as *"The friendship of the Lord"* for those who fear him (Psa 25:14).

19701.text: The choice carries God's own presence and attention: "For now I have chosen and consecrated this house that my name may be there forever. My eyes and my heart will be there for all time" (2Ch 7:16).

19704.text: The chosen city can be cast off, and chosen again: "I will cast off this city that I have chosen, Jerusalem" (2Ki 23:27); "the Lord will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem" (Zec 1:17; also Zec 2:12); The choice is named against an accuser: "The Lord who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you!" (Zec 3:2)

19706.text: What the choosing makes them: "a people for his treasured possession" (Deu 7:6, 14:2); "his heritage" (Psa 33:12); "his own possession" (Psa 135:4)

19714.text: Its ground, as the verses state it: "chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before him" (Eph 1:4); "in order that God's purpose of election might continue, not because of works but because of him who calls" (Rom 9:11; said of the twins "not yet born"); "a remnant, chosen by grace" (Rom 11:5); "brothers loved by God, that he has chosen you" (1Th 1:4); "God chose you as the firstfruits to be saved, through sanctification by the Spirit and belief in the truth" (2Th 2:13, G0138)

19715.text: What it makes them: "a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession, that you may proclaim the excellencies of him who called you" (1Pe 2:9). This is near the wording of Deu 7:6.; "Put on then, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience" (Col 3:12). Being chosen is followed by what to put on.

19718.text: Others work for the elect: "Therefore I endure everything for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation" (2Ti 2:10); "for the sake of the faith of God's elect and their knowledge of the truth" (Tit 1:1)

19722.text: Priesthood and Levites: "the Lord your God has chosen him … to stand and minister in the name of the Lord" (Deu 18:5); also Deu 21:5, 1Ch 15:2, 2Ch 29:11; Choosing goes with bringing near: "The one whom he chooses he will bring near to him" (Num 16:5); "Blessed is the one you choose and bring near, to dwell in your courts!" (Psa 65:4).; The choice is shown, not argued: "the staff of the man whom I choose shall sprout" (Num 17:5).

19729.text: 3.6 Jesus chooses (6): "he called his disciples and chose from them twelve, whom he named apostles" (Luk 6:13); "the apostles whom he had chosen" (Act 1:2), given commands "through the Holy Spirit"

19733.text: A fast: "Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of wickedness … to let the oppressed go free" (Isa 58:6), against a fast of bowing the head (Isa 58:5).

19735.text: What is "more acceptable": "To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice" (Pro 21:3, Niphal).

19738.text: Choosing life, the Lord, his ways: "I have set before you life and death … Therefore choose life" (Deu 30:19); "choose this day whom you will serve" (Jos 24:15); the choice is then witnessed: "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the Lord" (Jos 24:22); "I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I set your rules before me" (Psa 119:30); "for I have chosen your precepts" (Psa 119:173); "who choose the things that please me and hold fast my covenant" (Isa 56:4); Preference is stated: "I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of wickedness" (Psa 84:10); Moses: "choosing rather to be mistreated with the people of God than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin" (Heb 11:25, G0138); "Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her" (Luk 10:42), set against her sister's anxiety (narrative 10.1).

19750.text: The church selects men for a task: "what they said pleased the whole gathering, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit" (Act 6:5); "it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, to choose men from among them" (Act 15:22); "having come to one accord, to choose men" (Act 15:25); The verses state the choosing as agreed together.

19753.text: "Choice" as value preferred over another: "To get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver" (Pro 16:16); "A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches" (Pro 22:1); "The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; the heart of the wicked is of little worth" (Pro 10:20); also Pro 8:10, 8:19, Song 5:15

19755.text: 2Ch 7:16 | heart (God's) | "My eyes and my heart will be there for all time"

19759.text: Pro 10:20 | heart | choice silver of the righteous tongue; "the heart of the wicked is of little worth"

19766.text: Act 1:2; Act 6:5 | Spirit | commands "through the Holy Spirit" to the chosen apostles; Stephen "full of faith and of the Holy Spirit"

19772.text: Face: Choosing before birth, not by works (v2); Who: God; Circumstance in the verses: "not yet born … not because of works but because of him who calls"; "before the foundation of the world"; Verses: Rom 9:11, Eph 1:4

19774.text: Face: Choosing to dwell, to put a name; Who: God; Circumstance in the verses: "to make his name dwell there"; "my eyes and my heart will be there"; Verses: Deu 12–16, 2Ch 7:16

19775.text: Face: Choosing that brings near; Who: God; Circumstance in the verses: "whom he chooses he will bring near to him"; Verses: Num 16:5, Psa 65:4

19778.text: Face: Chosen and then told how to live (v2); Who: God, then the person; Circumstance in the verses: "Put on then, as God's chosen ones … compassionate hearts"; "confirm your calling and election"; Verses: Col 3:12, 2Pe 1:10

19790.text: Face: Choosing together, as it seems good (v2); Who: the church; Circumstance in the verses: "pleased the whole gathering"; "it seemed good … having come to one accord"; Verses: Act 6:5, 15:22, 15:25

19800.text: Face: Choosing as preference / worth; Who: person; Circumstance in the verses: "to be chosen rather than silver"; Verses: Pro 16:16, 22:1, Psa 84:10

19812.text: God chooses what he wants (a fast, a response, whom he appoints) (6) | Pro 21:3, Isa 58:6, Jer 49:19, Jer 50:44 | Isa 58:5, Isa 66:4

19815.text: Jesus chooses (6) | Act 1:2 | Luk 6:13, Joh 6:70, Joh 13:18, Joh 15:16, Joh 15:19

19834.text: Act 1:2 | A | Jesus choosing: 13.1 Divine, human, or both?

19837.text: G1586, "choose" (Greek). Used for the gathering choosing the seven (Act 6:5), for the church choosing men to send (Act 15:22, 25), and for God's own choice before them: *"God made a choice among you"* (Act 15:7).

19841.text: Being taught. *"Who is the man who fears the Lord? Him will he instruct in the way that he should choose"* (Psa 25:12). The teaching comes from who the Lord is: *"Good and upright is the Lord; therefore he instructs sinners in the way"* (25:8). The psalmist asks for it: *"Make me to know your ways, O Lord; teach me your paths"* (25:4). In Psalm 119 he asks *"graciously teach me your law"*, and asks God to do the refusing with him: *"Put false ways far from me"* (119:29).

19847.text: Being pleased, and earnestness. In the church at Jerusalem the choosing comes out of a shared inward response: *"what they said pleased the whole gathering, and they chose"* (Act 6:5). Titus goes *"being himself very earnest … of his own accord"* (2Cor 8:17).

19856.text: Own accord, and God at work: Two things are named side by side and not set against each other: *"thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same earnest care I have for you"*; *"being himself very earnest he is going to you of his own accord"* (2Cor 8:16–17); The Macedonians gave *"of their own accord"*, and the order of their giving is set out: *"they gave themselves first to the Lord and then by the will of God to us"* (8:3, 5). The church's choice is joined to the Spirit's in the same verb: *"it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us"* (Act 15:28). The psalmist chooses, and asks God to give the room to carry it out: *"I will run in the way of your commandments when you enlarge my heart!"* (Psa 119:32). I read these verses as saying that what God puts into the heart becomes the person's own. The verses name both and do not explain how they fit.

19857.text: Choosing together: A people can choose as one.; Israel at Shechem: *"we will serve the Lord"*, and they become *"witnesses against yourselves"* (Jos 24:21–22).; The gathering in Jerusalem, out of being pleased (Act 6:5).; The church, *"having come to one accord"* (Act 15:25).; Weighing a case together is also called choosing: *"Let us choose what is right; let us know among ourselves what is good"* (Job 34:4).

19860.text: It is not the same as being able. *"You are not able to serve the Lord, for he is a holy God"* (Jos 24:19).

19864.text: It is held while waiting. *"May integrity and uprightness preserve me, for I wait for you"* (Psa 25:21).

19872.text: When the choice is right, the outcome reaches the inner being: *"His soul shall abide in well-being"* (Psa 25:13). "Well-being" is the same word as *"the good"* in *"choose the good"* (Isa 7:15). I read this as the good that is chosen becoming the place the soul lives.; *"The friendship of the Lord is for those who fear him"* (Psa 25:14). The upright are *"in his confidence"* (Pro 3:32), which is the same word.; *"I will … make them joyful in my house of prayer"* (Isa 56:7).; *"they rejoiced because of its encouragement"*, and Judas and Silas were *"sent off in peace"* (Act 15:31, 33).; Barzillai: *"the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him"* (2Sa 19:39).; The child who refuses the evil and chooses the good eats *"curds and honey"*, the food of *"everyone who is left in the land"* (Isa 7:15, 22). In the other oracle, *"If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land"* (Isa 1:19).

19876.text: What is chosen comes back on the chooser. Each of these is stated in its own verse: They set *"cups of mixed wine for Destiny"*, and the Lord says *"I will destine you to the sword"*. "Destiny" and "destine" share a root (Isa 65:11–12).; They chose gardens and desired oaks, and become *"like an oak whose leaf withers, and like a garden without water"* (Isa 1:30).; *"the strong shall become tinder, and his work a spark"* (Isa 1:31).; The Lord's choice answers theirs: *"I also will choose"* (Isa 66:4).; I read these as the same thing said in different figures.

19877.text: The way back stays open. In the same oracles the offer stands: *"Come now, let us reason together"* (Isa 1:18); *"those in her who repent"* (Isa 1:27).

19882.text: Choices weighed by another: The book does not let these evaluations have the last word. Job is the one the Lord calls *"a blameless and upright man, who fears God and turns away from evil"* (1:8). Of Eliphaz and his friends the Lord says *"you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has"* (42:7); Elihu is not named.; The choice Elihu pressed is made, in his own verb, but only when Job sees the Lord: *"now my eye sees you; therefore I despise myself, and repent"* (42:5–6).

19903.text: Act 6:5 | what draws it (pleased); together | batch 3

19916.text: 1Ch 29:18 | Ch 14 v13 gives the referent, "offering freely and joyously to you" (29:17) | Fixed under #1991. H5068 ("freely offered") is M18 and is not pulled.

19924.text: 3.6 Exo 36:2, in 10.7 *Willing*, *The willing heart*: Add a bullet after the Exo 35:21–22 bullet: > - Of the craftsmen, the skill given and the heart that moves are named together: *"every craftsman in whose mind the Lord had put skill, everyone whose heart stirred him up to come to do the work"* (Exodus 36:2).

19939.text: Turned toward it from far off: For those far from the chosen city, the city is the direction of prayer. Solomon's prayer gives the hardest case, the people in captivity because they sinned: *"for there is no one who does not sin"* (1Ki 8:46). The inner turning comes in steps: *"yet if they turn their heart in the land to which they have been carried captive"* (8:47); *"and repent and plead with you … saying, 'We have sinned and have acted perversely and wickedly'"* (8:47); *"if they repent with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies … and pray to you toward their land, … the city that you have chosen"* (8:48); "Turn" and "repent" are the one verb, *šûb*. The turning happens in the enemy's land. The whole heart and the whole soul are in it. The prayer is turned toward what God chose. Solomon prays it before the one who knows hearts: *"for you, you only, know the hearts of all the children of mankind"* (8:39). He also asks God to do the turning: *"that he may incline our hearts to him"* (8:58).; Nehemiah prays from exile in the same verb. He asks God to remember his word to Moses: *"if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, … from there I will gather them and bring them to the place that I have chosen"* (Neh 1:9). Here the return is to God himself, and the place is where he brings those who return. Nehemiah's own part comes first: he *"sat down and wept and mourned for days"* (1:4), and confessed *"Even I and my father's house have sinned"* (1:6).

19953.text: Knowing a choice, and arguing from it. In the dispute at Jerusalem Peter appeals to what the assembly knows: *"you know that in the early days God made a choice among you, that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel and believe"* (Act 15:7). The purpose of God's choosing one man lies in others: that they hear and believe. Their hearts were known by God and *"cleansed … by faith"* (15:8–9). The debate ends in silence and listening (15:12), and the assembly's own choosing follows (15:25).

19954.text: Knowing that others are chosen, from what was seen. *"For we know, brothers loved by God, that he has chosen you, because our gospel came to you not only in word, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with full conviction"* (1Th 1:4–5). The knowing rests on what Paul saw: faith, love and hope at work (1:3), joy in affliction (1:6), and a turning *"to God from idols"* (1:9).

19957.text: An inner act weighed by what God chooses: In one passage the inner act of the others is itself set against God's choosing. The people fast and ask, *"Why have we humbled ourselves, and you take no knowledge of it?"* (Isa 58:3). They *"delight to know my ways"* and *"delight to draw near to God"* (58:2). Yet *"in the day of your fast you seek your own pleasure, and oppress all your workers"* (58:3). Then: *"Is such the fast that I choose, a day for a person to humble himself?"* (58:5). "Humble himself" is the humbling of the soul, the same words as their own complaint. What God does choose is turned outward: *"to let the oppressed go free"*, *"to share your bread with the hungry"*, *"not to hide yourself from your own flesh"* (58:6–7).; The self-humbling they offered was not wrong in itself. The passage says it stood beside oppression and quarrelling in the same people, and that it was not what he chooses.

19961.text: Knowing.; Knowing that God chose is ground for settling a dispute (Act 15:7).; Another's being chosen is known from what is seen (1Th 1:4–5).; Not knowing God does not stop a man from being called for the sake of the chosen (Isa 45:4–5).; Not knowing the Father is named under the world's hatred (Joh 15:21).; *Why:* whose knowing, and of what. It is the knowing of a choice, or of the God who chose.

19965.text: Notes for other sections, not placed: Judg 20:34, for knowing and fear (not knowing, then seeing, then dismay); Pro 10:20, for speaking.

19982.text: Pro 10:20 | not about choosing (F2, as Pro 8:10); note for speaking, not placed | batch 2

19997.text: Where it is placed. The verses place this in the heart: *"The heart of man plans his way"* (Pro 16:9); *"who plan evil things in their heart"* (Psa 140:2); *"the month that he had devised from his own heart"* (1Ki 12:33); *"the purposes of the heart"* (1Co 4:5); *"every intention of the thoughts of his heart"* (Gen 6:5)

20003.text: 3.2 It works in time: the night before, the morning after: *"Woe to those who devise wickedness and work evil on their beds! When the morning dawns, they perform it, because it is in the power of their hand."* (Mic 2:1); *"He plots trouble while on his bed"* (Psa 36:4).; *"For I know what they are inclined to do even today, before I have brought them into the land"* (Deu 31:21). The inclination is already there before the occasion comes.; I read Mic 2:1 as the clearest picture in the set of looking ahead as such. The scheme is held overnight and carried out at dawn, when the hand has the power to do it. The verse itself names the power of the hand as the reason it is done.

20019.text: 3.9 God sees the intention: *"the Lord searches all hearts and understands every plan and thought"* (1Ch 28:9).; *"the intention of man's heart is evil from his youth"* (Gen 8:21; also Gen 6:5).; *"he knows our frame; he remembers that we are dust"* (Psa 103:14). H3336 here is "frame", the thing formed.; *"will disclose the purposes of the heart"* (1Co 4:5).

20020.text: God reckoning: *"he counted it to him as righteousness"* (Gen 15:6; Psa 106:31) and *"against whom the Lord counts no iniquity"* (Psa 32:2).

20025.text: H2161: God's fixed purpose, *"I have purposed; I have not relented"* (Jer 4:28); the psalmist's resolve (Psa 17:3); the wise woman considering a field (Pro 31:16); the wicked plotting (Psa 37:12)

20027.text: H3336: the evil intention of the heart (Gen 6:5); purposes David asks God to keep (1Ch 29:18); the mind stayed on God (Isa 26:3); the human frame (Psa 103:14); the idol-maker's own creation (Hab 2:18)

20031.text: 10.10 Relating to others, new section *Plotting against another* | Planned in the heart (Psa 140:2; Zec 7:10; 8:17). Done together (Psa 31:13; Jer 48:2; Joh 11:53; 12:10–11; Eze 11:2; Dan 11:25, 27; Jer 49:30). Aimed at the quiet and the weak (Psa 10:2; 35:20; 37:12; Eze 38:10–11). Hidden behind something friendly (Neh 6:2–3; 1Sa 18:25). Accusing the other of a plan (Neh 6:6, 8–9). The one plotted against: not knowing (Jer 11:19–20); praying to be guarded (Psa 140:4, 8; 35:4); trusting (Psa 31:14–15); another pleading (Est 8:3; 9:24); another stopping it (Act 27:42–43). Named and checked (Pro 24:8–9; 30:32–33; Deu 19:19–20) | New section

20035.text: 10.13 Anger, *What it does next* | The plot with gnashing teeth (Psa 37:12); rage that wants to kill at once, which is not a plan (Act 5:33–35) | Widened

20036.text: Ch 11 §4 One word, opposite values | New faces: "Purposing" (*zāmam*: Psa 17:3; 37:12; Pro 31:16; Jer 4:28) and "Planning ahead" (Luk 14:31; Act 27:12; 2Ti 3:10; Joh 11:53; Pro 16:9). The reading of what changes them is marked "I read" | New faces

20120.text: A resolve reached after weighing, then turned. *"her husband Joseph, being a just man and unwilling to put her to shame, resolved to divorce her quietly"* (Mat 1:19). The next verse: *"But as he considered these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream"* (1:20). The resolve was still being weighed, and God redirected it.

20128.text: The epistle openings and requests (*"I want you to know"*, Phi 1:12; Tit 3:8; Jude 5; 1Ti 2:8; 5:14; 2Jo 12; Phm 13; 3Jo 10) mostly use the word as a stated wish in teaching. Their bearing on setting direction is slight, but each still needs to be read.

20138.text: The willing heart (*nāḏîḇ*, H5081G, 5 verses) is the will freely given: *"Whoever is of a generous heart, let him bring the Lord's contribution"* (Exo 35:5); *"All who were of a willing heart brought"* (Exo 35:22; also 2Ch 29:31; 1Ch 28:21); It is asked of God: *"uphold me with a willing spirit"* (Psa 51:12).; 10.7 *Setting the heart* already cites Exo 35:21, *"everyone whose heart stirred him, and everyone whose spirit moved him"*, the verse just before 35:22.

20143.text: 5. If you want this woven: Read the 99 verses in their passages, the method used for the plan set.; Route them under rule 72. By scan, God's or the Spirit's will (route A) is 21 verses: Deu 10:10; 23:5; 29:20; Jos 24:10; 2Ki 8:19; 13:23; 24:4; 2Ch 21:7; Dan 4:17, 25, 32, 35; 5:21; Mat 11:27; Luk 10:22; Luk 22:42 (with B); Rom 9:19; 1Co 12:11; Heb 6:17; Jam 1:18; 2Pe 3:9. Job 39:9 is the wild ox (13.4 Nature).; A home in 10.7 would be a section on willing, next to *Planning* and *Holding a choice*. The working note already reserves "Will and resolve" for there.; Placed already (in the narrative for another reason, #1987): Deu 1:26; 2:30; 1Sa 31:4; Psa 51:12; Pro 6:35; Dan 5:19; Act 25:20; 1Ti 2:8. Each still needs reading for its will word.

20149.text: A plea: Tamar: *"No, my brother, do not violate me … But he would not listen to her"* (2Sa 13:12–14); Tamar again, after (13:16); The old man at Gibeah pleading with the men of the city (Judg 19:23–25); Israel calling on Benjamin to give up the guilty (Judg 20:12–13)

20152.text: A refusal that keeps faith: The king's servants would not kill the priests of the Lord. Doeg did (1Sa 22:17–18).; David *"would not put out my hand against the Lord's anointed"* (1Sa 26:23). He sets it beside a prayer: *"as your life was precious this day in my sight, so may my life be precious in the sight of the Lord"* (26:24).; David *"said longingly, 'Oh, that someone would give me water'"* (2Sa 23:15). When it came, *"he would not drink of it. He poured it out to the Lord and said, 'Far be it from me, O Lord, that I should do this. Shall I drink the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?'"* (23:16–17). His own longing was met, and he refused it for the sake of the men's lives. He gave the reason aloud, before the Lord.; The faithful refuse enticement and demand (Deu 13:8; Pro 1:10; 1Ki 20:8).

20167.text: Moved from inside: *"they came, everyone whose heart stirred him, and everyone whose spirit moved him"* (Exo 35:21), then *"All who were of a willing heart brought"* (35:22). Moses had said *"Whoever is of a generous heart, let him bring"* (35:5).

20168.text: After consecration: *"You have now consecrated yourselves to the Lord. Come near … and all who were of a willing heart brought burnt offerings"* (2Ch 29:31).

20170.text: Asked of God: *"Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me … take not your Holy Spirit from me. Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and uphold me with a willing spirit"* (Psa 51:10–12). Clean heart, right spirit, Holy Spirit and willing spirit are asked for in one prayer. The willing spirit is something God upholds.

20178.text: Overruled by right. Diotrephes *"refuses to welcome the brothers, and also stops those who want to and puts them out of the church"* (3Jo 10).

20179.text: Joseph. *"being a just man and unwilling to put her to shame, resolved to divorce her quietly. But as he considered these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream"* (Mat 1:19–20). He was unwilling to shame her, he resolved, and he went on considering. Then God spoke into the considering.

20186.text: Paul's wishes for the churches are mostly stated wishes in teaching. Their passages give each one a reason: *"I desire then that in every place the men should pray, lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling"* (1Ti 2:8); *"I would have younger widows marry … for some have already strayed after Satan"* (1Ti 5:14–15); *"I want you to insist on these things, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works"* (Tit 3:8); *"I want you to know … what has happened to me has really served to advance the gospel"* (Phi 1:12); *"I would rather not use paper and ink … talk face to face, so that our joy may be complete"* (2Jo 12); *"I want to remind you"* (Jude 5)

20187.text: Toward riches: *"those who desire to be rich fall into temptation, into a snare, into many senseless and harmful desires that plunge people into ruin"* (1Ti 6:9). Beside it: *"godliness with contentment is great gain"* (6:6), and *"flee these things. Pursue righteousness"* (6:11).

20202.text: The Son chooses: *"yes, Father, for such was your gracious will. All things have been handed over to me by my Father … and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him"* (Mat 11:26–27; Luk 10:21–22). The Father's gracious will and the Son's choosing stand together. Luke adds *"he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit"* (10:21).

20207.text: 2.2 Passages where Scripture itself puts them together: Pro 1:29–31. Did not choose the fear of the Lord, would have none of my counsel, are filled with their own devices: choosing, willing and devising in one sentence. Earlier in the same chapter, *"if sinners entice you, do not consent. If they say, 'Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood'"* (1:10–11) puts the will's "no" right against a group plot. That is plotting as written in 10.10.; Psa 81:11–12. Would not submit, given over to stubborn hearts, to follow their own counsels.; Isa 30:1, 9, 15–16. A plan *"but not mine"*; unwilling to hear; unwilling, and *"No! We will flee upon horses."* The refusal and the people's own plan are in their own mouth together.; 1Ch 28:19–21. The plan from the hand of the Lord, and *"every willing man who has skill"*. This is the positive pairing: a plan given, and the willing who carry it out.; Gen 24:5–8. Planning ahead allows for another person's will (*"Perhaps the woman may not be willing"*).; 2Sa 13:24–28. A planner presses another's will until it gives way, and the plan goes on to murder.; Mat 1:19–20. Unwilling, then resolved, while still considering, then redirected by God.; Act 12:3–5. Herod's intending is set beside the church's prayer.; 2Co 1:15–17. Wanting, then plans, then the question of a divided word.; Act 27:42–43. One man's wish against a group's plan.; Dan 4:27–35. Counsel offered and not taken; the human will made absolute; the Most High *"does according to his will"*; reason returned.

20211.text: The heart and spirit named with the act.; Planning: *"The heart of man plans his way"* (Pro 16:9); *"plan evil things in their heart"* (Psa 140:2).; Willing: the heart or spirit hardened, stubborn or lifted up (Exo 10:27; Deu 2:30; Eze 3:7; Psa 81:12; Deu 29:19; Dan 5:20); the willing heart and spirit (Exo 35:21–22; 2Ch 29:31; Psa 51:12).; So the will verses name the state of the heart and spirit more often than the plan verses do. Chapters 4 (the heart) and 6 (the spirit) should take this.

20218.text: *ʾāḇâ* | refusing God (Isa 30:15); refusing sin (Pro 1:10); refusing to harm the anointed (1Sa 26:23); refusing a gift for others' sake (2Sa 23:17); refusing a plea by force (2Sa 13:14); refusing in grief (2Sa 12:17); God not willing to destroy (2Ki 8:19); God not willing to forgive (Deu 29:20) | What is refused, and for whose sake. The passages give the reason each time: faith, fear, grief, honour, force, covenant, love, a stubborn heart

20223.text: Already in the narrative for another reason (#1987): Deu 1:26; 2:30; 1Sa 31:4; Psa 51:12; Pro 6:35; Dan 5:19; Act 25:20; 1Ti 2:8; Act 27:43 (as a plan verse in 10.10). Each is now read for its will word above.

20228.text: Colossians 3:12: "Put on then, as God's chosen ones … compassionate hearts": The chapter begins with where the chosen now stand: *"If then you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above"* (v1); *"Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth"* (v2); *"your life is hidden with Christ in God"* (v3).; Then it tells them what to put away: *"Put to death therefore what is earthly in you: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry"* (v5); *"But now you must put them all away: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and obscene talk from your mouth"* (v8); They have *"put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge after the image of its creator"* (v10).; The verse comes next: *"Put on then, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience"* (v12). "Compassionate hearts" is literally the inward parts (G4698) of compassion. The verse gives being chosen as the ground ("as God's chosen ones"), and then gives a command. The qualities are not described as already there. They are to be put on, as clothing is.; The chosen are called *"holy and beloved"*. The holiness that is the purpose of the choosing in Ephesians 1:4 is here a name the chosen already carry, and the inner qualities are still to be put on. I set the two letters side by side; neither refers to the other.; What the chosen put on is turned toward one another: *"bearing with one another and, if one has a complaint against another, forgiving each other; as the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive"* (v13); *"And above all these put on love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony"* (v14); *"And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to which indeed you were called in one body. And be thankful"* (v15); The forgiving is measured by being forgiven. The peace is to rule in the heart.

20229.text: 2 Thessalonians 2:13: "God chose you … through sanctification by the Spirit and belief in the truth": The chapter is about deception. Paul asks them *"not to be quickly shaken in mind or alarmed"* (v2), and warns *"Let no one deceive you in any way"* (v3). The lawless one comes *"with all wicked deception for those who are perishing"* (v10).; Before the choosing verse, the passage names the inner state of those who perish: *"because they refused to love the truth and so be saved"* (v10); *"Therefore God sends them a strong delusion, so that they may believe what is false"* (v11); *"in order that all may be condemned who did not believe the truth but had pleasure in unrighteousness"* (v12); Then: *"But we ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by the Lord, because God chose you as the firstfruits to be saved, through sanctification by the Spirit and belief in the truth"* (v13). "Belief" in v13 and "believe" in v12 are the same root (G4102, G4100), and "truth" is the same word in v10, v12 and v13 (G0225). The chosen are set against the perishing in the passage's own words. The perishing did not believe the truth. The chosen are saved *"through … belief in the truth"*. The perishing had pleasure in unrighteousness. The chosen are sanctified *"by the Spirit"*.; In the verse, God's choosing and the person's belief stand in one sentence. The verse does not say which comes first, or how they fit.; The passage then gives the chosen two things to do, and asks for one thing to be done in them: *"To this he called you through our gospel, so that you may obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ"* (v14); *"So then, brothers, stand firm and hold to the traditions that you were taught by us"* (v15); *"comfort your hearts and establish them in every good work and word"* (v17), asked of the Lord Jesus Christ and of God the Father, *"who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace"* (v16)

20231.text: James 2:5: "has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith": The setting is an assembly that chooses where people sit: *"if you pay attention to the one who wears the fine clothing and say, 'You sit here in a good place,' while you say to the poor man, 'You stand over there'"* (v3). James names what that shows of them inside: *"have you not then made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?"* (v4).; He answers their way of choosing with God's: *"Listen, my beloved brothers, has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which he has promised to those who love him?"* (v5). The poor man they sent to stand is the kind of man God chose. The assembly went by clothing. God's choice goes by something else, and its aim is that the poor be *"rich in faith"*.; The promise is to *"those who love him"*. The love here is the chosen people's love for God.; Then: *"But you have dishonored the poor man"* (v6). Choosing against God's choice is a sin: *"if you show partiality, you are committing sin"* (v9).; The faith of the chosen poor is then tested by what it does: *"What good is it, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works?"* (v14); *"So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead"* (v17); Abraham: *"faith was active along with his works, and faith was completed by his works … and he was called a friend of God"* (v22–23)

20234.text: Revelation 17:14: "those with him are called and chosen and faithful": The chapter is a vision of judgment on *"the great prostitute"*, with whom *"the dwellers on earth have become drunk"* (v2). The seer himself is moved: *"When I saw her, I marveled greatly"* (v6). He is asked *"Why do you marvel?"* (v7). Those who marvel at the beast are *"the dwellers on earth whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world"* (v8). The vision *"calls for a mind with wisdom"* (v9).; The kings who serve the beast are of one mind: *"These are of one mind, and they hand over their power and authority to the beast"* (v13). Then: *"They will make war on the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, for he is Lord of lords and King of kings, and those with him are called and chosen and faithful"* (v14).; The chosen are named by three words, and the third is about them: *"faithful"*. They are *"with him"*. The verse says nothing more of their inner life.; The chapter says this of the kings: *"for God has put it into their hearts to carry out his purpose by being of one mind and handing over their royal power to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled"* (v17). "Mind" in v13 and "purpose" in v17 are the same word (G1106): the kings' one mind is God's purpose carried out. This is God acting on the hearts of others, not on the chosen. It belongs with 13.1 more than here.

20235.text: The order seen in Isaiah 43:10 holds, and is widened. God chooses first, and the inner life of the chosen is the purpose: holy and blameless before him (Eph 1:4); rich in faith (Jam 2:5); saved through sanctification and belief in the truth (2Th 2:13); Ephesians puts the choosing *"before the foundation of the world"*. The one verse where people choose (Act 6:5) has the other order. The gathering chooses by what is already seen in the man.

20236.text: The chosen are told to act. Being chosen is given as the ground of commands: put on compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, meekness, patience and love (Col 3:12–14); stand firm and hold on (2Th 2:15); be diligent to confirm your calling and election, adding quality to quality (2Pe 1:5–10); This sits with batch 1: *"be strong and do it"* (1Ch 28:10).

20238.text: The chosen are set against others in the passage's own words: those who refused to love the truth and had pleasure in unrighteousness (2Th 2:10–12); those who profess to know God and deny him by works (Tit 1:16); an assembly that judges *"with evil thoughts"* (Jam 2:4); kings of one mind with the beast, and those whose names are not written (Rev 17:8, 13); Stephen's accusers, *"uncircumcised in heart and ears"* (Act 7:51)

20240.text: Knowing and remembering.: The chosen are prayed for, that the eyes of their hearts be enlightened to know their hope (Eph 1:18).; Their knowledge of the truth accords with godliness (Tit 1:1).; Forgetting one's cleansing is blindness, and another works to keep them remembering (2Pe 1:9, 12–15).; Batch 1 had the chosen called to remember (Psa 105:5; Isa 44:21).

20242.text: Ephesians 1:4 and Colossians 3:12. Holiness is the purpose of the choosing in one, and a name the chosen carry in the other. I set them side by side. Neither refers to the other.

20244.text: The chapter is one long blessing of God: *"Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing"* (v3). The choosing is part of that blessing: *"even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before him"* (v4).

20245.text: The love in the passage is God's: *"In love he predestined us for adoption to himself as sons through Jesus Christ, according to the purpose of his will"* (v4–5). The chapter goes on with what is given: *"redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses"* (v7).

20246.text: hearing and believing: *"when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit"* (v13)

20262.text: Nehemiah 1:9: "but if you return to me … I will gather them and bring them to the place that I have chosen": Nehemiah is in Susa when he hears of Jerusalem: *"The remnant there … is in great trouble and shame. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down"* (v3). His response is inward first: *"As soon as I heard these words I sat down and wept and mourned for days, and I continued fasting and praying before the God of heaven"* (v4).; His prayer confesses his own part: *"confessing the sins of the people of Israel, which we have sinned against you. Even I and my father's house have sinned"* (v6). Then he asks God to remember a word: *"Remember the word that you commanded your servant Moses, saying, 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the peoples, but if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, though your outcasts are in the uttermost parts of heaven, from there I will gather them and bring them to the place that I have chosen, to make my name dwell there'"* (v8–9).; "Return" is *šûb* (H7725O), the same tag as "repent" in 1Ki 8:47–48. Here the return is *"to me"*, to God himself. The chosen place is where God brings those who return. The verse says nothing of the place before that.; The prayer ends with those who pray with him: *"your servants who delight to fear your name"* (v11). The narrative already cites this phrase in 10.9.

20263.text: What this verse shows of others around the choosing: The return is to God. The chosen place is where he gathers those who return.; The returning is joined to keeping: *"return to me and keep my commandments and do them"*.; The one who prays mourns, fasts and confesses his own sin with the people's (v4, v6).; Nehemiah asks God to remember his own word (v8). He prays from that promise.

20265.text: Toward the place: the whole desire of a Levite's soul, which may bring him there (Deu 18:6); the turning of the heart, and repentance with all the heart and soul, prayed toward the city from an enemy's land (1Ki 8:47–48; 2Ch 6:37–38)

20285.text: Romans 11:7: "Israel failed to obtain what it was seeking. The elect obtained it, but the rest were hardened": Paul asks whether God has rejected his people and answers: *"By no means!"* (v1). *"God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew"* (v2). He gives Elijah, who thought he was alone, and God's reply: *"I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal"* (v4). *"So too at the present time there is a remnant, chosen by grace. But if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works"* (v5–6).; Then v7: *"What then? Israel failed to obtain what it was seeking. The elect obtained it, but the rest were hardened"*.; The others are *"the rest"*. Two things are said of them: They were seeking (*epizēteō*, G1934) and did not obtain.; They were hardened (*pōroō*, G4456).; The hardening is described from Scripture: *"God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that would not see and ears that would not hear, down to this very day"* (v8). The giving is God's act (rule 72, A). The eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear are in the human inner being.; Paul does not leave it there: *"So I ask, did they stumble in order that they might fall? By no means! Rather, through their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, so as to make Israel jealous"* (v11). He goes on: *"how much more will their full inclusion mean!"* (v12).

20286.text: What this verse shows of others around the choosing: Those who are not among the chosen are described as seeking and not obtaining.; They were hardened: eyes that do not see, ears that do not hear (v8).; The hardening is not the end. Their stumbling is not *"in order that they might fall"* (v11).; Jealousy is named as an aim: *"so as to make Israel jealous"* (v11).; The remnant is chosen *"by grace"*, not by works (v5–6). The verse says how the elect were chosen. It does not say why the rest were not.

20294.text: What others do around a choice, in these verses: hate the chosen, because they are chosen out of the world (Joh 15:19); know that God chose, and settle a dispute on it (Act 15:7); believe, as the purpose of God's choosing one man (Act 15:7); seek and not obtain, and be hardened, with eyes that do not see (Rom 11:7–8); know that others are chosen, from what was seen when the gospel came (1Th 1:4–5); endure suffering for the sake of the chosen (2Ti 2:10); reject the chosen one after testing (1Pe 2:4, 7); believe in the chosen one, and not be put to shame (1Pe 2:6); love the chosen in truth (2Jo 1)

20303.text: The frame the book sets: Before any friend speaks, the book says who Job is, twice: the narrator: *"that man was blameless and upright, one who feared God and turned away from evil"* (1:1); the Lord: *"there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, who fears God and turns away from evil"* (1:8); Job's choosing is already named there, in its refusing side: he *"turned away from evil"*.; At the end the book gives a verdict on the friends: *"the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite"*: *"My anger burns against you and against your two friends, for you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has"* (42:7). The verdict is about how they spoke *of God*. Elihu is not named in it, either way.; So every evaluation of Job's choices in these speeches is made by someone the book does not let have the last word.

20304.text: Job 15:5 — Eliphaz: "your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty": Eliphaz weighs Job by his words. He opens with *"Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge"* (v2), and charges *"you are doing away with the fear of God and hindering meditation before God"* (v4). Then he names the choice: *"For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty"* (v5). He reads it this way: something inside, iniquity, teaches the mouth; the mouth then chooses a crafty tongue; From that he gives the verdict: *"Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; your own lips testify against you"* (v6).; He takes his evaluation further inside. He moves from the mouth to the heart, eyes and spirit: *"Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash, that you turn your spirit against God and bring such words out of your mouth?"* (v12–13). For Eliphaz, the words show what the heart has chosen.; His grounds for judging are age and tradition: *"Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, older than your father"* (v10); *"what wise men have told, without hiding it from their fathers"* (v18); His picture of the outcome is the wicked man's end (v20–35).; Set against the book's frame, his charge *"you are doing away with the fear of God"* (v4) runs against the narrator's and the Lord's *"one who feared God"* (1:1, 8). The Lord's verdict in 42:7 is on how Eliphaz spoke of God, not directly on this charge. Still, the man Eliphaz says has chosen the tongue of the crafty is the one the Lord twice calls *"my servant Job"* (42:7–8).

20309.text: Job 34:33 — Elihu: "For you must choose, and not I": Elihu's verdict follows anyway: *"Job speaks without knowledge; his words are without insight"*; *"Would that Job were tried to the end"* (v35–36).; The book records what Job did choose, and when. It is not after Elihu, but after the Lord speaks (38–41): *"I have uttered what I did not understand, things too wonderful for me"* (42:3); *"I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you; therefore I despise myself, and repent in dust and ashes"* (42:5–6); *"I despise"* is the same verb, H3988A, as Elihu's *"you reject"*. In the record the verb stands without its own tagged object; the ESV supplies *"myself"*. I read this as Elihu having named the right kind of choice, a refusing, but the choice being made when Job's eye saw the Lord, not under Elihu's argument. The text gives the order (*"now my eye sees you; therefore"*). It does not comment on Elihu.

20310.text: Job 36:21 — Elihu: "this you have chosen rather than affliction": Elihu speaks *"on God’s behalf"* (v2), and his speech is about what affliction is for: *"if they are bound in chains and caught in the cords of affliction, then he declares to them their work … He opens their ears to instruction and commands that they return from iniquity"* (v8–10); *"If they listen and serve him, they complete their days in prosperity … But if they do not listen, they perish"* (v11–12); *"He delivers the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ear by adversity"* (v15); In Elihu's account, affliction is how God opens the ear.; Then he turns to Job, and what he sees in him is inward: *"you are full of the judgment on the wicked"* (v17); *"Beware lest wrath entice you into scoffing"* (v18); *"Do not long for the night"* (v20); His evaluation: *"Take care; do not turn to iniquity, for this you have chosen rather than affliction"* (v21). The choice he sees is a preference, as in Proverbs 16:16 (*"rather than"*). Of the two things before Job, affliction (H6040, the word in v15) and iniquity (H0205), Elihu says Job has taken iniquity rather than accept the affliction as the opening of his ear. The warning *"Take care"* treats the choice as still able to be turned.; He ends by pointing to God: *"who is a teacher like him?"* (v22). "Teacher" here is H4175, from the same root as *"instruct"* in Psalm 25:8, 12 (H3384).

20449.text: The Hebrew Bible: The source is the *lēv* (heart), not the brain. Examples are Proverbs 4:23 ("from it flow the springs of life") and Genesis 6:5 ("every intention of the thoughts of his heart").

20453.text: 1. From within: the heart is where they come from.: Mark 7:21 and Matthew 15:19 say it directly: "from within, out of the heart … come evil thoughts."; Genesis 6:5 speaks of "the intention of the thoughts of his heart," and Luke 1:51 of "the thoughts of their hearts."; Also Hebrews 4:12, Luke 2:35, 1 Chronicles 29:18, Matthew 9:4 and Luke 5:22.; In these verses thoughts are never located in the head. They come out of the heart, the centre of the person.

20456.text: 4.2 What thoughts are: Inner speech. 21 of the rows (H0559, *ʾāmar*, "to say") are places where the Hebrew says "he *said*" and the ESV renders it "he thought," as in 1 Samuel 18:11: "Saul thought, 'I will pin David…'" The Greek *dialogismos* (G1261) and *logismos* (G3053) are also built on *logos*, "word" [lexical]. In these texts, to think is to speak inwardly. *Caveat:* how many rows show this depends on the ESV's choices.; Devising or planning. H4284 *maḥăšāvāh* (from H2803 *ḥāšav*, "to devise"). These thoughts are designs with a direction. They can be just (Proverbs 12:5), evil (Isaiah 59:7), or God's own plan (Micah 4:12). Because they point somewhere, they can be judged, and they can be abandoned (Isaiah 55:7).; Likening, or interpreting. H1819 *dāmāh* ("to resemble") is used in Psalm 50:21: "you thought that I was one like yourself." Many rows record thoughts that were wrong: Genesis 38:15, Mark 6:49, Luke 24:37, Matthew 20:10, Acts 12:9, Judges 3:24 and 2 Kings 5:11. So a thought is a reading of reality, not reality itself.; Something that grows and matures. 1 Corinthians 13:11: "I thought like a child … I gave up childish ways."; Transient, yet weighty. Human thoughts are "but a breath" (Psalm 94:11) and "futile" (1 Corinthians 3:20). Yet God weighs them (Proverbs 15:26), and before the flood they were the measure of human wickedness (Genesis 6:5). God's thoughts, by contrast, are "very deep" (Psalm 92:5), "vast" (Psalm 139:17) and "higher" (Isaiah 55:8–9).

20462.text: intention / intent | H3336 *yēṣer* | Gen 8:21 | *yēṣer* is also in Gen 6:5; central to origins

20470.text: Evil schemes: Esther 9:25 (Haman's "evil plan"), Jeremiah 18:18, Proverbs 6:18.

20477.text: 4. One word covers both inner reasoning and outward dispute. *Dialogismos* is rendered "thoughts" (Mark 7:21), but also "quarreling" (1 Timothy 2:8), "disputing" (Philippians 2:14) and "opinions" (Romans 14:1). The same activity happens inside a person as an inner conversation and between people as argument.

20481.text: 1. The heart or mind is the place thoughts come from. Mark 7:21 and Matt 15:19 ("out of the heart come evil thoughts"). Also: "a heart that devises wicked plans" (Prov 6:18); "plan evil things in their heart" (Ps 140:2); "devise evil … in your heart" (Zech 7:10; 8:17); "The heart of man plans his way" (Prov 16:9); "his heart does not so think; but it is in his heart to destroy" (Isa 10:7); "the reasoning of their hearts" (Luke 9:47); In Jer 4:14, thoughts *lodge* within: "How long shall your wicked thoughts lodge within you?" This follows the call to "wash your heart."

20483.text: 3. The bed is also where people devise deliberately.: "He plots trouble while on his bed" (Ps 36:4); "devise wickedness … on their beds! When the morning dawns, they perform it, because it is in the power of their hand" (Mic 2:1); The same place hosts thoughts that come unbidden (Dan 2:29) and thoughts that are worked on on purpose (Ps 36:4).

20489.text: 9.2 What thoughts are: Design: forming something that does not yet exist. H2803G (19 rows) describes craftsmanship: cherubim "skillfully worked" (Exod 26:1, 31) and "skilled design" (Exod 39:3). The faculty itself is neutral. *Maḥăšāvāh* covers both artistry and plots, and *mᵊzimmāh* covers both "discretion" (Prov 2:11) and "evil devices" (Prov 12:2). What makes a thought good or evil is what it is designed toward.; Reckoning: giving something its value or category. H2803H/J (60 rows): Human misreckoning: Eli "took her to be a drunken woman" (1 Sam 1:13), "we esteemed him stricken" and "we esteemed him not" (Isa 53:3–4), Judah "thought she was a prostitute" (Gen 38:15).; God's reckoning: "he counted it to him as righteousness" (Gen 15:6), "the Lord counts no iniquity" (Ps 32:2), and the nations "accounted as the dust on the scales" (Isa 40:15, 17).; To think is to judge the worth of something, and people can judge wrongly.; Inner speech.; "all his thoughts are, 'There is no God'" (Ps 10:4). The thought is quoted as a sentence.; Hannah "was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved" (1 Sam 1:13).; *Dialogismos* covers both inner reasoning and outward "argument", "quarreling" and "disputing".; "conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse" (Rom 2:15).; Something that affects the body and emotions.; "his thoughts alarmed him; his limbs gave way, and his knees knocked together" (Dan 5:6; also 4:19; 5:10; 7:28).; "the cares of my heart" (Ps 94:19), and "haste within me" (Job 20:2).; A divided mind stalls a person: "limping between two different opinions" (1 Kgs 18:21, H5587A).; Creaturely and passing.; "but a breath" (Ps 94:11).; "When his breath departs … on that very day his plans perish" (Ps 146:4).; "futile" (1 Cor 3:20; Rom 1:21).; "striving of heart … striving after wind" (Eccl 2:22; 4:16).; Fully open to God.; "you discern my thoughts from afar" (Ps 139:2); also Ps 139:23; 1 Chr 28:9; "I know their works and their thoughts" (Isa 66:18); Heb 4:12.; Jesus knows people's thoughts (Luke 5:22; 6:8; 9:47; 11:17; Matt 9:4; 12:25).

20490.text: 9.3 From thought to action (Claude's reading): The verses trace a path from thought to deed: Arising. Thoughts come, often in the night (Dan 2:29; Job 4:13; Ezek 38:10; Luke 24:38).; Lodging. They stay and are dwelt on (Jer 4:14).; Reckoning. They weigh up and value things (Isa 53:4; 1 Sam 1:13).; Devising. They take the form of a plan (Ezek 38:10b; Ps 36:4).; Expression. Tongue, lips and eyes: "your tongue plots" (Ps 52:2), "devise words of deceit" (Ps 35:20), "winks his eyes plans" (Prov 16:30), "whisper … imagine the worst" (Ps 41:7).; Action. Hand and feet: "when the morning dawns, they perform it" (Mic 2:1); "a heart that devises … feet that make haste" (Prov 6:18); "their feet run to evil … their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity" (Isa 59:7).; The same path also runs toward good: "When I think on my ways, I turn my feet to your testimonies" (Ps 119:59).

20491.text: Where responsibility sits. The commands address the stages from lodging onward: "forsake … his thoughts" (Isa 55:7); "let none of you devise evil" (Zech 7:10); "take every thought captive" (2 Cor 10:5); "wash your heart" (Jer 4:14); The *arising* is not commanded, but it is not neutral either. What comes up shows the condition of the heart (Gen 6:5; Mark 7:21). So thoughts that arise reveal the heart, and devising engages the will. The heart itself can be changed from outside: written on, given discretion, guarded, or darkened.

20493.text: 1. Outward: heart → speech → body → action.: "a heart that devises wicked plans, feet that make haste" (Prov 6:18); "your tongue plots" (Ps 52:2); "winks his eyes plans" (Prov 16:30); "when the morning dawns, they perform it, because it is in the power of their hand" (Mic 2:1)

20497.text: 5. Back again: consequences returning to the one who devised.: "his evil plan … should return on his own head" (Esth 9:25); "the fruit of their devices" (Jer 6:19); "let them be caught in the schemes that they have devised" (Ps 10:2); "The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance" (Prov 21:5)
