20506.text: The heart is where thoughts come from: Mat 15:19 / Mar 7:21; Pro 6:18 (§9.1.1): Ch 3 "The heart is the source"; Ch 12 (Gen 6:5, Mat 15:19)

20513.text: Where responsibility sits: forsake thoughts (Isa 55:7), take every thought captive (2Co 10:5), wash your heart (Jer 4:14) (§9.3): Ch 13 "Made new" (not yet using these verses)

20514.text: 3. New — not yet in any chapter: The path from thought to deed (§9.3). Arising (Dan 2:29; Job 4:13; Luk 24:38) → lodging (Jer 4:14) → reckoning (Isa 53:4) → devising (Ps 36:4) → expression through tongue, lips and eyes (Ps 52:2; Pro 16:30) → action through hand and feet (Mic 2:1; Pro 6:18; Isa 59:7). The same path runs toward good: "When I think on my ways, I turn my feet to your testimonies" (Ps 119:59). Commands address the stages from lodging onward. Arising is not commanded, but it shows the state of the heart.; Thinking as reckoning, i.e. assigning worth (§9.2.2). Human misreckoning (Gen 38:15; 1Sa 1:13; Isa 53:3–4) against God's reckoning (Gen 15:6; Ps 32:2; Isa 40:15, 17). This links directly to justification language. It has no home in the narrative yet.; Thoughts that arrive, especially at night (§9.1.2–3). The bed is where thoughts come unbidden (Dan 2:29) and also where people plot on purpose (Ps 36:4; Mic 2:1). The night thoughts are tied to revelation (Dan 2:29–30).; Thought moves the body (§9.2.4). "his thoughts alarmed him; his limbs gave way" (Dan 5:6); the divided mind "limping between two different opinions" (1Ki 18:21). This fits Ch 6 (flesh) or Ch 11 §3 ("The parts give way in sequence").; Outbound hearing: God hears the plots (§13.1). "You have heard their taunts … all their plots" (Lam 3:61); Mal 3:16. The narrative has hearing only as the inbound way in. Your comment in the discussion: *"Yes, hearing is an integral part of the outbound thought."*; Design and craft as the good form of devising (§9.2.1). Exod 26:1; 35:32–35: God fills craftsmen with skill "to devise artistic designs".

20515.text: 5. Checks needed before any of it enters a chapter: Under the narrative rules ("each unfounded claim must be checked and restated", quotes checked against the ESV): Quotations: the discussion quotes the ESV "as supplied in the datasets". Each verse must be checked against iba.db verse before use, as was done for chapters 01–14 (#1915).; Items marked [verify]: the discussion's own uncertain claims, including the Hebrew notes that §9.4 says the English obscures.; Claude's readings: §4.3, §9.3 and §11 are labelled as Claude's reading. They stay inferential and would enter as "I read this as…", not as findings.; Open threads (§14): these words have not been pulled yet: *yēṣer* H3336 (Gen 6:5; 8:21, "intention", central to where thoughts come from and already quoted in Ch 12), "say in the heart" (H0559 with heart), *hāgāh* H1897 (meditate), *dāmāh* H1819, *logizomai* G3049 (reckon, which would strengthen item 3.2), and *dialogizomai* G1260. The strand is incomplete until these are read.; Data flags (§13.2): H4209 sits in M06, which may be doubtful. H7451C sits in M24 but is mostly "devised evil". The dream/vision/night words sit in T2, so cluster-based pulls miss them.

20516.text:
What the heart says is mostly a verdict: about God's seeing, about self, about the future. Kinds seen:
• denial that God sees (Ps 10:11, 13; Zep 1:12; Isa 47:10)
• self-exaltation (Isa 14:13; 47:8; Zep 2:15; Obd 3; Eze 28:2)
• self-credit (Deu 8:17; 9:4)
• fear (Deu 7:17; 1Sa 27:1)
• enquiry (Ecc 1:16; 2:1, 15; 3:17–18; Deu 18:21; Jer 13:22)
• denial of God (Ps 14:1; 53:1)

20518.text: Scripture speaks back into inner speech. It forbids it ("Do not say in your heart", Deu 9:4; "Beware lest you say", 8:17) and answers it (Deu 7:17–18; 18:21–22)

20528.text: Face: Imputing before God; Verses: Gen 15:6; Psa 106:31; 32:2; Lev 7:18; 17:4; Mal 3:16; What differs: Who reckons: God. What is counted: faith (Gen 15:6), a zealous act (Phinehas, Psa 106:31), no iniquity (32:2), bloodguilt (Lev 17:4), an offering *not* credited (7:18), honouring his name (Mal 3:16); Why (basis): God's reckoning can credit or withhold; what he looks at is faith, zeal and the heart's honour (S)

20534.text: Face: Devising against; Verses: Psa 36:4; 52:2; 41:7; 35:4, 20; 21:11; 140:2, 4; 10:2; Mic 2:1; Eze 11:2; 38:10; Nah 1:9, 11; Neh 6:2, 6; Jer 11:19; 18:18; 48:2; Est 8:3; 9:24–25; 1Sa 18:25; 2Sa 14:13; Dan 11:24–25; Hos 7:15; Pro 16:30; 24:8; Zec 7:10; 8:17; Gen 50:20a; What differs: Aimed against a named person or God, nearly every time. Joined with arrogance (Psa 10:2), whispering together (41:7), tongue and lips (52:2; Pro 16:30), the bed (Psa 36:4; Mic 2:1), envy of a rival (1Sa 18:25, after the anger of 18:8). Against the one who trained them: "Although I trained and strengthened their arms, yet they devise evil against me" (Hos 7:15); Why (basis): The "against" is stated (S). Ingratitude turns into a plot (S, Hos 7:15)

20537.text: Thoughts to be forsaken: "let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts" (Isa 55:7). The next line gives the answer: "for he will abundantly pardon".

20539.text: Pure words against impure thoughts: "The thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord, but gracious words are pure" (Pro 15:26).

20548.text: Face: The inclination, evil; Verses: Gen 6:5; 8:21; Deu 31:21; What differs: God's response: grief and judgement (6:5–7) or forbearance (8:21); Why: The same fact grounds both (S; OT-22)

20564.text: *logizomai* | God reckons righteousness · God does not count sin · faith reckons God able · told to reckon oneself dead to sin · told to think on what is excellent · love does not reckon wrong · "may it not be charged" · others' estimate · suspicion · counting on boldness · claiming credit, denied · numbered with transgressors · counted as nothing · counted as offspring · wages counted as due, not gift · a calculation that became prophecy | Rom 4 (×11); Gal 3:6; Jam 2:23 · Rom 4:8; 2Co 5:19 · Heb 11:19 · Rom 6:11 · Phili 4:8 · 1Co 13:5 · 2Ti 4:16 · 1Co 4:1; 1Pe 5:12; 2Co 11:5; 12:6 · 2Co 10:2 · 2Co 10:2 · 2Co 3:5 · Luk 22:37 · Act 19:27 · Rom 9:8 · Rom 4:4 · Joh 11:50–51 | Who reckons (God, faith, love, the apostle, opponents); what is set to whose account (2Co 3:5: "Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to claim anything as coming from us"); whether it counts up wrong (2Co 10:2 suspect) or refuses to (1Co 13:5). Caiaphas reckons a death to be expedient (Joh 11:50), and "he did not say this of his own accord, but … prophesied" (11:51): a cold calculation is taken up into God's purpose, as in Gen 50:20 (S/R). Tagging notes: Mar 11:31 "discussed" and Joh 11:50 "understand" (OT-H3)

20565.text: *dialogizomai / dialogismos* | Honest troubled reasoning · hardened anxious reasoning · inner questioning seen by Jesus · reasoning together into murder · self-talk of the rich man · quarrel, dispute, opinions · argument about greatness · futile thinking · evil thoughts from the heart · partiality: "judges with evil thoughts" · thoughts revealed by the child set for a sign | Luk 1:29 · Mar 8:16–17; Mat 16:7–8 · Mar 2:6, 8; Luk 5:21–22; 6:8; 9:47 · Luk 20:14; Mat 21:25 · Luk 12:17 · 1Ti 2:8 ("without anger or quarreling"); Phili 2:14; Rom 14:1 · Luk 9:46 · Rom 1:21; 1Co 3:20 · Mar 7:21; Mat 15:19 · Jam 2:4 · Luk 2:35 | Inner reasoning becomes outward quarrel when it is shared and set on one's own standing (Luk 9:46; Rom 14:1) (R). The heart state decides honest or hardened (Luk 1:29 against Mar 8:17, S). In 1Ti 2:8 the quarrel word stands beside anger, a link to the anger strand

21280.text: Crying or weeping aloud is itself a purposeful act of the inner being: the voice is raised so as to be heard (by God, by others), and the verse names what it is for or what it brings (heard, answered, mercy asked, restraint overcome).

21282.text: Quiet gives a peaceable nature: a calm and gentle disposition of a spirit, a life, a house, or a people, named by another word.

21283.text: Quiet is the inner calm and stillness of a person or God: a chosen or given settledness, or its refusal, that the verse commands, praises, laments the lack of, or promises.

21290.text: Quietness is itself the settled inner rest and trust: the result of righteousness, the ground of strength, and better than toil and striving.

21294.text: Silence is a chosen holding back of speech by the person, in reverence, attention, waiting, grief or submission; the verse names the attitude it expresses, and so silence is the characteristic.

21296.text: Being silent is a person's, or God's, holding back of speech for a reason the verse shows: submission, fear, shame, awe, wisdom, obedience, waiting, or failure to speak up; or the refusal of it (anguish, praise, the watchmen's duty).

21301.text: Call is a purposeful act of the inner being turned to God: calling or crying out to the Lord, or on his name, in need, trust, praise or worship, or refusing to.

21304.text: Call is God's own act of summoning, choosing or appointing a person or people; it bears on their inner response (faith, obedience, hope), which other words of the verse name, and is the outward act upon them.

21308.text: Call is here the judgement a person puts on a thing in naming it (calling evil good, the Sabbath a delight, a fast acceptable): a valuing of the heart voiced in speech.

21311.text: Called here only names, designates or labels a person, place or thing (to be called such a name, to call it so); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21313.text: Called is here the outward act of summoning, addressing or sending for another person or thing; it bears on the other's response but names no inner-being operation of the one who calls.

21314.text: Called is the standing given by God's call (the vocation); it is what diligence, worthiness or walking is directed at, not an inner operation in itself.

21315.text: Called is God's own act of summoning, choosing or appointing a person or people; it bears on their inner response (faith, obedience, hope), which other words of the verse name, and is the outward act upon them.

21316.text: Called is here a public proclamation, summons or announcement to others; it is the outward act and bears on the hearers, with no inner-being operation of the caller named.

21319.text: Calling is the standing given by God's call (the vocation); it is what diligence, worthiness or walking is directed at, not an inner operation in itself.

21346.text: Deal is here the outward act of dealing with a person, with a disposition (kindness, loyalty, honesty, courage or good faith) named by another word of the verse; it bears on the one dealt with and names no inner operation of its own.

21351.text: Deal is here the outward act of dealing with a person in hatred, fury, violence or by what they deserve, named by another word of the verse; it bears on the one dealt with and names no inner operation of its own.

21356.text: Dealt is God's own act of dealing with a person or people according to what they are or have done, or according to his own faithfulness or love; it bears on them and is the outward act upon them.

21359.text: Offer here is the ritual or narrated presenting of an offering, a prescribed or reported act with no inner-being operation named by it.

21361.text: Offer is here an offering made to God in a stated inner condition (thanksgiving, joy, faith, fear, trust, willingness, resolve, cost, weeping, reverence or conscience), or refused for want of it; the act bears on that condition, which other words of the verse name.

21365.text: Offered here is the ritual or narrated presenting of an offering, a prescribed or reported act with no inner-being operation named by it.

21366.text: Offered is here an offering made to God in a stated inner condition (thanksgiving, joy, faith, fear, trust, willingness, resolve, cost, weeping, reverence or conscience), or refused for want of it; the act bears on that condition, which other words of the verse name.

21371.text: Offers here is the ritual or narrated presenting of an offering, a prescribed or reported act with no inner-being operation named by it.

21379.text: New here describes a thing, a time or a figure (a new garment, a new cart, fresh water, an old pool, a parable of wineskins); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21380.text: New is here something newly given by God or Christ (a covenant, commandment, name, way, city or world); it names what the person is brought into or receives, not an inner operation of its own.

21381.text: New gives newness to the self, the man, the creature or the lump: a changed condition of the person or community, set against what was put off or cleansed out.

21384.text: New gives freshness to a song of praise: the praise of the person is voiced afresh to the Lord.

21386.text: Old here states an age, an old age or an age class (years old, an old man, young and old, the older brother); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21390.text: Old here dates a thing to the past (of old, the days of old, from of old) or names the people or prophets of old; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21393.text: Old is here the former time (the days of old, the things of old) as what remembering, considering or comfort is directed at; the inner act is named by another word of the verse.

21394.text: Old gives long standing to a condition or a way: the ear never opened, or the way wicked men have trodden, since of old.

21407.text: Anger is here the anger, wrath or fury of God against persons or nations (kindled, poured out, turned away, executed, provoked); it is God's own act upon them, and bears on their inner response, which other words of the verse name, if at all.

21408.text: Anger is here the anger, wrath, rage or fury of a person or people: a state of the heart aroused against another, a thing or God, named by the word itself.

21410.text: Angry is here the anger, wrath, rage or fury of a person or people: a state of the heart aroused against another, a thing or God, named by the word itself.

21411.text: Angry is here the anger, wrath or fury of God against persons or nations (kindled, poured out, turned away, executed, provoked); it is God's own act upon them, and bears on their inner response, which other words of the verse name, if at all.

21412.text: Enraged is here the anger, wrath, rage or fury of a person or people: a state of the heart aroused against another, a thing or God, named by the word itself.

21420.text: Indignation is here the anger, wrath, rage or fury of a person or people: a state of the heart aroused against another, a thing or God, named by the word itself.

21424.text: Madness is here madness or derangement of the mind or heart: a state of the inner being, set against wisdom or sanity, or a craze such as a passion for idols.

21425.text: Rage is here the anger, wrath, rage or fury of a person or people: a state of the heart aroused against another, a thing or God, named by the word itself.

21434.text: Wrath is here the anger, wrath or fury of God against persons or nations (kindled, poured out, turned away, executed, provoked); it is God's own act upon them, and bears on their inner response, which other words of the verse name, if at all.
